author: chrislawcodes
body:
## What & why

Two changes to the animated replay viewer, designed for the **spectator**.

### Mobile: replay-first
On a phone the replay was buried **~622px down**, below the full standings table — the main event was below the fold. A scoped grid-order rule at `≤620px` puts the **stage first** with the standings rail **directly below it**, so the action is the first thing you see (now **~290px** down). The home hero deliberately keeps its own order.

### Talk in the ring center
The line a bot is saying now shows in the **empty center of the ring** instead of a fixed 104px strip below it: speaker name **in their own colour**, the line, and a faint **ghost of the previous line** so a quick exchange still reads as a back-and-forth.

The key constraint: the ring center is also the choreography lane (pacts meet there; gifts/bats walk across it). So the bubble shows **only during the talk phase and clears before any bot moves** — measured **zero frames** where the bubble and a mover overlap. Talk happens before the action, so there's a clean window.

Also: theme-aware (pulls from the same vars as every card), reduced-motion gets a no-slide version, and messages render via `textContent` so bot-authored text can't inject markup. Removed the now-dead rolling-log code and the `_marquee` computation that only fed the old pin.

## Verification (headless Chromium)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Bubble vs. movers | **0 overlap frames** (`talk talk talk - move move …`) |
| Mobile stage position | 622px → **~290px** (above the rail) |
| Dark palette | border + text hold |
| Reduced motion | bubble shows, no slide, no errors |
| Skip-talk / no-talk turn | no bubble; action plays clean |
| JS errors | none |

Known trade-offs: on the small mobile ring the bubble's edges sit over two *dimmed* side bots (reads as an intentional callout); couldn't seed a 16-bot ring offline but the ring radius — and thus the center hole — is bot-count-independent; the bubble's look/motion deserves a later game-art pass.

## Validation

Ran from repo root:

- `python3 -m ruff check .` → **pass**
- `mypy app/ mcp_server/` → **pass** (85 files)
- `pytest -q` → **pass** (315 passed)

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
Wires the two system-wide shortcuts (`globalHotkey` ⌘⇧G, `quickInput` ⌘⇧/) via Electron's [`globalShortcut`](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/global-shortcut) API and adds 6 missing [menu accelerators](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/keyboard-shortcuts#menu-shortcuts) that the Swift app had but the Electron app was missing. Both global shortcuts and menu accelerators re-register immediately when the user changes hotkey settings — no restart required.

**Why this is safe:** Existing menu accelerators for the 5 original commands are unchanged. New commands dispatch through the same `dispatchToFocused` pipeline as existing ones. The `VellumCommand` union is additive-only — renderer handlers for unrecognized kinds no-op by design (partial `Record` in `useVellumCommands`). The pre-existing missing `rePair` variant in `preload/index.ts` is also fixed.

**Architecture — two layers, matching [Electron's keyboard shortcut docs](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/keyboard-shortcuts):**
- `globalShortcut.register()` for 2 shortcuts that must work system-wide (app not focused)
- Menu accelerators for app-focused shortcuts (sidebar toggle, home, prev/next conversation, command palette, pop out)

**Alternatives rejected:**
- `globalShortcut` for ALL shortcuts — would steal keybinds from other apps system-wide
- Renderer-side `keydown` only — no menu integration, no visible shortcut hints, doesn't work when minimized
- Waiting for settings UI — wiring is independently valuable; settings UI layers on top

Closes LUM-1857

## Prompt / plan

Investigated LUM-1857, identified that the Electron app had zero `globalShortcut` usage and was missing 6 of the Swift app's shortcuts. Proposed two-layer architecture (global + menu accelerators), got approval, then implemented.

## Test plan

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes in both `apps/macos/` and `apps/web/`
- `bun run lint` passes in `apps/web/` (only pre-existing warnings)
- Pre-commit hooks (lint, typecheck, secrets scan) pass

author: arthurzengg
body:
## Summary

Closes #298.

`App.tsx` re-walked the full message list on every render — including every coalesced streaming frame:

- `groupTurns(state.messages)` ran inline in JSX (O(N) rebuild of the turn structure each render).
- `busy` / `activeProcessID` / `agentActivityMessageID` each scanned `state.messages` (`.some` / `.findLast`) on every render.

These inputs only change when `state.messages` changes, so the work was redundant during streaming.

### What changed

- Wrapped `groupTurns(state.messages)` in `useMemo` keyed on `state.messages` (which `MessageView`'s existing `memo` already relies on for stable identity).
- Wrapped the three derivations in one `useMemo` keyed on `[state.messages, state.busy, state.agentsStatus?.total]`.

`groupTurns` itself is untouched, so the dedicated `test/webview/group-turns.test.ts` continues to pin the grouping behavior. Memoization with correct deps cannot change rendered output — it only skips recomputation when the message array is referentially unchanged (the reducer produces a fresh array on every real change).

### Deferred (kept out to stay focused)

The plan's optional `PromptBox` / `StatusBar` filter memos were left out: those derivations feed into effects and only run while a menu is open (not the streaming hot path), so the risk/benefit didn't justify bundling them here.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run test` — full suite green (**961 tests, 63 files**), including `group-turns.test.ts`.
- [x] `cd webview && bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `bun run check-types` — clean (host untouched).
- [ ] Manual smoke (Extension Development Host): long conversation streams smoothly; turn grouping, per-turn sticky bubbles, review card, and agent-activity attribution render identically.

author: jaco-brink
body:
Closes [NES-1588](https://linear.app/jesus-film-project/issue/NES-1588/launch-privacy-notice-copy-on-chat-surface).

## What this does

Adds the user-facing data-disclosure surface that NES-1588 has been blocking the public chat launch on.

- **New page** at `/legal/about-chat` (`apps/journeys/pages/legal/about-chat.tsx`) that explains:
  - the chat is powered by an AI assistant
  - messages and replies are stored in a third-party analytics service (Langfuse) so the team can review conversations in aggregate
  - no name / email / account identifier is stored, conversations are not linked to identity
  - the only opt-out today is not using the chat
- **Inline link from `ChatHeader.tsx`** — appended to the existing subtitle:
  > Replies may not be perfect · **About this chat**
  
  Renders identically on mobile (PinnedChatBar) and desktop (ChatOverlay) because both share `ChatHeader`. Opens in a new tab so it never navigates the user away from the journey, including inside iframe embeds.

## Copy decisions worth knowing

- Surface microcopy intentionally avoids leading with "AI". The PRD already plans for the assistant to be honest when asked ("are you a bot?" → yes), so the surface doesn't need to confront the user with it before they've typed. *"Replies may not be perfect"* was already shipping; we only appended the link.
- Link label, page H1, and `<title>` are all *"About this chat"* — one canonical string, consistent across the click.
- No reference to the Cru privacy policy on the new page. The Cru policy doesn't disclose Langfuse chat-content storage, and folding it in would create the impression that it does. The page stands on its own.
- `whiteSpace: nowrap` on the link keeps *"About this chat"* tokenised so longer translations don't break mid-word. The surrounding `Typography` still wraps the whole subtitle to a second line when the combined string overflows — important for languages like German.

## Locale changes

- `libs/locales/en/apps-journeys.json` — 10 new English keys (page H1, `<title>`, three section headings, three body paragraphs, last-updated, back-link).
- `libs/locales/en/libs-journeys-ui.json` — one new key, `"About this chat"`, used by `ChatHeader`.
- Crowdin will pick up both on the next sync; no manual translation work in this PR.

## What I deliberately did NOT do

- No unit test for the page — `.claude/rules/frontend/apps.md` explicitly says don't unit-test copy strings.
- No edits to the Cru-linked footer in `pages/home/index.tsx` — out of scope.
- No new opt-out mechanism — page is honest that one doesn't exist yet.

## How to test on the Vercel preview

1. Open `<preview-host>/legal/about-chat` — verify the page renders with the Next Steps logo, sections, and back link.
2. Open any journey with `showAssistant = true` (or flip the LD flag) — verify the chat header subtitle reads *"Replies may not be perfect · About this chat"* and that clicking the link opens the page in a new tab.
3. Resize the chat to the mobile breakpoint and a narrow width to confirm the subtitle wraps gracefully (link wraps as a whole token to the next line if the combined string overflows).
4. Check in an in-app webview (Slack / Messenger / FB) — link should still open the page; iOS in-app webviews may render it in the same webview rather than a new tab, which is acceptable.

author: fivetran-davefowler
body:
## Summary

Adds `notes_on`, an optional Agents Schema provider under `examples/providers/notes_on` for teams that want a durable note layer on warehouse schemas, tables, and columns. It is useful as-is for agents, catalogs, review workflows, or analytics tooling that need object-scoped notes.

This is not a built-in/core provider and does not require everyone adopting Agents Schema to adopt this note shape. It does not change the core `agents-schema` CLI, core `ROOT_ENTRIES`, reusable workflows, package metadata, or the official `SPEC.md`.

The provider publishes durable object-scoped notes using provider-prefixed tables:

- `AGENTS.NOTES_ON_SCHEMATA`
- `AGENTS.NOTES_ON_TABLES`
- `AGENTS.NOTES_ON_COLUMNS`

It also upserts provider-authored `AGENTS.ROOT` rows at runtime. Those rows are deployment/provider metadata, not new core registry entries.

## Implementation

The package includes:

- a standalone `agents-schema-notes-on` CLI
- YAML source parsing and validation
- Snowflake publishing for the three `NOTES_ON_*` tables
- provider-owned `AGENTS.ROOT` upsert behavior
- sample YAML input
- standalone SQL snippets for tables, root rows, and context aggregations
- unit tests for parsing, validation, SQL binding, credentials, CLI errors, and publish flow

## Positioning

This reframes the old memory idea as an optional provider rather than a core Agents Schema feature. The shape is intentionally narrow: physical schema/table/column notes, no agent memory state, no write-back semantics, no polymorphic anchors, and no requirement that other providers or consumers adopt these opinions.

The useful distinction from database comments is still preserved: multiple authors, provenance, tags, confidence, importance, and history without overwriting a single canonical object comment.

## Context view compatibility

The provider id is `notes_on`, so the table names line up with the context-view naming scheme from #12. Since the source tables are one row per note, any `AGENTS.SCHEMATA`/`TABLES`/`COLUMNS` enrichment should aggregate to object grain before joining. The example uses a `notes_on_notes` VARIANT array rather than concatenated text so note boundaries and provenance are preserved.

## Verification

```text
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests
Ran 7 tests
OK

PYTHONPATH=examples/providers/notes_on/src uv run python -m unittest discover -s examples/providers/notes_on/tests
Ran 8 tests
OK

uv run python -m compileall -q src examples/providers/notes_on/src
git diff --check
clean
```

body:
Implements **Step 3.5a** (DESIGN.md §22, §24) — the deterministic, keyless real-data regression gate for **memory and actions**. The reference Vercel app + adapter tool-trace capture is 3.5b.

## What's in it
- **Harness** (`arango_memory/sim/`): `run_scenario` plays a multi-session agent loop *with interleaved tool calls* against the core's HTTP surface (`/v1/store` → async worker → `/v1/step` / `/v1/retrieve`) over a decoupled `HttpClient` Protocol (FastAPI `TestClient` satisfies it structurally). Stubbed models → reproducible. Scoring reuses the `eval` metrics.
- **Scenario** (`tests/data/sim_scenario.json`): a 3-session Patagonia-trip conversation with interleaved tool calls (`weather_lookup`, `product_search` ×2, `booking_create`) + cross-session QA.
- **CI gate** (`tests/test_sim.py`) asserts the four §22 categories:
  - **Recall** — cross-session, lite **and** full (≥ floor)
  - **Procedural** — 3 distinct steps, `product_search` `use_count`=2 (reuse across sessions), `TOUCHED`/`TRANSITION` edges
  - **Degradation** (§15) — simulated write failure → turn stays `queued`, retrieval degrades to memory-less (no 500)
  - **Isolation** — cross-tenant query returns nothing
- Moved the `api` TestClient fixture to `conftest.py` (shared by API + sim tests).

## Verification
`ruff` ✅ · `mypy --strict` (29 files) ✅ · **67 tests** (5 sim + the prior 62). Runs in the existing `make ci` — deterministic + keyless, exercising the real async write path end-to-end.

## Notes
- **Placement deviation**: the harness lives at `arango_memory/sim/` (mirroring `eval/`), not a standalone root `sim/` (§3), to reuse the testcontainers fixtures.
- A *true* lite-vs-full quality delta still needs a real model → **3.5b**.

author: florianpaumier
body:
## Problem
`php bin/console assets:install` reports `No assets were provided by any bundle` even though `src/Resources/public/` exists with CSS and JS files.

## Root Cause
`AbstractBundle::getPath()` returns the `composer.json` directory (project root), not `src/`. Symfony's `assets:install` command looks for `Resources/public/` relative to `getPath()`, which would be `<root>/Resources/public/`. But files were at `<root>/src/Resources/public/` — invisible to the command.

## Fix
- Move `src/Resources/public/` → `Resources/public/` (project root)
- Update `package.json` build output paths to match
- Update Flex recipe `copy-from-package` path

## Verification
- `src/Resources/skeleton/` preserved (separate from `public/`)

## 요약

오디오 플레이어의 재생 버튼과 진행바 포인터(thumb) 색상을 색상 스킴을 추종하던 `--theme` 에서 테마 중립 색 `--accent`(고정 중립 차콜)로 교체했습니다.

## 변경 내용

`css/style.css` 의 다음 속성에서 `--theme` → `--accent`:

- `.audio-play-btn` 배경 (재생/일시정지 버튼)
- `.audio-progress` 진행바 채움 그래디언트
- `.audio-progress::-webkit-slider-thumb` 및 `::-moz-range-thumb` 배경
- thumb 포커스/호버 링 (`color-mix` 알파)

재생 버튼 아이콘은 그대로 `--bg` 라 차콜(라이트)·밝은 회색(다크) 배경 양쪽에서 대비를 유지합니다.

## 영향

테마색(`--theme`, 색상 스킴 추종) 적용 범위가 **절 번호·단락 기호·FAB·오디오 플레이어 4곳 → 절 번호·단락 기호·FAB 3곳**으로 좁혀졌습니다. 오디오 바는 하단 chrome 표면(frosted glass)에 얹히는 컨트롤이라 스킴 시그니처보다 chrome 톤 일관성이 자연스럽다는 판단입니다.

## 문서

- `docs/decisions/028-design-system.md` §6 — 개정 블록 추가 (2026-06-05)
- `DESIGN.md` §2 — 토큰 표·스킴 범위·규약 갱신
- `CLAUDE.md` 현재 상태 절 갱신

CSS 전용 변경으로 JS 유닛 테스트에 영향이 없습니다.

https://claude.ai/code/session_011HHQvZTeafayiLUJLLfaKJ

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_011HHQvZTeafayiLUJLLfaKJ)_

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CSS·문서만 변경되며 런타임 로직·데이터·인증에 영향이 없고, 시각 토큰 정렬 수준의 저위험 변경입니다.
> 
> **Overview**
> 오디오 미니 플레이어(재생 버튼, 진행바 채움·thumb·호버 링, 재생 속도 버튼)의 강조색을 색상 스킴을 따르던 **`--theme`에서 고정 chrome 색 `--accent`로 바꿉니다.** 하단 frosted-glass 바 위 컨트롤이 탭·설정 등과 같은 중립 톤으로 맞춰지고, 스킴을 바꿔도 플레이어는 더 이상 빨강/초록/보라로 물들지 않습니다.
> 
> **`--theme` 적용 범위 문서를 정리합니다.** 읽기 본문은 **절 번호·단락 기호**만 스킴 추종으로 명시하고, 이미 제거된 검색 FAB는 ADR-030 기준으로 빼며, 모핑 탭바의 접힌 홈 아이콘 `--theme` 틴트는 ADR-030 내비 결정으로 별도 기술합니다. `css/style.css` 주석, `DESIGN.md` §2·§7·부록, `docs/decisions/028-design-system.md` §6(2026-06-05 개정), `CLAUDE.md` 현재 상태를 같은 내용으로 맞춥니다.
> 
> **동작·JS 변경 없음** — CSS와 ADR/디자인 문서만 갱신합니다.

author: littlepoolshark
body:
## Bug Description

Session resume crashes with `rich.errors.MarkupError: closing tag [/] at position 30 has nothing to close` because ANSI escape codes and Rich markup tags are mixed incorrectly.

Fixes #39469

## Root Cause

`_DIM` is an ANSI escape code (`\x1b[2;3m`), not a Rich markup tag. But `_restore_session_cwd()` wraps it in Rich-style brackets and closes with `[/]`:

```python
self._console_print(f"[{_DIM}]{_escape(msg)}[/]")
```

Rich parses `[/]` as a close tag, but since no Rich tag was opened (the `[` was followed by ANSI ESC, not a valid tag character), it raises `MarkupError`.

## Fix

Replace the 3 occurrences in `_restore_session_cwd()` (lines 5381, 5391, 5401) with the pure ANSI pattern used everywhere else in the codebase:

```python
# Before:
self._console_print(f"[{_DIM}]{_escape(msg)}[/]")

# After:
self._console_print(f"{_DIM}{_escape(msg)}{_RST}")
```

`_RST = "\033[0m"` (ANSI reset) is already defined at line 1601. This pattern `{_DIM}...{_RST}` is the standard ANSI-only convention used throughout `cli.py`.

## How to Verify

1. Start a Hermes session from a directory
2. Exit
3. Resume from a different working directory: `hermes chat -r <session_id>`
4. Confirm the session resumes cleanly with the working directory message displayed in dim style

## Test Plan

- [ ] The fix is a 3-line ANSI-only change identical to every other `_DIM` usage in `cli.py`
- [ ] Manual verification of session resume flow
- [ ] No new dependencies or imports needed

## Risk Assessment

**Low** — The change replaces a broken pattern with the same ANSI-only pattern used in hundreds of other places in the codebase. No logic change, only string formatting.

author: castrojo
body:
## Root cause

The Fedora-minimal base image has no `USER` directive, so `os.geteuid()` returns 0 inside the container.  `qecore-headless` detects this and calls `exit_headless_or_propagate_error(sys.exit(1))` — silently terminating before any test scenario runs:

```
headless: Script is not meant to be run under the root user.
headless: Exiting the headless script.
```

## Why the existing patch didn't fully fix it

The RUN block already has **Patch 1** that removes `recoverable=False` from every `print_fail` call. This makes the _message_ non-fatal, but `exit_headless_or_propagate_error(propagate_to_sandbox=False)` is called **on the very next line** — and that always calls `sys.exit(1)` when not propagating to sandbox.

## Fix

Add **Patch 3** to short-circuit the entire `elif` branch:

```python
elif os.geteuid() == 0 and not self.no_automatic_login:
# becomes
elif False:  # patched: container runs as root but is isolated inside QEMU/GHA
```

This causes qecore-headless to skip the root check entirely. All other isolation concerns (dconf, sandbox.py headless_errors, ponytail) are already handled by existing patches in the Containerfile.

## Impact

Fixes **every e2e nightly failure since 2026-06-02** (the `PR #204` runner-container regression). Merging this triggers `build-runner.yml` to rebuild `ghcr.io/projectbluefin/testsuite:runner` automatically.

## Testing

After merge + image rebuild, trigger the nightly or manual e2e run against any image.

author: androm3da
body:
Add missing k_spin_unlock() calls on error return paths in gpio_altera_configure() and gpio_altera_pin_interrupt_configure(). Both functions returned -EINVAL in their default/else branches while still holding the spinlock acquired earlier.


[Clang Thread Safety Analysis](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ThreadSafetyAnalysis.html) yielded some cases where locks were incorrectly leaked.

See also #106847

author: skynavga
body:
## Summary

Phase 11.Y closes the deferral pinned by the 10.final.pre-1 `verbs.yaml` comment block on the curse-VERB `mura` entry ("v_iter_redup intentionally NOT opted-in ... Can be added later under audit-corpus attestation pressure"). The 2026-06-04 informant / reviewer pass confirmed `mura-mura` from the curse-VERB is common, productive ITER/HABITUAL reduplication parallel to `iyak-iyak` / `tawa-tawa`. The surface-collision with the ADJ `adj_redup` `mura-mura` "rather cheap" is now intentional — both readings co-exist, disambiguated by lemma / REDUP_SEM / AV_ABSOL.

Non-FU carry-forward (formerly `tgllfg-out-of-scope.md` §18.1.4 line 70; rescheduled 2026-06-04 as a named Phase 11 sub-PR; attestation landed same day).

## Lex change

Single-line `data/tgl/verbs.yaml` change on the curse-VERB `mura` entry:

```
- affix_class: [mag, in_oblig, pag_gerund]
+ affix_class: [mag, in_oblig, pag_gerund, v_iter_redup]
```

The 10.final.pre-1 "intentionally NOT opted-in" comment block above the entry flips to a SHIPPED design note documenting the 2026-06-04 informant attestation, the surface-collision disambiguation strategy, and the cross-reference to `project_mura_mura_attestation` memory.

## What now parses

- `Mura-mura siya.` "He keeps cursing" — bare predicative VERB-iter via the 10.E.3 `v_iter_redup` VERB→ADJ POS-flip → predicative-ADJ rule (REDUP_SEM=ITER on the matrix). Parallels canonical `Iyak-iyak siya.` / `Tawa-tawa siya.`
- `Mura-mura ang lalaki.` "The man keeps cursing" — same shape with full-NP SUBJ.
- `Puro mura-mura ang lumabas sa bibig niya.` "Nothing but curses came out of his mouth" — one of the 2 redup-form attested exemplars from the 2026-06-04 informant pass. Parses via the predicative-ADJ rule embedded in the `puro X ang Y` construction.

## Cross-POS coexistence at `muramura`

Post-11.Y, the morph analyzer produces TWO ADJ entries at the `muramura` surface:

- `lemma='mura'`, `REDUP=FULL`, no `REDUP_SEM`, no `AV_ABSOL` — the pre-existing ADJ-derived (`adj_redup`) scalar-moderate "rather cheap" reading.
- `lemma='mura-mura'`, `REDUP=FULL`, `REDUP_SEM=ITER`, `AV_ABSOL=True`, `PREDICATIVE=True` — the new VERB-iter-derived "cursing-iteratively" reading.

Both are valid; downstream consumers disambiguate by lemma / REDUP_SEM / AV_ABSOL.

## Test coverage

New file `tests/tgllfg/test_phase11_y_mura_curse_iter.py` (9 tests across 4 classes):

- `TestMuramuraCrossPOSSentry` (3): both lemma paths present; ADJ-derived REDUP_SEM=None preserved; VERB-iter-derived REDUP_SEM=ITER + AV_ABSOL + PREDICATIVE.
- `TestMuramuraVerbIterPredicative` (2): bare predicative parses with both PRON and full-NP SUBJ.
- `TestMuramuraInformantExemplar` (1): the `puro X ang Y` exemplar parses.
- `TestMuramuraScopePreserved` (3): the 10.E.1 ang-exclamative preserves REDUP_SEM=INTENS; the bare scalar ADJ `Mura ang bahay.` still parses; the inflected curse-VERB `Nagmura siya.` still parses.

Existing `tests/tgllfg/test_phase10_h_post1_mura_adj_correction.py`:

- `test_mura_redup_is_full_underspecified` narrowed to filter by `lemma='mura'` (the ADJ-derived entry) — the new VERB-iter entry has `lemma='mura-mura'` and is verified separately in the 11.Y file.
- `test_curse_verb_shipped_under_10_final_pre_1` docstring updated to note the 11.Y change (the "bare-redup `muramura` stays ADJ-only" claim is no longer true; both readings co-exist).

## Audit-corpus impact

3 new unattributed-corpus exemplars under `unattributed/mura-mura-curse-iter` (161 → 164):

- `bare-pred-pron-subj`: `Mura-mura siya.`
- `bare-pred-full-np-subj`: `Mura-mura ang lalaki.`
- `puro-x-ang-lumabas`: `Puro mura-mura ang lumabas sa bibig niya.`

Wave-1 audit unchanged (122/123 closed pre→post). Other waves: existing `Mura...` surfaces across waves 2-5 are all the ADJ "cheap" sense (no `mura-mura` curse-iter attestations in extracted corpora), so 11.Y's only audit impact is the 3 new unattributed exemplars.

## Out of 11.Y scope (flagged for future)

- **NP-head possessor exemplar** (`Narinig ko ang mura-mura niya habang nag-aayos ng makina.` "I heard him muttering curses while fixing the engine") — requires nominalized-ITER-in-NP-head support (predicative-ADJ → nominal-head coercion or separate nominal-redup cell). Different construction-class problem.
- **X-nang-X intensive-repetition construction** (`Mura nang mura siya sa referee.` "He kept cursing at the referee") — separate construction entirely (not a redup form).

Both are pre-existing chart gaps, not regressions from 11.Y. Flagged in the test file docstring + `project_mura_mura_attestation` memory.

## Audit doc cleanup bundled into commit 2

Per user direction 2026-06-04 ("we can roll [the small audit-doc edit] into the upcoming 11.Y branch"), commit 2 bundles a small docs cleanup that was uncommitted in the working tree from after the 11.X PR-crank:

- `docs/fu-extension-audit.md` §3 backlog table: "11.B.3 ... SHIPPED — PR pending" → "PR #208"; "11.X ... SHIPPED — PR pending" → "PR #211".
- §3.5 bare-Huwag entry: "(PR pending)" → "(PR #211, ae2a53d)".

Plus §3.5 v_iter_redup entry flipped from "Stays audit-attestation-gated" to "SHIPPED 2026-06-04 by Phase 11.Y" with full shipping outcome.

## Reference

- Informant attestation memory: `project_mura_mura_attestation` (2026-06-04 reviewer pass: two distinct lexemes; productive ITER parallel to iyak-iyak/tawa-tawa).
- Original deferral: 10.final.pre-1 `verbs.yaml:1808-1811` comment block.
- `v_iter_redup` cell origin: Phase 10.E.3 (PR #132).
- 10.H.post-1 ADJ-redup REDUP_SEM=None scalar-moderate analysis: preserved unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `hatch run test-both` — 10162 passed in 175.67s (was 10147 pre-11.Y; +15, 0 regressions).
- [x] `hatch run check` — 437 source files, clean.
- [x] Wave-1 audit re-parse — 122/123 closed, no change vs pre-11.Y.
- [x] Manual probe — both `Mura-mura siya.` (new VERB-iter) and `Ang mura-mura ng bahay!` (existing 10.E.1 INTENS) parse with the expected REDUP_SEM readings.

## 목적
운영 무료/유료 진단(`/free-diagnosis`)에서 사용자가 입력한 값이 UI→API→DTO→DB→ENGINE 전 구간에서 살아남도록 입력 전달 경로를 복구합니다. 엔진 로직·Rule·법해석은 변경하지 않습니다(배선만).

## 변경 파일
1. `services/diagnosis_nexas_adapter.py` — `DiagnosisRunBody.form_data`에 원본 form_data 보존 (기존엔 pop 후 소실)
2. `services/diagnosis_integrated_svc.py`
   - `run_diagnosis`: `_merge_form_data_into_inp()`로 form_data를 step1 `input`(inp)에 합류 → `legal_context._input_to_facility_context`가 읽는 키(has_*, electric_capacity, gas/boiler 용량, floor_count 등)가 엔진까지 도달
   - BUILDING `floor_count`: 하드코딩 `5` → 사용자 입력값 사용
   - `anonymous_diagnosis_results.input_data`에 `form_data` 보존 (DB 저장 누락 복구)
   - `upgrade_diagnosis`: 재실행 시 저장된 form_data 복원

## 남은 항목 (이 PR 범위 밖 — 엔진 키 매핑 필요, GPT 담당)
`legal_context` ctx가 키 이름을 다르게 읽거나 아직 읽지 않는 항목은 inp까지는 도달하나 조건매칭엔 미반영:

body:
## Resumo

Implementa os 4 itens de follow-up do filtro grep-like do drill-down (`PodWatchView`/`LiveSessionView`) que ficaram fora do V1 de #460.

### Item D — Regex-timeout
- Adiciona `regex>=2024.0` às dependências
- Termos `r:` usam `regex.compile`/`.search(timeout=0.1s)` em vez de `re`
- `regex.TimeoutError` → filtro no-op + toast; graceful fallback para `re` quando o pacote não está instalado

### Item C — Multi-filtro AND/OR
- Gramática fechada: `term ( SEP term )*` com `SEP = " AND " | " OR "`
- Operador único por expressão; mistura → no-op + toast
- `quoted_term` (`"a AND b"`) para citar separadores literais
- Per-termo `r:` com compilação individual; falha → no-op + toast com índice do termo
- Limite de 200 chars aplicado à expressão inteira

### Item A — Highlight visual
- `_build_highlighted_body` constrói `Text` com spans `reverse` para cada segmento matched
- Termos literais: busca por `str.find` em laço (sem regex)
- Termos `r:`: `regex.finditer(timeout=)` — reutiliza a lib de D, evita reabrir DoS
- `regex.TimeoutError` no highlight → linha renderizada sem spans (texto cru)
- Realça **todos** os termos de expressão multi-termo

### Item B — Persistência
- `~/.deile/panel_filters.json` (schema v1, escrita atômica, read-merge-write)
- Cap de 50 entradas (LRU); TTL de 30 dias
- `PodWatchView.on_unmount` salva; `on_mount` restaura via chave `pod:{ns}/{pod_name}`
- `LiveSessionView` ganha `on_unmount` + restore via chave `session:{task_id}`

### Testes
- Novo `deile/tests/infra/test_panel_filter_followups.py` — 31 pass + 3 skip (timeouts requerem `regex` instalado, que será disponível em CI via `pyproject.toml`)
- `test_panel_pod_watch_filter.py` atualizado para comportamento V2 (invalid regex → no-op, AC-C4)
- 50 testes passam localmente

Closes #544

author: antmikinka
body:
## Summary

Fix `[scatter] Axes don't match array dimensions` error that occurs during text generation when `repetition_penalty != 1.0`.

## Root Cause

MLX C++ `scatter()` has two issues:
1. Does not normalize negative axis values (`-1` is rejected by host-side validation)
2. Strict shape constraint: `updates.ndim == src.ndim + indices.ndim` — incompatible with the `take_along_axis` pattern

## Fix

Replace `scatter()` with `put_along_axis()`, which is the mirror of `take_along_axis()` and handles negative axis normalization internally. Uses the same `shaped_indices`, keeping the take→modify→put-back pattern clean.

## Tests

Added 3 test cases that exercise the scatter path with non-trivial repetition penalties (previous tests all hit early returns with `penalty == 1.0f`).

- **Bug 1:** ODOO_SRC detection uses `maxdepth 4`, but Doodba layout needs depth 5 → now detects `odoo/custom/src/odoo/setup.py`
- **Bug 2:** Docker tag version mismatch (`16.0` stripped to `16`) → now uses full version for tag construction
- **Bug 3:** `requirements.txt` inline comments break pip install → now preprocesses to strip comments
- **Bug 4:** Silent failures propagate through setup steps → now validates all required variables before proceeding

## Changes

- Increased ODOO_SRC find maxdepth from 4 to 5 with validation gate
- Split ODOO_VERSION into ODOO_VERSION_FULL + ODOO_VERSION for proper Docker tag construction
- Added requirements.txt preprocessing pipe to strip inline comments
- Added Step 7 validation block in Prerequisites to catch missing environment variables

All fixes are generic and documentation-only (no code changes required).

Closes #5

### Motivation

- Provide a fast, responsive, conversion-focused static landing page for the Seeto Realty Agent Referral Program that can be hosted on GitHub Pages without a build step.
- Enable secure referral submissions with a configurable client-side endpoint and a mailto fallback for GitHub Pages hosting limitations.

- Added the static site assets: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `script.js`, and `config.js` to implement the landing page, UI, client-side form handling, Calendly links, and mailto fallback.

body:
## What

The slide-type picker (Plan step) now **greys out any slide type the AI found no source content for**:

| Slide type | Locked when… |
|---|---|
| **Testimony** | the article has no attributed quote |
| **Stat** | the report has no figure to feature |
| **Multi-stat** | the report has fewer than 3 figures |
| **Key fact** | the report has no clear fact |

Structural / DR-voice slides — **Response, Tiers, Before/After, CTA** — stay available, because they draw from editable defaults and Deen Relief's own messaging, not from the report.

## Why it's honest (and £0)

The extractor is already instructed to **never fabricate** — *"If raw_payload contains no attributed quote, return an EMPTY quotes array… a zero-quote output is correct and required."* So the absence of a quote/fact/stat card is a **real** signal, not a guess. No extra AI call — the gate just reads what was already extracted.

## How

- New `roleHasContent(role, content)` + `roleLockReason(role)` in `slideRoles.ts` — the **single source of truth**.
- `suggestPlan` now uses it, so the auto-suggested plan never seeds a role that would appear locked.
- `PlanStep` disables the locked buttons (lock icon + tooltip), greys them, and shows a one-line hint explaining why.
- A slide's **own current selection is never locked out from under her** (defensive: `!available && !on`).

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `npm run build` clean (exit 0)

author: weksler
body:
## Problem

The Woodpecker queue-backup desync bug (present on 3.14.x and 3.15.x) has jammed CI **three times** (twice on 2026-05-30, again 2026-06-04). When a pipeline is superseded/cancelled (Dependabot bursts, force-pushes), rows linger in the `tasks` queue table whose backing `workflows` row has already reached a terminal state. The server then tight-loops:

```
queue: resubmitting expired task <id>
pull queue item: <id>: failed to remove from backup: sql: no rows in result set
caught agent performing illegal instruction: workflow was already marked as finished
```

…saturating every agent worker slot with phantom tasks, so new pipelines never get scheduled. User-visible symptom: **"CI not starting pipelines"** (it is — the slots are just starved). The latest incident showed 71 phantom task rows starving all 7 workers. Clearing it requires a server restart (to flush the in-memory queue), not just a DB delete — which is why manual recovery has been the only fix so far.

## Fix

A guarded self-healing cron on the CI host (`*/5`, under `flock`), deployed via `ci/ansible/`:

- **Acts ONLY on the bug's exact fingerprint** — a dual-signal guard requiring BOTH a sustained `resubmitting expired task` server-journal loop (≥20 in 10 min) AND live zombie task rows (≥5). Healthy operation produces zero of either, so it's a silent no-op. The dual guard also prevents post-recovery oscillation (stale journal lines linger after a restart, but zombies drop to 0).
- **Validated recovery**: stop agent+server → back up the SQLite DB → surgically delete only zombie rows → restart server then agent → prune to newest 5 backups.
- **Fail-safe delete**: a task is a zombie only when its backing workflow is in a known *terminal* state (`success/failure/killed/canceled/error/declined/skipped`) or is missing. Any non-terminal or unrecognised state (`pending/running/created/blocked/`future) is **preserved**. Empirically validated against a live DB copy: `blocked`/`created` tasks preserved, terminal-backed + orphan tasks deleted, in-flight pipeline tasks untouched.
- **Hardening**: self-heal a unit left `failed` by a botched restart; resilient dual-start so the single-VM host is never left half-down; `umask 077` + `chmod 600` on DB backups (full copies of `woodpecker.sqlite`, which holds CI secrets).

Already front-installed on the CI box (with the exact `#Ansible:` cron marker, so the next provision is idempotent) to restore protection immediately; this PR makes it durable.

> Follow-up (not in this PR): reduce supersede pressure (stagger Dependabot / cap concurrent PR pipelines / consider disabling auto-cancel) and file the desync bug upstream — 3 recurrences qualifies as "frequent."

## OSS Compliance Review

**VERDICT: CLEAN** (CRITICAL: 0 | HIGH: 0 | MEDIUM: 0 | LOW: 0). No real tenant domains, personal info, hardcoded credentials, private registry references, or internal IPs/hostnames. All identifiers (systemd unit names, `/var/lib/woodpecker/` paths, the `template`+`cron` task pattern) already exist in the public repo at HEAD; the script is a generic recovery tool for a public upstream bug.

## Security Review

Initial review found **1 HIGH + 2 MEDIUM**, all fixed and re-verified clean (final: CRITICAL: 0 | HIGH: 0 | MEDIUM: 0 | LOW: 0):

- **HIGH (fixed)** — DELETE predicate was a fragile *preserve-denylist* that omitted the valid non-terminal states `blocked`/`created` and included a non-existent `started`, risking deletion of legitimate dependency-gated queued work during a jam. Inverted to an explicit *terminal-or-missing delete allowlist* so any unknown/future state fails **safe** (preserved). Re-verified against synthetic states including an unknown future state.
- **MEDIUM (fixed)** — restart-failure availability gap: added top-of-run self-heal of `failed` units (won't fight a deliberate `inactive` stop) + resilient dual-start in the recovery path.
- **MEDIUM (fixed)** — DB backups could be world-readable: added `umask 077` + explicit `chmod 600`.

Verified clean: correct `tasks.id`↔`workflows.id` join (confirmed against Woodpecker source), stop-before-delete quiescing (no TOCTOU), no shell/SQL injection (no untrusted input; SQL is a fixed predicate), `flock`-serialised, mode `0700` root, no secret exposure.

author: sethogieva
body:
**Real root cause of 'Couldn't reach Stripe'** (my Sub-A4 cold-start theory was wrong; reverted that band-aid).

Live edge-function logs showed `brand-stripe-refresh-status` (and `brand-stripe-balances`) returning **401 on every call**, ~150ms each — i.e. the function *ran* and its own `auth.getUser(token)` rejected the token (a gateway/cold-start reject would be ~10ms).

The client passed `useAuth()`'s `session.access_token` as a **custom `Authorization` header**, overriding `supabase.functions.invoke`'s default. That React session snapshot **lags the Supabase client's silently-refreshed token**, so a stale/expired token reached the edge fn → 401. (`startBrandStripeOnboarding`, which passes no custom header, never 401'd — that's the working pattern.) 'Try again worked' only because the snapshot had refreshed by then.

**Fix:** drop the custom header in both services so invoke uses the client's current auto-refreshed token. Revert Sub-A4's retry:4 (pointless against a 401). 4 files + 1 test updated ([TEST-MOD-APPROVED]). Client-only — no edge fn/migration. eslint clean, balances suite 3/3.

body:
## What

Records and justifies the decision to run the container as the host UID/GID, and documents the mounted surface — so the call isn't silently re-litigated. **Decision: keep UID-matching.** Docs only; no mechanism change.

## Changes

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — new top-level subsection "Why the container runs as the host UID" (the existing "Container user" table row already covers the mechanism; this captures the *why*):
  - **Rationale:** bind-mounted `Repositories` files land owned by the host user — no `sudo`, no ACL drift; simplest correct ownership model for a bind-mount dev container that edits your real repos in place.
  - **Trade-off:** a container escape acts as your UID over the *mounted surface only* — it does not grant root; Docker namespace isolation and SSH-agent socket forwarding (no private keys in the container) still hold.
  - **Mounted surface enumerated:** projects dir (`PROJECTS_DIR`), repo-local `./.claude/` + `./.claude.json`, repo-local gh config dir, worktrunk config, read-only `~/.gitconfig`, forwarded SSH agent socket — nothing else.
  - **Alternatives considered & rejected:** POSIX ACLs (`setfacl`, fragile/abandoned); rootless Docker / userns-remap (remaps ownership through subuid, reintroduces the mismatch pain); Podman `--userns=keep-id` (functionally equivalent, viable future port, not a security improvement); named-volume-only (defeats the purpose).
- **`docs/host-setup.md`** — lightly expand §9 (security trade-off) to note userns-remap's ownership cost and cross-reference the new CLAUDE.md section.

Closes #27

author: tillahoffmann
body:
## Summary
Adds MLX patch `10-layernorm-vjp-bias-war-hazard.patch`, fixing an intermittent **wrong bias gradient** from `fast::layer_norm` on the Metal GPU.

## Root cause
`LayerNormVJP::eval_gpu` (`mlx/backend/metal/normalization.cpp`) reduces the cotangent `g` into the bias gradient `gb`, then dispatches the vjp kernel — which overwrites `g`'s buffer **in place** when the cotangent is donated (`gx`/`gw_temp` alias `g`). The `gb` reduction reads `g` while the kernel writes it: a **write-after-read hazard**. MLX's Metal `CommandEncoder` only auto-inserts barriers for *read-after-write*, so the two dispatches race and `gb` is intermittently wrong (~5–15% of evaluations, off by ~100%). The input and weight gradients are unaffected. The patch adds an explicit `compute_encoder.barrier()` after the `gb` reduction.

## Why it started failing recently
This is a **latent MLX bug** — it reproduces in pure eager MLX on both v0.31.0 and `main`. jax-mps exercised this path for ~6 weeks on jax 0.9 with green CI; it only began manifesting after the **jax 0.10 bump (#144)**, whose buffer donation newly satisfies the hazard's precondition. So this is environment drift exposing an old bug, not a regression here.

## Verification
- Standalone MRE: **108/2000 wrong → 0/3000** with the patch.
- Through the plugin: layer-norm grad tests pass; `d/db` 0/2000.
- Patch applies cleanly to vanilla v0.31.2 and coexists with the existing patches.

Upstream repro (to be filed with ml-explore/mlx): https://gist.github.com/tillahoffmann/0ce6b748d7249da10962e4aad4155bcd

## Not covered
Other intermittent numpyro grad failures (e.g. `Gamma`, `NegativeBinomial2`) are **separate** latent MLX kernel bugs similarly exposed by jax 0.10. They are not addressed here, so CI may still fail intermittently on those until they're fixed.

author: charlie-yang-gogox
body:
## Problem

Step 1.3's clean check `[ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]` aborts the whole batch on **any** porcelain output — including untracked files.

That's stricter than the check's purpose. The clean-tree gate exists to avoid automating over a human's in-progress work — and the signal for that is **tracked modifications**. Untracked files can't be touched by dispatch at all: the dispatcher never edits the main worktree, and every spawned pipeline works in its own `../<TICKET>` worktree.

**Real-world cost**: the 2026-06-05 06:00 scheduled fire aborted (0 dispatched, one ready-to-dev ticket left waiting) because of `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` — a short-lived Claude-harness runtime lock that was auto-deleted minutes after the fire. A whole slot wasted on a file no pipeline would ever touch.

## Fix

```bash
# Block: tracked changes (staged or unstaged) = human's in-progress work
[ -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ] || abort ...
# Warn + proceed: untracked files
note: N untracked file(s) present — proceeding (agents work in separate worktrees)
```

The default-branch check and `--test` skip behavior are unchanged.

author: 0xgleb
body:
## Motivation

ADR-0001 (`adrs/0001-jobs-replace-services.md`) replaces cqrs-es Services with
durable, retryable jobs. Command handlers stay pure
`(state, command) -> Vec<Event>` and enqueue side effects as jobs that flush
inside the same SQLite transaction that commits the triggering events — so a job
is enqueued iff its events commit, closing the crash window between a side effect
and the event meant to record it.

This is the base of the jobs implementation stack: the `Job` trait everything
else builds on.

## Solution

- Add the `Job` trait to `event-sorcery`: a durable, retryable unit of
  side-effecting work, with associated `Input` (consumer-owned dependency
  bundle), `Output`, and `Error` types; `WORKER_NAME`/`KIND` consts; a
  `TERMINAL_FAILURE_MSG`; a `label()` for structured logging; and an async
  `perform(&self, &Input)`.
- Add the `Label` newtype for human-readable job identifiers used in logs and
  failure-injection targeting; unit-tested via the `SendEmail` example job.
- Re-export `Job` and `Label` from the crate root.
- Add apalis (`apalis`, `apalis-sqlite`, `apalis-core`, `apalis-codec`) as the
  queue backend; the `Cargo.lock` churn is the resolution of those and their
  sqlx 0.8 sub-tree.

Bottom of the jobs stack (onto `adr/associated-job`); #12-#16 stack the worker,
buffered enqueue, `EventSourced` reshape, and example/doc migration on top.

author: ilyin-ilya
body:
## Problem

A race between the resync task and \`stop()\` in the destructor produced an on-disk state of \`DEVB + clean_unmount=1 + empty superbitmap\`. On second mount the degraded-clean invariant check threw \`std::runtime_error\`, making the volume permanently unassemblable. This caused the nublox \`resiliency-2-0-dense\` test failure tracked in issue #300.

**Root cause sequence:**
1. Array goes degraded. Route = DEVB. \`_sb->superbitmap_reserved\` has dirty bits set.
2. Health is restored; resync task launches and calls \`clean_region\` for each completed chunk, progressively zeroing \`_sb->superbitmap_reserved\`.
3. Resync calls \`__yield()\` (per-iteration sleep). At that moment \`stop()\` (from the destructor) CASes state → STOPPING. \`__yield()\` returns STOPPING → \`__run()\` returns STOPPING → the \`while(true)\` breaks **without reaching \`__become_clean\`**.
4. Destructor: \`sync_to\` sees an empty superbitmap → writes nothing. \`write_superblock\` copies \`_sb\` with zeros → writes \`DEVB + clean_unmount=1 + empty superbitmap\` to disk.
5. Second mount: \`route=DEVB, clean_unmount=1, superbitmap=zeros\` → invariant fires → throw → volume refuses to assemble.

## Fix

**Fix 1 — resync task** (\`_start()\` in \`raid1_resync_task.cpp\`):

Capture \`pages_before = dirty_pages()\` before each \`__run()\` call. When STOPPING fires, if \`pages_before > 0 && dirty_pages() == 0\` the resync cleared every dirty chunk during \`__run()\` but was interrupted in \`__yield()\` before \`complete()\` committed route→EITHER. Call \`complete()\` immediately so the destructor sees route=EITHER rather than leaving DEVA/DEVB + empty-superbitmap on disk. The \`pages_before > 0\` guard prevents a spurious \`complete()\` call for the Fix 2 recovery path (where \`dirty_region + load_from\` produces an empty bitmap with \`pages_before == 0\`). Calling \`complete()\` while \`stop()\` holds \`_launch_lock\` and waits at \`join()\` is safe — no I/O arrives during destruction, so \`dirty_region()\` cannot fire under \`_clean_transition_mutex\`, making \`complete()\` returning false impossible here.

**Fix 2 — mount invariant** (\`__init_bitmap_and_degraded_route\` in \`raid1.cpp\`):

Replace the throw with \`RLOGW + dirty_region(0, capacity())\`. The \`load_from\` call that follows reads the bitmap page from the active device; if it returns zeros (as the race-state disk would), \`isal_zero_detect\` clears the superbitmap bit — leaving the array in degraded mode for a clean transition on the next healthy shutdown. Defense-in-depth for any state not covered by Fix 1.

## Test

\`DegradedCleanEmptySuperbitmap\` in \`src/raid/raid1/tests/superblock/init_issues.cpp\` covers **Fix 2**:

- \`StrictMock<TestDisk>\` pair, 1 GiB each (→ exactly 1 bitmap page)
- \`disk_b\` carries the exact race-state SB: \`DEVB\`, \`age=1\` (wins \`pick_superblock\`), \`clean=1\`, empty superbitmap
- Constructor: Fix 2 fires → \`dirty_region(0, capacity())\` → \`load_from\` reads zeros → superbitmap bit cleared → array mounts in degraded mode without throwing
- Asserts: \`EXPECT_NO_THROW\`; route stays DEVB (resync disabled via \`toggle_resync(false)\`)

**Fix 1** (the \`pages_before\` guard in \`_start()\`) is covered by the nublox \`resiliency-2-0-dense\` integration test, which exercises the full resync-to-completion-then-stop sequence.

## Checklist

- [x] Fix 1: resync thread commits clean transition when stopped after emptying the bitmap
- [x] Fix 2: mount invariant replaced with warn + dirty-all fallback
- [x] Regression test exercises Fix 2 end-to-end (Fix 1 covered by integration test)
- [x] clang-format applied to modified files
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated (0.32.10)
- [ ] CI — build must run on Linux (liburing / isa-l are Linux-only)

Closes #300

author: arkmish
body:
## What this changes

One line in `zookeeper-client/zookeeper-client-c/ssl/gencerts.sh`: cap the certificate CommonName at 64 characters.

## Root cause

`gencerts.sh` derives the X.509 CommonName from `hostname -f`. On runners with a long FQDN — e.g. Kubernetes pods / self-hosted CI runners whose names look like `rdev-aks-…-cq4mx.corp.rdev.svc.cluster.local` (~80 chars) — the CN exceeds the **64-character ASN.1 limit**, so every `openssl req` fails with `string too long:maxsize=64` and **no certificates are generated**.

The Java test server then silently skips its secure port (22281 never listens), and `Zookeeper_simpleSystem::testSSL` (`TestClient.cc`) issues a **synchronous** `zoo_create` against `127.0.0.1:22281` whose session can never establish. Synchronous C-client ops have no per-call timeout, so the IO thread spins on connect-refused and the main thread blocks forever in `wait_sync_completion` — **hanging the `full-build-java-tests` and `full-build-cppunit-tests` jobs indefinitely** (camping on runners until the 6h timeout).

This is why it reproduced only on long-FQDN runners and not on upstream CI (short hostnames), and why it had nothing to do with the C client itself.

## Fix

Truncate the CN-deriving FQDN to 64 characters (`FQDN=${FQDN:0:64}`). The CN isn't used for hostname verification in these tests (the client connects to `127.0.0.1`), so any valid ≤64-char value is sufficient.

## Testing Done

- **Diagnosed** via a `gdb` thread dump on a long-FQDN Linux runner: main thread blocked in `wait_sync_completion`, IO thread spinning on connect-refused to `127.0.0.1:22281`; `/tmp/certs/gencerts.stderr` showed the `string too long:maxsize=64` openssl failure and `ss -ltn` confirmed 22281 was not listening.
- **Verified locally**: the original 80-char CN reproduces the exact `string too long:maxsize=64` error; with the truncation, the full `gencerts.sh` run completes and generates `root.crt` / `server.crt` / `client.crt` + keystores.
- **Verified on CI**: with the fix, both `full-build-cppunit-tests` (8m22s) and `full-build-java-tests` jobs completed **green** — the exact jobs that previously hung for hours.

### Dependency note
`@vercel/analytics@2` declares an *optional* `@sveltejs/kit` peer that drags in a `vite@8` chain conflicting with the project's `vite@5` (vitest). Installed with `npm install --force` (strict resolver, force past the optional peer) — this adds **only** the one package with **no transitive drift** (`zod`/`@testing-library` versions unchanged), and `npm ci` installs the resulting lock cleanly, so **no `.npmrc`/`legacy-peer-deps`** is needed.

body:
## Cross-reference repair + live render fixes + developer cross-link enrichment

A full cross-reference and visual-polish pass over the docs, **verified against the live docs.taskade.com site** with a multi-agent render audit (curl-based; the site is server-rendered). Repairs every broken live cross-reference, fixes render leakage that showed as raw text, and connects product/help pages to the developer hub.

### How this was scoped

- Audited all **962 `.md` files**; excluded `archive/` (738 files, not in nav) → focused on the **188 live pages** reachable from `SUMMARY.md`.
- Fetched live pages across every section with 5 audit agents — which surfaced a defect class **static analysis alone misses** (see below).
- **Disjoint from #56 / #57** — no file or `SUMMARY.md` overlap, so all three PRs merge independently.

### 1 · Cross-reference repairs (broken links → real targets)

| Broken target | Repointed to | Files |
|---|---|---|
| `space-apps-guide/app-styles.md` (missing) | `space-apps-guide/advanced-features.md` | 3 |
| `./version-history.md` (wrong dir) | `../genesis/version-history.md` | 2 |
| `../genesis/create-your-first-app.md` | `../genesis/getting-started.md` | 1 |
| `../../ai-credits.md` | `account-management/credits-and-billing.md` | 1 |
| `./templates.md` | `./examples-and-templates.md` | 1 |
| legacy `../../api/genesis/`, `../../api/forms/` | `apis-living-system-development/developer-home.md` | 2 |
| `../../index.md` (tutorial nav) | same-dir `README.md` | 2 |

### 2 · GitHub-blob fallback fixes (the audit's key catch)

GitBook renders a relative link to **any file not in `SUMMARY.md`** (missing *or* orphaned) as an external `https://github.com/taskade/docs/blob/main/…` URL — silently **ejecting readers out of the docs to raw markdown**. A file-existence check can't catch these; the live fetch did.

| Page | Was (ejected to GitHub) | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `workspaces/README.md`, `workspaces/collaboration.md` | `../../features/project-views-mastery.md` | `./project-views.md` |
| `ai-features/ai-agents-getting-started.md` | `../../features/…automation-getting-started.md`, `…project-views-mastery.md` | `../automation/README.md`, `../workspaces/project-views.md` |
| `automation/actions.md` | `../../automation/triggers.md` | `./advanced-actions.md` |
| `space-apps-guide/genesis-prompt-library.md` | `../../features/…genesis-getting-started.md` | `../genesis/getting-started.md` |
| `help-center/import-and-export.md`, `mobile-app.md` | orphan `getting-started/`, `ai-features/…`, `features/` | real `../getting-started/`, `../genesis-living-system-builder/…` |

### 3 · Render leakage fixes (rendered as raw text on live)

| File | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `automation/recipes.md` | Entire stepper + a hint were **backslash-escaped** (`\{% step %\}`) → rendered as literal `{% step %}` text | Reconstructed as valid GitBook `{% stepper %}` / `{% hint %}` blocks |
| `space-apps-guide/advanced-features.md` | Literal prose `\n` showed as visible "\n" and collapsed a bullet list | Converted to real line breaks / bullets |

*(Systemic scan confirmed `recipes.md` was the only file with escaped tags; `markdown.md`'s `\n` are intentional syntax examples inside code spans and were left alone.)*

### 4 · Enrichment — connect product docs → developer hub (16 pages)

One conservative, additive developer cross-link added to each page **where it already mentions API / programmatic / integration access** — matching existing table/hint/content-ref style. Targets: `developer-home.md`, `comprehensive-api-guide/README.md` (REST v1), `webhooks.md`, `autonomous-agents.md`.

Examples: Genesis "Go Deeper" table → Developer Hub · Workspaces "API access" → REST API v1 · Agent Tools (HTTP/Webhooks) → Webhooks · API tutorial chapter → Developer Home + Webhooks · Credits & Billing → API rate limits.

### Verification

- ✅ **0** live broken links · **0** github-blob fallbacks (re-checked after enrichment)
- ✅ All 16 new enrichment links resolve to real files
- ✅ Balanced GitBook syntax across all 32 files (0 escaped tags remain)
- ✅ No secrets / placeholders / `/broken/pages/` markers

author: voicific
body:
Seed suppliers are remapped to slug IDs in state (e.g. 'british-airways') so carousel links work, but updateSupplier/deleteSupplier were passing the slug directly into .eq('id', slug) against a uuid-typed PK column. PostgreSQL rejects the cast, returning a cryptic error; the DB row was never touched.

Introduce a dbIdBySlug ref that records slug→actual UUID during load and after resetToSeedData. All write paths now resolve the real UUID before calling Supabase, while keeping the slug id in local state for link parity.

author: sighingpotato
body:
## 작업 내용

- ERD 설계에 맞춰 Payment 엔티티의 컬럼을 확장하고, 포인트 복합 결제 시 발생하던 금액 검증 버그를 해결했습니다.
- 실제 가동 환경에서의 데이터 무결성을 위해 동시성 제어(비관적 락)를 적용하고, 정합성 예외 발생 시 외부 PG 결제까지 함께 취소해 주는 안전장치(보상 트랜잭션)를 구축했습니다.

## 변경 이유

- 금액 검증 논리 결함: 포인트 복합 결제 시 사용자가 포인트를 사용하면 외부 PG사에 기록되는 실제 승인 금액은 pg_real_amount가 됩니다. 기존 코드는 이를 총 주문 금액(amount)과 대조하고 있어, 포인트를 쓴 모든 결제가 무조건 실패하는 버그가 있었습니다.
- 동시성 레이스 컨디션: 사용자의 결제창 완료 시점에 프론트엔드가 쏘는 /confirm API와 포트원 서버가 쏘는 웹훅 알림이 동시(수 ms 차이)에 인입될 경우, 멱등성 검증 코드가 무력화되어 포인트 적립 및 멤버십 누적 결제액이 이중 합산되는 치명적인 데이터 오염 우려가 있었습니다.
- 결제 실패 상태 방치: 우리 서버 검증단에서 에러가 터졌을 때 DB 데이터만 FAILED로 바꾸고 끝내면, 사용자의 돈은 이미 외부 PG 망에서 출금된 상태로 방치되는 심각한 정합성 불일치가 발생합니다. 이를 자동 환불 처리해야 했습니다.

## 주요 변경 사항

Payment.java
- ERD 명세에 따라 pg_real_amount, subscription_id (간접 참조용 필드), pg_provider, payment_method 컬럼을 확장했습니다.
- 단건 상품 결제 팩토리(createPayment)에서는 amount - usedPoint 수식으로 실결제액을 자동 산정하며, 새로 오버로딩된 구독용 팩토리(createSubscriptionPayment)에서는 포인트 사용 없이 전액 출금되도록 구현했습니다.
- 정기 구독 결제 내역도 수용할 수 있도록 order_id 외래키 제약조건을 nullable = true로 완화했습니다.

PaymentRepository.java
- 동시성 동시 진입을 차단하기 위해 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE를 가동하는 @Lock(LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) 기반의 findByPortonePaymentIdWithLock 메서드를 신설했습니다.

PaymentService.java
- validatePortOneStatus 내부 대조 대상을 payment.getPgRealAmount()로 전면 교정했습니다.
- try-catch 예외 처리 블록을 설계하여, 교차 검증 실패 시 portOneClient.cancelPayment를 원격 호출하는 자동 보상 취소 안전장치를 도입했습니다.
- 포인트 차등 적립 정책이 원활히 작동하도록 멤버십 누적금 합산 직전에 등급별 적립률을 연산하도록 흐름을 정돈했습니다.



## 테스트 및 확인

- [ ] 로컬 실행 확인
- [x] 관련 기능 동작 확인
- [x] 기존 기능 영향 없음 확인

## 리뷰 포인트

- PaymentService에서 금액 위변조나 정합성 예외가 감지되었을 때, 선차감되었던 재고의 복구와 외부 PG사 자동 환불 연동(cancelPayment)이 트랜잭션 롤백 직전에 순차적으로 잘 맞아떨어지는지 예외 전파 흐름을 리뷰해 주세요.
- 비관적 락 조회가 잘 적용되었는지 확인해주시면 좋겠습니다.

## 참고 사항

- Subscription 및 SecurityConfig 코드는 건드리지 않았습니다.
- closes #75

* **사용 AI 툴**
  - Gemini

* **활용 목적**
  - 리팩터링 제안, PR 작성

* **핵심 프롬프트 및 반영 내용**
  - 리팩토링에서 빠진 부분 및 PR작성 시 빠진 부분

author: peterkang34
body:
## Summary

Fixes the **Deal Architect** achievement, which could never unlock in real games — reported by a player via feedback. Root cause is a field-name mismatch: the game-over aggregation read `a.details.dealStructure` off acquire actions, but the real acquire paths in `useGame.ts` record financing as `a.details.structure` (a `DealStructureType`). So `dealStructureTypes` was always `{}` in real play.

The same dead read had a second, opposite effect: **No Leverage**'s `usedLeverage` check was always false, so it was auto-granted to any solvent C-grade-or-better run regardless of how much bank debt was used. Both are now correct.

It only looked like it worked because the `#/go-test` harness fixture used the *same wrong field name* (and an invalid `'cash'` value), masking the bug.

## Changes

- **Extract** the aggregation into a pure, tested helper `src/utils/strategyAggregation.ts` (`aggregateDealStructureTypes`, `countRolloverEquityDeals`, `ACQUIRE_ACTION_TYPES`) as a single source of truth — it feeds the achievement, the Operator Playbook deal-structure/rollover breakdown, telemetry, and admin overview.
- **Wire** `GameOverScreen.tsx` to the helper (reads `details.structure`).
- **Fix** the `goTestSetup.ts` fixture (`dealStructure` → `structure`, invalid `'cash'` → `'all_cash'`) so the test harness can't mask this again.
- **Regression test** `src/engine/__tests__/strategy-aggregation.test.ts` over the real action shape, including a guard that a legacy `dealStructure` field is ignored, plus an end-to-end check that `deal_architect` unlocks at 4 unique structures.

body:
## Description

The `osx` / `osx-arm64` legs of the **MSSQL VSIX Launch Verification** workflow were failing to launch VS Code with an `EINVAL` error.

Root cause: the launch utility built the user-data directory from `os.tmpdir()`, which on macOS returns a long `/var/folders/.../T` path. Combined with the nested `vscode-mssql-test-<timestamp>/user-data` directories and VS Code's recently changed IPC socket filename (e.g. `1.12-main.sock`), the resulting Unix domain socket path was **105 chars**, exceeding macOS's hard **103-char socket path limit** — so VS Code could not create its IPC socket and Electron failed to launch.

Fix: on macOS, use a short `/tmp` base instead of `os.tmpdir()` for the test's user-data/extensions directories, keeping the socket path well under the limit. Linux/Windows continue to use `os.tmpdir()`.

This mirrors the same workaround already applied to `sql-database-projects` in #22295, tracked in [vscode#319752](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/319752).

**What changed**
Added explicit `aria-label` attributes to icon-only buttons in `QazaDetailSheet.tsx` (Close button) and `CycleSettings.tsx` (Remove cycle period button).

Users relying on screen readers (like VoiceOver or TalkBack) need text descriptions to understand what icon buttons do. Without labels, these buttons are announced simply as "button," making the app difficult or impossible to use for visually impaired individuals.

**Mobile UX impact**
While visually unchanged, this makes the app significantly more robust and trustworthy for users who rely on accessibility features native to mobile operating systems.

Directly addresses the standard: "Every icon-only button must have an aria-label." Screen readers will now correctly announce "Close details" and "Remove cycle period" instead of a generic button prompt.

## For Tuesday
A standalone seeder that populates the admin dashboard with real-looking traffic so the sparklines, revenue totals, recent-orders feed and customer-insights modal all tell a story for the showcase.

**Run before the demo:**
```
php artisan db:seed --class=DemoTransactionsSeeder
```

**Not wired into `DatabaseSeeder::run()`** — deliberately invoked-only so it never runs against prod accidentally.

## What it seeds
Per your two answers: **last 10 days only**, **moderate volume**.

- **60 synthetic customers** (`demo+NNN@ridly.local`) joined across the last 10 days so new-users metric has variation
- **250 orders** weighted **78% paid / 12% pending / 8% failed / 2% cancelled**, tilted toward the last 3 days so the 7d sparkline is busy and the 10/30d view shows a recent surge
- **1–3 line items per order**, brand-popularity weighted (Steam, Netflix, Discord overrepresented) so the top-products chart looks real
- **20% of paid/pending orders carry a voucher** with a real `discount_amount`, so the cart/discount columns aren't all blank
- **Paid voucher orders consume real `ProductKey`s** (or mints them if the pool is dry); **paid direct-topup orders get a `sent` `TopupCredential`** — so Transactions/Inventory pages look fulfilled
- **Test user (id=1) is force-fed ~11 orders** so logging in as them on demo day shows a populated transactions/inventory feed

## Idempotent
Everything created is tagged with `INV-DEMO-` invoice prefix or `demo+%@ridly.local` email — re-running drops the prior demo rows (frees product keys back to the pool, unlinks discounts) then re-seeds. Real users/orders are never touched.

## Verified locally
After `migrate:fresh --seed && db:seed --class=DemoTransactionsSeeder`:
```
orders total: 250
paid: 196
revenue (paid): Rp 158.580.300
test user orders: 11
test user paid keys: 11
```

author: bu-bu-butasan
body:
## 一言でいうと

このPRは、地震イベントの「被災セル」が本物だと確かめるための計算ロジックを、新しい共通部品 `@sonari/proof-core` にまとめる変更です。あわせて、別の言語（Rust・Move・Python）で計算した結果と1バイトもずれないことを、固定の見本データ（ゴールデンベクター）で固定します。

親issue #141 を分けた子issue「A（土台）」です。後続のB/C/Dがこの土台の上に乗ります。

## なぜ必要か

被災セルの証明（proof）を作る計算は、すでにある居住セルのRust製ツールと、leaf（末端データ）の種類以外はほぼ同じ中身です。

ただしRust製ツールはそのままWeb配信側（TypeScript）に載せられません。2つの言語で同じ計算を二重に持つのは、保守コストが高く、MVP段階では割に合いません。

そこで証明を作る計算はTypeScriptで実装し、Rust・Move・Pythonと結果が一致することは見本データで担保します。さらに、これまで居住セル用パッケージに埋もれていた汎用ロジックを `@sonari/proof-core` に集約し、TypeScript内の二重実装も解消します。

ここでいう用語の補足です。

- leaf（リーフ）: 木構造の末端にある1件分のデータ。ここでは1つのセルの情報。
- Merkle root（マークルルート）: 複数のデータが改ざんされていないか確かめるための代表値。1つでもデータが変わると値が変わる。
- proof（プルーフ）: 「このセルは確かにこの代表値に含まれる」と確かめるための検証用データ。
- BCS: Moveに渡すために決まった形へ変換したバイナリ表現。
- fail-closed: あやしい入力のときは処理を進めずに止める方針。

## 何が変わったか

| 見る場所 | 変更前 | 変更後 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ユーザーや運用から見える動き | 変化なし（被災セル証明の配信機能はまだ無い） | 変化なし。今回は土台の部品追加のみ |
| システム内部の動き | 証明の計算ロジックが居住セル用パッケージに混在 | 汎用ロジックを `@sonari/proof-core` に集約。居住セル用は薄い参照に |
| 失敗した時の動き | （被災セル用の入力検証は未整備） | 不正な入力（重複・未ソート・範囲外・不明な区分値）はすべて処理を止める（fail-closed） |

主な追加内容です。

- 新パッケージ `packages/proof-core/` を追加。
- 被災セルleafのBCS変換とleafハッシュ、Merkle rootの生成・検証、proofの生成、配信形式の証明への変換、shard（分割）の割り当てを実装。
- 見本データ（`schemas/examples/affected_cells.json` ほか）で、計算結果がRust・Move・Pythonと一致することを固定。
- 既存の `@sonari/residence-proof-worker` を `@sonari/proof-core` 依存へ付け替え（中身の動きは変えない）。

## 流れ

被災セルの入力ファイルから、代表値（root）と証明（proof）を作る流れです。

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[被災セルの入力ファイル] --> B[検証する]
  B -->|不正なら止める| E[エラーで停止]
  B --> C[セルを番号の昇順に並べる]
  C --> D[各セルのleafハッシュを計算]
  D --> F[Merkle rootを計算]
  D --> G[各セルのproofを生成]
  G --> H[配信形式に変換 / shardへ割り当て]
```

## レビューで見てほしい点

- 被災セルleafのバイト並び（10項目の順序・`event_uid`を長さ情報なしの生32バイトで扱う・整数はリトルエンディアン）が、Python参照（`schemas/examples/verify_golden_vectors.py:284`）とMove（`contracts/sources/affected_cell.move:63`）と同じでよいか。
- Merkle rootの作り方（要素数が奇数のとき末尾を複製せずそのまま昇格・中間ノードは`0x01`を先頭に付ける）と、proofの左右判定（`sibling_on_left = 兄弟の位置 < 自分の位置`）の規約でよいか。
- 居住セル用パッケージの改修が「中身の動きを変えない」範囲に収まっているか（既存テストは1行も変えずに通過）。
- Python参照で整数値が未定義の区分値 `shakemap_hdf_h3_area_weighted_p90_v1` を、あえて未対応（エラーで停止）にした判断でよいか。勝手な値を割り当てないための fail-closed です。

## 影響範囲

| 領域 | 影響 |
| --- | --- |
| API | なし |
| DB / schema | なし（既存schemaは参照のみ。新規schema文字列は子issue Bで確定） |
| Move contract | なし（`affected_cell.move` は一致確認のため参照のみ） |
| verifier / relayer / worker | あり（`residence-proof-worker` を proof-core 依存へ改修。動作は不変） |
| UI | なし |
| docs | なし |

## 壊れていないことの確認

- [x] `pnpm --filter @sonari/proof-core test`（158→159件 通過）
- [x] `pnpm --filter @sonari/proof-core typecheck`（通過）
- [x] `pnpm --filter @sonari/residence-proof-worker test`（15件 通過・テスト無改変＝リグレッションなし）

author: ceekay-munshot
body:
## Gap identified

The eval suite's J-check (framework source contracts) protected five bodies of system wiring — the §24 Avoid-Big-Risks filters, the §17 catalyst module, three-tier output, the review scheduler — but **not the five post-run audit command files** that implement the system's truth-auditing and learning loop:

- `verify-evidence` — checks claimed figures against the data pool, reconciles math, tests cross-module anchor consistency
- `pre-mortem` — red-teams the thesis adversarially (one inviolable rule: can only hold or lower conviction, **never raise it**)
- `expectations-gap` — tests whether variant perception is real and the gap is exploitable
- `review-decisions` — writes append-only outcome reviews, never overwrites decision records
- `calibrate` — aggregates performance and calibration, refuses to fake metrics on insufficient data

If any of these commands were modified to remove their read-only constraints, no-fabrication rule, the pre-mortem one-direction rule, append-only semantics, or their JSON schema keys, the regression harness would **not catch it**. These are the commands that make the engine harder to fool — regressing them silently is the worst possible failure mode.

## Why this is the highest-leverage gap

- The system's golden fixtures (BG, HCG) pass the eval cleanly today
- All five modules, the synthesizer, the three-tier output, and the scheduler are regression-protected by J-check
- But the audit command layer — the commands that check the system's own outputs for truthfulness — was an unguarded blind spot
- The pre-mortem's "never raise conviction" rule is the single most important constraint in the system; it was not protected

## Files changed

`eval.md` only — three targeted edits:
1. **Markdown description of check J**: Updated "two bodies of wiring" → "five bodies of wiring," added item **(v) Audit command layer** describing what is now protected
2. **Python comment** at the J-check block: Updated to mention all five protected bodies
3. **`FRAMEWORK_CONTRACTS` dict**: Added 5 new entries (one per audit command), each checking the most critical structural strings

## Architecture fit

Pure extension of the existing J-check pattern. No new commands, no new agents, no new schemas, no changes to the run flow. Adds 5 entries to an existing dict; the loop that runs them is unchanged. Zero risk of breaking existing behavior.

## Validation performed

Ran the full 23-entry J-check against the live command files — all **23/23 PASS**, including all 5 new audit command contracts. The BG and HCG golden fixtures are unaffected; the full eval suite passes.

## Remaining limitations

- The J-check tests string presence, not semantic correctness. A command file that retained the protected strings but broke its logic in a non-string way would not be caught. That is a known limitation of all J-check entries, not new with this change.
- The check still treats audit report *presence* on finished runs as optional (check G is N/A if absent). Making pre-mortem or verify-evidence mandatory per run would require a bigger orchestration change.

## Suggested next improvement

The most impactful next gap to address: **sector-specific valuation templates**. For cyclical/commodity businesses like BG, the DCF should use mid-cycle normalized EBITDA rather than spot earnings — the intrinsic-dcf agent claims to branch by business type but there is no explicit mid-cycle normalization framework. For financials, DDM/residual-income is mentioned but not mechanically enforced. Adding a business-type → valuation-method contract to the J-check (and the corresponding mechanical steps to the intrinsic-dcf agent) would reduce false precision in cyclical valuations.

---

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The plaintext Gemini API key was being rendered inside the HTML `value` attribute of the settings text input. Even though `type="password"` obscures the text visually, the actual secret value was sent to the user's browser, exposing it to DOM inspection and potential browser extensions.

## 问题

线上已部署 #56,但经 blockrun 渠道(如 `gpt-4o-br`)的请求仍报:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Invalid value for 'parallel_tool_calls': 'parallel_tool_calls' is only allowed when 'tools' are specified. Received Model Group=gpt-4o
```

## 根因

#56 只修了 `relay/channel/openai/adaptor.go`。但 blockrun 是**独立渠道**(ChannelType 100 / `APITypeBlockRun` / 独立 `blockrun.Adaptor`),它的 `ConvertOpenAIRequest` 是**纯透传**(`return request, nil`),从未走到 #56 的剔除逻辑。

链路:`客户端 → LiteLLM(gpt-4o) → newapi(blockrun, gpt-4o-br) → 原样透传 parallel_tool_calls(无 tools)→ 上游 400`。

## 改动

`relay/channel/blockrun/adaptor.go`:`ConvertOpenAIRequest` 在 `len(request.Tools) == 0` 时把 `request.ParallelTooCalls` 置 nil,再透传。带 tools 的请求不受影响。

`relay/channel/blockrun/adaptor_test.go` 新增:
- 无 tools → parallel_tool_calls 被剔除;
- 有 tools → parallel_tool_calls 保留;
- 原有 passthrough / nil 用例不受影响。

`go build` 通过,blockrun 包全量测试 ok。

同样的纯透传缺口还存在于约 15 个 OpenAI 兼容渠道(moonshot / deepseek / xai / volcengine / minimax / siliconflow 等)。彻底根治可在唯一公共入口 `relay/compatible_handler.go` 调 `ConvertOpenAIRequest` 前集中剔除一次。本 PR 按需只先修 blockrun。

author: crowlbot
body:
## Problem

`@param` documentation was not rendered for **rest/spread parameters** in the HTML output (issue #574). Given:

```ts
/**
 * @param first the leading number
 * @param rest the trailing numbers
 */
export function sum(first: number, ...rest: number[]): number { /* … */ }
```

the doc for `first` rendered, but the doc for `rest` was silently dropped.

## Cause

When matching `@param` tags to parameters, `function.rs` keyed the lookup on the *rendered* parameter name. For a rest parameter, `param_name()` produces a `...`-prefixed name (`...rest`), while the JSDoc `@param` tag name is the bare identifier (`rest`). The keys never matched, so the description, default and optional flag were all lost for rest parameters.

## Fix

Match each parameter to its `@param` tag by the bare identifier it binds, via a new `param_doc_name` helper that unwraps rest (`...rest` → `rest`) and default (`x = 1` → `x`) patterns. Array/object destructuring patterns bind no single name, so they yield `None` and are not matched by name — otherwise an unrelated tag's doc could be attached to them.

## Test

- `html_rest_param_jsdoc` covers the reported case: the rest parameter's doc now renders.
- `html_param_jsdoc_destructuring` pins the boundary: a rest parameter alongside a destructured one still resolves, and a `@param` naming no parameter is not attached to the destructured one.
- The existing `diff_comprehensive` snapshots pick up the now-rendered doc for a `...middlewares` rest parameter, confirming the fix end-to-end.

Fixes #574

author: mujtaba3b
body:
## Summary

Converges `qa:browser` from a gstack-browse-daemon mockup-diff skill into a **live-browser QA skill**: it drives the user's persistent agent-browser session (`abrowser`, headed) at click/pixel level, not just endpoint calls. This codifies the workflow proven in hesco PR #81 and wires QA Quincey into the build-time Stop hook (`mujtaba3B/dev#32`) and the PR qa-gate CI (hesco `#82`).

The plugin reorg (PR #19) renamed the old skill to `qa:browser` unchanged; this PR is the actual convergence we aligned on.

### What changed
- **Driver:** persistent `abrowser` session instead of the gstack browse daemon. Cookie-import auth path removed (the session carries logins). All `abrowser` calls are batched per step to avoid the 1Password `op`-prompt storm.
- **Walk the spec:** opens `spec/eng` docs + Pencil frames and reports per-assertion **Spec compliance** (`matches`/`drifts`/`missing`); no green without it (hesco rule).
- **Seed/teardown:** boots + seeds TAGGED data and tears it down exactly via a committed per-repo recipe (`.gstack/qa-quincey/recipe.yml`), **declarative pointers only** (no inline code, so it is not a supply-chain surface for autonomous agents). A bundled validator (`scripts/validate-recipe.py`) rejects inline secrets, absolute paths, and an unscoped teardown.
- **Adversarial probe:** at least one off-happy-path probe is now required (the precision check, e.g. hesco #81's "company blanked still detours").
- **QA posture contract:** the run ends by stating `QA_STATUS`/`EVIDENCE`, satisfying the lenient build-time Stop hook and the strict PR qa-gate CI, including the `skip_requested -> skip_approved` escalation (CI rejects a bare `skip_requested`). Added to shared `core.md` so `qa:headless` states a posture too. Reconcile-to-`/pm:bug` is now optional.

### New artifacts
`references/{abrowser-driving,recipe-schema,qa-contract}.md`, `scripts/{validate-recipe.py,test_validate_recipe.py}`, `evals/{triggering.jsonl,README.md}`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Plugin + skill bumped to v2.0.0. Obsolete `references/cookie-profile-probe.md` removed.

### Design decisions (with a second opinion)
The per-repo recipe lives in-repo and committed (not `~/.gstack`) because MuTwo agents and CI have no `~/.gstack`; this follows gstack's own in-repo carve-out for must-travel / CI-trusted artifacts. Codex (gpt-5.5) stress-tested the design and drove the "declarative pointers, not inline code" + "validate the recipe" guardrails.

## QA

QA_STATUS: verified

author: jacekradko
body:
The `generic` leg runs ~210 tests against one shared staging instance, so any single post-retry flake reds the whole matrix. That is the main reason the staging run has been ~100% red and gives no signal.

This splits the gate. A handful of stable core-auth happy paths are tagged `@smoke` and run as their own small matrix leg against just the two core apps, and the full `generic` leg becomes `continue-on-error` so it still runs and uploads results but no longer fails the run. Because only gating legs (smoke plus the framework legs) can fail the matrix job, `needs.integration-tests.result` is `failure` only on a real gating-leg failure, so the existing report job notifies on meaningful failures instead of on generic-only flake. The clerk_go commit-status block stays commented out; when it is wired up (follow-up) it inherits the same gating semantics.

The load-bearing choice here is the `@smoke` set, since it is what gates. I kept it deliberately conservative: five happy paths that never appeared in a failed/flaky list across the recent runs (sign-in with password, with instant password, the modal variant, sign-up with password, and a single-flow sign-out), run against `react.vite.withEmailCodes` and `next.appRouter.withEmailCodes`. It is just tags, so it should grow as the rate-limit flake is brought under control. A few tests now run in both legs (smoke and the informational generic), which is cheap insurance and lets the smoke result come from the clean, low-load leg rather than the noisy 210-test one.

Stacked on #8757.

body:
💡 **What:** Optimized `getCurrentUVFromHourly` by replacing `new Date(times[i])` with `Date.parse(times[i])` to avoid allocation inside the loop, and using `now.getTime()` outside the loop. Additionally added an early `break` statement since the data is sequential.
🎯 **Why:** The original code redundantly instantiated `Date` objects during every loop iteration and continued checking all items even after passing the closest matching timestamp.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** Baseline (Original code iterating 10,000 times): middle-of-array search was 938.8ms; start-of-array search was 925.2ms. Optimized implementation: middle-of-array was 206.7ms (4.5x faster); start-of-array was 10.6ms (87x faster). Overall average performance is much faster due to earlier breaking and avoiding Date object allocations.

## Problem

The build fails during `composer install` because `phpoffice/phpspreadsheet`, `simplesoftwareio/simple-qrcode`, and `maatwebsite/excel` all require `ext-gd`, but the extension was not declared in `composer.json` and therefore not installed by Railpack's PHP provider.
