author: sdh07
body:
Closes #515.

Follow-up from #491 / PR #513 (curated-portal auto-refresh, option 4b). `wiki_index_update.py --set-leadin` stamps each engine-owned portal lead-in with `refreshed:<date> bullets:<N>`, but nothing read the stamp yet — the producer shipped ahead of the consumer. This adds the read-only drift consumer.

## Summary
- New `pipeline-summary.py portal-staleness --wiki-root <root> [--threshold N]` subcommand: walks `<wiki-root>/wiki/index.md` per `## <theme>` section, parses the stamped `bullets:<N>` from the `MACHINE-OWNED:PORTAL-LEADIN:START` sentinel, counts the live `- … [[slug]] …` slug-bullet rows, and returns `{stale_count, threshold, stale_themes:[{theme, stamped_bullets, live_bullets, delta}]}`. A theme is stale when `delta = live - stamped > threshold` (default 2). Themes with no machine lead-in span are skipped silently; a missing/unreadable `index.md` is fail-soft success (`stale_count: 0`).
- `knowledge-dashboard` overlay now calls `portal-staleness` and renders a one-line `stale portal lead-ins: M theme(s)` signal in the `## Pipeline health` block — **only when `stale_count > 0`** (acceptance: zero-drift bases are silent). Fail-soft: a failed call omits the line and keeps going, same posture as the existing cache-health failure note.
- Pure observability: no auto-refresh trigger, no write path. The section/stamp/slug-bullet parsing is reimplemented locally in stdlib — **no cogni-wiki import** (the dependency direction stays cogni-knowledge → cogni-wiki). The local `_HEADING_RE` / `_LEADIN_START_RE` mirror `wiki_index_update.py` L74/L107 so the reader stays in lockstep with the producer.
- Plugin version bump 0.1.77 → 0.1.78, mirrored in `marketplace.json`.

## Acceptance
- [x] The dashboard surface reports the count of themes whose machine lead-in is stale by the threshold.
- [x] Zero-drift bases are silent (the dashboard line renders only when `stale_count > 0`).

## Test plan
- `bash cogni-knowledge/tests/test_portal_staleness.sh` — 14 assertions: stale-by->threshold flagged with correct stamped/live/delta, within-threshold not flagged, no-machine-lead-in skipped, `--threshold` override (0 flags both, 5 flags none), zero-drift base silent, missing index.md fail-soft.
- `bash cogni-knowledge/tests/test_dashboard_contract.sh` — ALL PASS (existing surfaces survive).
- `bash cogni-knowledge/tests/test_pipeline_summary.sh` — ALL PASS.

## Scope decisions
- **Deferred (follow-up):** the cogni-wiki-side `wiki-health` info-count leg of the issue's "and/or". It adds cross-plugin blast radius (a `cogni-wiki/.../health.py` change) not required to meet the acceptance, which the cogni-knowledge dashboard surface already satisfies.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>tsarna/vinculum (github.com/tsarna/vinculum)</summary>

### [`v0.37.1`](https://redirect.github.com/tsarna/vinculum/releases/tag/v0.37.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/tsarna/vinculum/compare/v0.37.0...v0.37.1)

##### Fixed

- **Container images can now actually build and load plugins** (0.37.0 shipped the plugin feature but the images could not use it). `-buildmode=plugin` always requires external (cgo) linking, and a statically linked host cannot `dlopen` a plugin — but the `vinculum-build` and runtime images were built with `CGO_ENABLED=0`. The `vinculum-build` image and the default (alpine) runtime image are now built **cgo-enabled** (with `gcc` + `musl-dev`, dynamically linked against musl). The scratch-based **minimal image remains statically linked and cannot load plugins** — this is now documented; its pre-created `/plugins` dir and `--plugin-path` flag are inert unless a config declares a `plugin` block.
- **Plugin ABI identity**: the default runtime image now builds its host binary by installing the versioned module (`go install github.com/tsarna/vinculum@<ref>`) instead of `go build .` from the working tree. A plugin imports vinculum as a versioned dependency, and `-buildmode=plugin` bakes the module path+version into every package's build ID; a `go build .` host gave those packages "main-module" identity and dependency-built plugins failed to load with `different version of package …`. A new `VINCULUM_REF` build-arg selects the version (the release tag; a commit pseudo-version for `:latest`/`:dev`).

</details>

author: holeman79
body:
## 무엇을 / 왜

중앙집중돼 있던 `gb-config-yaml-importer/application*.yml` 을 **각 모듈이 자기 설정을 소유**하는 구조로 분산하고, `GbEnvironmentPostProcessor` 가 `classpath*:` 로 전 모듈 설정을 병합하도록 변경했다 (meet-again 패턴 이식).

기존엔 "설정을 담는 모듈은 importer 하나"였는데, 이는 Spring Boot 의 단일 `classpath:` 로딩 제약을 우회하지 못한 단순화였다. EPP + `classpath*:` 로 모듈별 `config/application.yml` 충돌을 해소한다.

## 분산 매핑

| 모듈 | 파일 | 내용 |
|---|---|---|
| `gb-config-yaml-importer` | `GbEnvironmentPostProcessor` + `META-INF/spring.factories` | 병합 로직만 (yaml 제거) |
| `gb-boot-web` | `application.yml` (루트) | 앱 공통 — multipart |
| `gb-db-core` | `config/application.yml` | JPA 공통 (open-in-view, batch_fetch_size, ...) |
| `gb-db-core` | `config/application-{local,prod}.yml` | datasource (`on-profile` gated) |
| `gb-id-obfuscator` | `config/application.yml` | `id-obfuscator.salt` / `min-length` |

## 동작

`GbEnvironmentPostProcessor` 가 `classpath*:` 로 ① 루트 `application.{yml,yaml}` ② `config/application.{yml,yaml}` (모듈 공통) ③ `config/application-*.{yml,yaml}` (`spring.config.activate.on-profile` 매칭) 순으로 스캔·병합 → 최상위 `MapPropertySource` 로 `addFirst`.

- `classpath*:` (전 jar) 로 읽어 여러 모듈의 `config/application.yml` 이 충돌 없이 모두 병합된다.
- 프로파일 미지정 시 EPP no-op → 기존 "프로파일 필수(기본 datasource 없음)" 불변식 유지.

## 검증

- ✅ `:infrastructure:storage:gb-db-core:test` + `:boot:gb-boot-web:test` 통과
- ✅ `local` 프로파일 실부팅 — `Started GroubingServerApplicationKt`, HikariPool(H2)·JPA·HashidsIdObfuscator(salt) 정상 주입
- ✅ no-profile 기동은 설계대로 실패

## 참고

- 이 PR 은 `gb-id-obfuscator` 모듈에 의존하므로(아직 dev 미머지) base 를 `refactor/explicit-path-variable-names` 로 잡아 스택 위에 쌓았다. #18 머지 시 base 자동 재지정됨.
- `CLAUDE.md` 의 옛 중앙집중 설명도 신규 구조에 맞춰 갱신.

author: iap
body:
---

Greptile Summary

This PR restructures CI/CD into a two-tier model (`ci-fast.yml` for every PR, `ci-full.yml` for nightly/manual runs) backed by reusable workflow components, replaces Gitleaks-via-Docker with trufflehog, consolidates governance workflows, updates the ZK circuit with a domain-separated 5-input Poseidon for output commitments, and regenerates the Groth16 verifier. - **CI restructure**: `ci-fast.yml` now correctly declares `on: workflow_call:`, fixing the reusable-workflow contract that `ci-full.yml` depends on; actions are uniformly pinned to immutable SHAs. - **Governance check-name mismatches** (flagged in prior review): `\"Gitleaks Scan\"` remains in the governance required-check lists while the new trufflehog job is named `\"Secret Scan (trufflehog)\"`, so running `apply-governance.sh` will require a check that no CI job ever satisfies. - **Circuit & contract**: Output commitment binding corrected to 5-input Poseidon with domain-separated `dstChainId`; verification key constants and contract name (`Groth16Verifier`) updated to match the new circuit.

Confidence Score: 2/5

Not safe to merge: running apply-governance.sh will require a check named 'Gitleaks Scan' that no workflow produces, permanently deadlocking all future PRs on dev and main. The governance required-check lists still name 'Gitleaks Scan' while the new secrets job is 'Secret Scan (trufflehog)'. The release orchestration smoke tests were dropped with no replacement. scripts/github/apply-governance.sh and scripts/github/verify-governance.sh need the 'Gitleaks Scan' entry corrected.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | .github/workflows/ci-fast.yml | New top-level fast CI workflow; correctly declares workflow_call so ci-full.yml can invoke it; governance required-check list still names 'Gitleaks Scan' which no workflow produces. | | .github/workflows/ci-full.yml | New daily/manual full CI workflow; calls ci-fast.yml via workflow_call (now valid) then adds invariant tests and the release-gate container. | | scripts/github/apply-governance.sh | Required-check lists updated to match new CI job names but still include 'Gitleaks Scan' — trufflehog job is named 'Secret Scan (trufflehog)' — applying this config will permanently deadlock all PRs. | | .github/workflows/_reusable-circuits-core.yml | New reusable circuits workflow; circomspect runs with -l ERROR only, omitting --error unconstrained_signals and --error non_deterministic_circuits flags. | | circuits/mark/MARKPool.circom | Output commitment corrected to 5-input Poseidon with domain-separated dstChainId. Relayer constraint uses LessThan(161) instead of Num2Bits(160); equivalent for practical values. | | contracts/src/pool/verifier/MARKPoolVerifier.sol | Updated verification key constants; contract renamed to Groth16Verifier (snarkjs default); referenced by address/interface so rename does not break compilation. | | contracts/test/integration/bridge/CrossChainDoubleSpend.t.sol | testCrossChainDoubleSpendViaBridgeIn has no assertion in step 5 (previously flagged). Other four sub-tests are well-formed. | | contracts/test/unit/pool/RYLACreditLedger.t.sol | testSetAdapterAllowsReSetWhenZero never exercises its claimed re-set scenario; otherwise correct. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD PR([Pull Request / Push]) --> CF[ci-fast.yml] CF --> S[Secret Scan trufflehog] CF --> TL[Typecheck + Lint] CF --> CC[Contracts Core] CF --> CS[Contracts Security] CF --> CIR[Circuits Core] CF --> FE[Frontend Checks] RG[contracts-release-gate.yml] --> RG_JOB[check: Release Gate Container] GOV([Governance requires: Gitleaks Scan]) -.->|no workflow produces this|DEADLOCK([PR deadlock]) SCHED([Schedule / Dispatch]) --> FULL[ci-full.yml] FULL --> CF FULL --> INV[Contracts Core With Invariants] ```

Comments Outside Diff (1)

 1. `scripts/github/verify-governance.sh`, line 118-123 ([link](https://github.com/trade/mark/blob/fd00a59095c44de7d8b18c52059e19f9b8dce0eb/scripts/github/verify-governance.sh#L118-L123)) **Push-restriction check inconsistent with `apply-governance.sh`** `check_branch` hard-codes a check that `restrictions.teams[].slug == "maintainers"`. But `apply-governance.sh`'s new `build_restrictions()` function can be invoked with `MAIN_PUSH_ALLOW_USERS=iap` (documented in the header comments), which produces a user-based restriction with `teams: []`. When the governance is applied with user-based restrictions, every `verify-governance.sh` run will report `FAIL: push restrictions do not include maintainers team` on both branches. Either the verify script should also accept user-based restrictions, or the apply script should disallow that mode for protected branches.

body:
## Summary

- **`app.py`** — Flask web app with three routes: `/` (home), `/trending` (trending 30), `/book?title=...` (deep-dive). Each route runs all scrapers concurrently via `asyncio.gather` and returns the rendered HTML report.
- **`templates/index.html`** — Minimal home page: book search form + "Trending 30" button + JS loading overlay while scraping runs (20–60 s).
- **`templates/report.html.j2`** — Added web-mode navigation bar (Back to Home / Trending 30) that appears only when rendered by Flask.
- **`renderer.py`** — Added `render_to_string(report, web_mode)` alongside the existing file-based `render()` so CLI and web app share the same template.
- **`requirements.txt`** — Added `flask>=3.0.0` and `gunicorn>=21.2.0`.
- **`Procfile` + `render.yaml`** — Render.com deployment config (`gunicorn` with 120 s timeout).
- **`runtime.txt`** — Pins Python 3.11.

## Architecture note on Netlify

Netlify only hosts static sites and short-lived serverless functions (10 s free-tier timeout). Scraping 7 sources takes 20–60 s, so Flask cannot run on Netlify directly. **Render.com** (free tier, supports gunicorn, no request timeout cap on web services) is the correct deployment target.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pip install -r requirements.txt`
- [ ] `python app.py` → open `http://localhost:5000`, confirm home page loads
- [ ] Search "Dune" → loading spinner appears → full report with web nav bar renders

## Summary

Two targeted consolidations identified by a codebase-wide audit:

### 1. `ensureArray<T>()` utility (6 call sites)

The pattern `Array.isArray(x) ? x : [x]` appeared in six separate production files with no shared abstraction. A new `ensureArray<T>(value: T | T[]): T[]` helper is added to `src/utils/core/typeGuards.ts` and exported from the `@utils/core` barrel.

**Call sites updated:**
- `src/utils/config/configUtils.ts` — `watchConfig` key normalisation
- `src/tools/lean/LoogleTool.ts` — query coercion in `execute()`
- `src/tools/texcount/TexcountTool.ts` — body of `toFileArray()` helper
- `src/latex/texcount.ts` — file-path coercion in `getTeXCount()`
- `src/agent/modelHandlers/support/MediaAttachmentProcessor.ts` — inline coercion (×1) and body of `normalizeToArray()` (×1)

### 2. `delay()` from `@utils/core/async` (11 call sites)

`@utils/core/async` already re-exports the `delay` package as the codebase's canonical async-sleep helper. Eleven files ignored this and reinvented the wheel with `new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms))`. One file (`ProcessOutputPoller.vitest.ts`) had defined its own private `delay()` function, which is removed entirely.

**Files updated:** `UsageLogService.ts` (production) + 10 test-kernel files across agent, auth, cli, desktop, progressView, settings, tools, and transcript suites.

- [ ] `npm run typecheck` — requires full dev-dep install (blocked in sandbox); changes are type-safe by inspection (`ensureArray<T>` preserves the generic and `delay` signature is identical to `setTimeout`-based pattern)

author: fortmarek
body:
## Incident: CI docker down fleet-wide

Controller `0.8.0` was deployed to **production** at ~17:37 UTC (via a `server-deployment.yml` workflow_dispatch, `✓ Deploy to tuist`). Since then, server CI `Test` jobs fail immediately at `Initialize containers`:

```
docker version --format '{{.Server.APIVersion}}'
failed to connect to the docker API at unix:///var/run/docker.sock ... no such file or directory
```

The dind sidecar isn't coming up in new runner pods, so there's no docker for jobs that use service containers.

## Root cause

`0.8.0`'s **only** change to the runner pod template is the dind `--registry-mirror=https://mirror.gcr.io` flag from [#11096](https://github.com/tuist/tuist/pull/11096) (the other `0.8.0` changes are autoscaler logic, which doesn't touch the template). Adding the flag changed the dockerd command, hence the pod-template hash, churning the fleet onto new pods. The new pods' dind sidecar never produced `/var/run/docker.sock`.

Empirical timeline (server.yml `Test` job):

| Time (UTC) | docker | note |
|---|---|---|
| 17:28 | ✅ works | still on pre-`0.8.0` pods |
| ~17:37 | — | `0.8.0` finishes rolling to prod |
| 17:50, 20:41, 20:55, 21:05 | ❌ socket missing | 100% of jobs reaching the docker step |

The consistency (not intermittent) is the tell that it's the controller change, not transient rate-limit starvation.

Most likely mechanism: the fleet-wide pod churn forced a re-pull storm of `docker:28-dind`, which hits the **containerd-layer** Docker Hub pull that the dockerd mirror does not cover, so sidecars land in `ImagePullBackOff`. (Confirm on a stuck pod: `kubectl -n tuist-runners describe pod <pod>` — `ImagePullBackOff`/`toomanyrequests` on `docker:28-dind` vs `CrashLoopBackOff` if dockerd rejected the flag.)

## What this PR does

Pin `runnersController.image.tag` back to the known-good `0.7.0`. The deployed controller reverts to the working pod template.

**Pin-only on purpose:** `values-managed-common.yaml` is not under `infra/runners-controller/**`, so this triggers no controller release — it just redeploys `0.7.0`.

**Side effect:** `0.7.0` predates the `0.8.0` autoscaler/fleet-allocation refactor; that reships with the next clean controller release.

## Deploy

Use the path that worked at 17:37: a `server-deployment.yml` workflow_dispatch to production (the full production cascade has been failing on the separate `canary / Platform chart` "lost communication" issue). The `Build server image` step is already on `ubuntu-latest`, so it won't hit the rate limit.

## ⚠️ Follow-up required (or this rollback gets undone)

The `--registry-mirror` flag is **still in main's `podtemplate.go`**. The next controller release will rebuild it and rebump this pin, re-breaking the fleet. Before any controller release:
1. Revert (or guard) the flag in `podtemplate.go`, and
2. Reship the mirror only once the containerd-layer `docker:28-dind` pull is also mirrored/authed (host containerd mirror, Docker Hub auth on the fleet, or a pre-pulled/baked sidecar image) so deploy-time pod churn can't trip the rate limit.

## Validation

YAML parses. Single-line pin change (`0.8.0` → `0.7.0`) plus a guard comment.

author: ninyawee
body:
Lay i18n infrastructure where each language lives in its **own source file**, routed per language rather than toggled client-side.

## Design (locked via decisions)
- **Routed per language** — primary language at bare `/blog/<slug>`, alternates at `/blog/<slug>/<lang>`. No duplicate-content URLs.
- **Folder per post** — `<slug>/en.svx` + `<slug>/th.svx`.
- **EN + TH, default TH** — when a post has both, the bare URL serves Thai.

## What's in here
- **i18n core** (`src/lib/i18n.ts`) — `Lang`, `DEFAULT_LANG=th`, `primaryLang()`, `postPath()`.
- **Loader** (`posts.ts` / `types.ts`) — discovers both flat `<slug>.svx` (legacy single-lang) and folder `<slug>/<lang>.svx` (multilingual); groups by slug, exposes `langs[]`.
- **Routing** — `[slug]` → `[slug]/[[lang]]` (optional param) with `canonical` + `hreflang` alternates and a per-article `lang` attribute.
- **LanguageSwitcher** — link-based (each language is its own prerendered URL, not a client toggle).
- **Migrated all three bilingual posts** off inline `{#if lang}` toggles into separate-source folders — `until-we-reach-shared-understanding`, `gh-x-html`, `in-html` — each with its own per-language frontmatter (Thai titles/descriptions for the `th` variants).

## Verification (static build)
- bare URL → TH, `/en` → EN for each post
- `canonical` + `hreflang` correct in each `<head>` (1 canonical + 2 alternates; nothing leaks into the body)
- all inline imagetools assets bundle per page
- legacy flat posts unaffected (no stray lang dirs); all 18 posts prerender
- `bun run check` clean for all new/changed files (pre-existing gsap `onMount` typings in untouched blog components remain)

## Follow-ups (out of scope)
- Root `<html lang>` stays static; per-page it's set on the `<article>`. Making the root dynamic needs a `transformPageChunk` hook.
- RSS still emits one item per post in its primary language with a hardcoded `<language>en</language>`.

## Problem

The Spring Boot app fails to start with "Driver org.postgresql.Driver claims to not accept jdbcUrl, postgresql://..." because Railway's DATABASE_URL begins with `postgresql://`, but the JDBC driver requires the full `jdbc:postgresql://` scheme.

## Solution

Updated `spring.datasource.url` in `application.properties` to prepend `jdbc:` before the URL, using `DATABASE_URL` as the primary source with a fallback to the individual `PG*` variables for local development. When `DATABASE_URL` is set (as Railway does), the result is `jdbc:postgresql://...`; when it is absent, the existing `PGHOST`/`PGPORT`/`PGDATABASE` construction is used unchanged.

### Changes
- **Modified** `backend/src/main/resources/application.properties`

author: v3ron
body:
## What is this?

This PR removes Voltra's direct need for `@babel/plugin-transform-export-namespace-from` in React Native CLI projects. The iOS and Android package entrypoints keep exporting the same `Voltra` and `VoltraAndroid` namespaces, but no longer use the `export * as` syntax that requires that Babel transform.

## How does it work?

The package entrypoints now import their primitives barrels as namespace objects and re-export those bindings explicitly. The root Babel config and direct dev dependency on the namespace export transform are removed because Voltra source no longer uses that syntax.

## Why is this useful?

React Native CLI apps can consume Voltra without needing to install or configure an extra Babel plugin for namespace exports. The public package API stays the same while the Babel setup becomes simpler and less fragile.

body:
## Summary Three navigation / interaction upgrades requested: 1. **External-link icon** (small `↗` SVG) next to "App" in the navbar, plus `target="_blank"` so it opens in a new tab on every page. 2. **Hamburger menu** for mobile (<720px) with all five destinations — Launch Site, Team, RITMO DNA, App (external), Impressum. 3. **Fade-in / fade-out animations** using **Motion One** — the vanilla-JS sibling of Framer Motion (same author, same `animate` / `inView` API). The site has no build step, so real React-only Framer Motion isn't feasible; Motion One delivers the same animation language as an ES module from JSDelivr. ## `motion.js` — what it does Loaded on every page via `` and respects `prefers-reduced-motion` throughout. 1. **Page-exit fade-out** — intercepts clicks on internal links, fades `` opacity 1 → 0 over 250ms with `ease-out`, then navigates. Skips: external URLs, `target="_blank"`, `mailto:` / `tel:`, anchor links (`#…`), cmd/ctrl/shift/alt-clicks, non-primary mouse buttons. 2. **Scroll-triggered fade-in** — every `section.sect` after the first one starts hidden (`opacity:0` + `translateY(28px)` applied via JS so no-JS fallback shows content), and animates in via `inView(...)` when 12% visible. 700ms with the brand easing `[0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1]`. 3. **Hamburger toggle** — `aria-expanded` / `aria-hidden` flip, body scroll lock, overlay fade-in, staggered `translateX(-16px → 0)` entrance for each nav item with 60ms per-item delay. ## Markup pattern (added to all five pages) ```html
Launch Site Team RITMO DNA App Impressum
``` The active page is marked with `aria-current="page"` per page (Launch / Team / DNA / Impressum), styled orange in the mobile nav. ## New CSS in `styles.css` - `.nav-external` + `.ext-icon` — inline-flex with 5px gap, icon at 55% opacity (100% on hover), 10×10px in the navbar, 16×16px in the mobile menu next to the larger italic type. - `.burger` — 32×24 button with three absolutely-positioned `` lines that morph to an X via `top` + `transform: rotate(±45deg)`. `display: none` by default, `display: block` below 720px. - `.nav-mobile` — `position: fixed; top: 88px; inset:0` overlay with the page background, large italic links (`clamp(28px, 7vw, 40px)`), 24px vertical padding per item, hairline dividers, `padding-left` shift on hover, active item in orange. - `body.nav-open` locks scroll and hides the Bauhaus bottom strip so the menu reads as one clean panel. ## Reviewer notes - **No-JS fallback**: page navigation and scrolling still work without `motion.js`. Sections that would scroll-reveal stay visible because we apply the initial hidden state via JS, not CSS. The burger becomes inert (footer nav remains the no-JS fallback for mobile users). - **Why Motion One and not Framer Motion**: Framer Motion is React-only. Motion One (motion.dev) is by the same author, ships ESM, and the `animate` / `inView` / easing-array API is intentionally identical, so the code style reads the same. Added to `CLAUDE.md` so this is documented for future sessions. - The desktop nav still does **not** show Impressum (per the earlier change). The mobile menu **does** include Impressum so mobile users don't have to scroll to the footer. - All external `ritmopadel.app` links in the navbar and footer now open in a new tab. CTA buttons elsewhere on the page (e.g. the App pillar card on the home page) were intentionally **not** modified in this PR — flag if a wider sweep is wanted. ## Test plan - [ ] Open `index.html`; click "App" in the navbar — opens in a new tab, original tab stays put. - [ ] Look at "App" in nav: small `↗` icon visible at ~55% opacity, brightens on hover. - [ ] Click `Launch Site` in the navbar: body fades to black, page navigates to `launch.html`. - [ ] Cmd-click (Mac) or Ctrl-click `Launch Site`: opens in new tab, no fade animation triggered. - [ ] Click an in-page anchor (e.g. `#archetypes` on the DNA page): no fade animation. - [ ] Resize browser to <720px: desktop nav disappears, hamburger appears in its place. - [ ] Tap hamburger: lines morph to X, full-screen menu fades in, nav items stagger in left-to-right. - [ ] Tap any item in the open menu: closes menu, navigates with fade. - [ ] Open menu, press `Escape`: menu closes, focus returns to burger. - [ ] Scroll down on the DNA page: sections below the fold fade/slide in as they enter view. - [ ] In macOS / iOS, enable "Reduce Motion" → reload → confirm fades are skipped (instant), but burger menu still toggles. - [ ] Block CDN (DevTools → Network → block `cdn.jsdelivr.net`) → reload → confirm pages still navigate normally and content is visible; burger no longer toggles (acceptable — footer is the fallback). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jakechampion
body:
## Summary

Fixes a miscompile: an array literal of variant structs assigned to a **union-typed** array didn't tag-wrap its elements.

```fern
struct A { x: i32 } struct B { y: i32 } type N = A | B;
var xs: N[] = [A { x: 5 }, B { y: 7 }];   // elements stored as bare, un-tagged structs
match (xs[0]) { A(a) => …, B(b) => … }    // misfires
```

The checker's `ArrayLit` case never applied the implicit union wrap (`maybeWrapForUnion`) that a single `var n: N = A { … }`, a `return`, and an `arr.push(A { … })` argument all get. So elements were stored as raw structs without a variant tag, and a later `match` broke — the interpreter reported `match scrutinee is *interp.Struct, expected enum value`, and the native backends **segfaulted**. The `.push` path was unaffected because it coerces through the Call-argument path.

## Fix

When an array literal's element-type hint is a union enum, wrap each element via `maybeWrapForUnion` (a no-op for elements that are already enum values or don't match a variant — so explicit-enum arrays like `Box[] = [Val(…), None]` and generic `Option[string][]` are unchanged).

This also makes a **mixed-variant** literal `[A { … }, B { … }]` type-check — previously rejected with `E034 array element type B, expected A` because the element type was inferred from the first element only.

## How it surfaced

Found while building self-hosted map iteration (PR #2029): a synthesized `[ExprIdent{…}, ExprIdent{…}]` over the parser's `Expr` union hit this and made a later `match` in `build_stmt` misfire. That PR worked around it with `.push`; this fixes the root cause.

## Tests

`internal/e2e/union_array_literal_test.go` — mixed- and same-variant union array literals, read back through a `match`, on x86-64 + arm64 + wasm (returns a 0/99 value-check sentinel that survives the 8-bit exit code).

Full `internal/e2e` suite green; `internal/checker`, `internal/ir`, `internal/interp` unit tests green.

author: blamechris
body:
## Summary

Defines the **wire contract** for the Control Room activity tree in `@chroxy/protocol` — the foundation the server emitter (#5160), store-core reducer (#5162), and dashboard panel (#5163) all build on. Schema-only; no emitter / reducer / UI here.

### Activity entry shape
One node in the per-session activity tree:
- `id` — stable server-assigned id (deltas reference it; survives status flips)
- `kind` — `'agent'` (Task subagent) | `'shell'` (backgrounded Bash) | `'tool'`
- `label` — human-readable description (may be empty when not yet known)
- `status` — `'running'` | `'blocked'` | `'done'` | `'failed'`
- `startedAt` — server wall-clock ms epoch (server clock, not client)
- `endedAt?` — set iff terminal (`done`/`failed`)
- `parentId?` — session→agent→tool hierarchy; absent = top-level
- `outputRef?` — `{ kind: 'tool_use' | 'shell' | 'message', id }` to locate the live output stream (reuses existing `agent_event` / background-shell / `stream_delta` channels)

### Messages
- **`activity_snapshot`** — full current tree for a session (subscribe/resync). Flat `entries` array; empty array is the valid no-activity state. Mirrors the `background_work_changed` full-snapshot philosophy so a late joiner is canonical in one message.
- **`activity_delta`** — incremental `started` / `updated` / `ended` change. Carries the **full entry** per op (not a partial patch) so the reducer is trivial and each delta self-heals against a dropped earlier one.

### Safety / compat
- `superRefine` guards: `endedAt` required iff terminal, forbidden while running/blocked, `endedAt >= startedAt`; an `ended` delta must carry a terminal entry.
- `schemaVersion` (`ACTIVITY_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`) on both messages + Zod's default unknown-field stripping, so older clients ignore newer payloads gracefully and unknown message types are skipped at the dispatch layer.
- Exported Zod schemas + inferred TS types, pinned as a public contract at the package entry point.

### Tests / coverage
- Added a `Control Room activity tree (#5161)` block to `schemas.test.js` (entry refinements, all kinds/statuses, snapshot/delta happy + reject paths, forward-compat field stripping).
- Documented both messages in the `ws-server.js` Server→Client contract and added them to `INTENTIONALLY_UNHANDLED` in `handler-coverage.test.js` (handlers land with #5162/#5163).
- `tsc` clean; `packages/protocol` tests green (183 pass).

Closes #5161
Part of #5159

author: xenon010101
body:
## Description
Sanitizes HTTP error responses to prevent internal exception details from leaking to API clients. All error details are now logged server-side with `logger.error(exc_info=...)`, while clients receive generic, user-safe messages.

## Changes
- **backend/main.py** — 5 exception sites fixed:
  - `POST /tickets`: `detail=str(e)` → generic failed-to-create message
  - `POST /ai/analyze_ticket`: `detail=str(e)` → generic analysis-failed message (with logging)
  - `GET /auth/me` (session check): `detail=f"Invalid session: {exc}"` → `"Invalid session"` (with logging)
  - `POST /auth/login`: `detail=str(exc)` → `"Invalid credentials"` (with logging)
  - `POST /auth/signup`: `detail=str(exc)` → generic signup-failed message (with logging)
- Added module-level `logger` for structured error logging

## Security Impact
- **Before**: An attacker sending malformed tokens or requests received stack traces, Supabase query details, and internal paths
- **After**: All errors return generic messages; details go to server logs only

Closes #1780

author: konboi
body:
## Why

When Robot Framework tests are organized in subdirectories (e.g. `tests/robot/api/*.robot`), the `parse_func` in `robot.py` was assigning the **directory-level suite name** (e.g. `Api`, `Integration`) as the `classname` instead of the **file-level suite name** (e.g. `Auth`, `Comments`).

This caused the server-side `RobotFrameworkResolver` to fail because it tries to match `Api` → `api.robot`, which doesn't exist. The actual files are `auth.robot`, `comments.robot`, etc.

## What

Added a `find_leaf_suites` helper inside `parse_func` that recursively traverses the suite hierarchy until it reaches leaf suites (suites that contain `<test>` elements directly but no child `<suite>` elements). Only leaf suites — which correspond to individual `.robot` files — are passed to `parse_suite`, ensuring the correct file-level suite name is used as `classname`.

Before:
```xml
<testcase classname="Api" name="Register New User Successfully"/>
```

After:
```xml
<testcase classname="Auth" name="Register New User Successfully"/>
```

Also updated test fixtures (`output.xml`, `record_test_result.json`) to cover both flat (2-level) and nested (3-level) suite structures.

## Please Review Here

- `find_leaf_suites` is recursive and handles any depth (2, 3, 4+ levels), verified by the updated `output.xml` which mixes 2-level and 3-level structures in the same run.
- `test_record_test_legacy` was already failing on `v1` before this change (token/org mismatch in mock setup) — not related to this fix.

author: dduportal
body:
Ref. https://github.com/jenkins-infra/helpdesk/issues/5093#issuecomment-4591903553

As we want to get rid of ASDF, this PR changes the installation of NodeJS on Ubuntu to the official binaries:

- Per CPU architecture and specific pinned version is used
- The GPG keyring of the NodeJS project is added in the repository to verify the download
- Not only NPM is installed globally, but also Yarn and PNPM (caching them so less downloads per builds, assuming it's part of the default NodeJS installation)
- Note about the `PATH`: since calls to `npm install -g ...` are adding the installed binaries in the same `$node_install_dir/bin` as `npm`, we have no other choice than adding this `bin` directory to the `PATH`. As such, the same technique is used as `go`:
  - The `/etc/environment` file holds the new `PATH`: this will be used by VM agents where we connect using SSH and non-interactive shell.
  - The `Dockerfile` is appended with the proper `ENV` values: Kubernetes and Docker agents will have the `PATH` set up through this technique

=> This `PATH` change required to update the `playwright` global installation and the `goss` tests (they were assuming ASDF for NodeJS/NPM)

## 概述

添加新技能 stp-pfc-reservoir-goal-planning，源自 arXiv:2606.03481 论文。

### 论文信息
- **标题**: Short-Term Synaptic Plasticity Stabilizes Goal-Conditioned Dynamics in a PFC-Inspired Reservoir Model for Multistep Goal-Directed Action Planning
- **作者**: Jin Nakamura, Yuichi Katori
- **领域**: Quantitative Biology > Neurons and Cognition (q-bio.NC)
- **发布日期**: 2026-06-02

### 核心贡献
1. **STP鲁棒性提升**: 在噪声条件下，STP组保持89.2%成功率（vs 无STP组49.5%，Cohen's dz=1.31）
2. **目标条件化动力学**: STP通过动态调制目标依赖的有效递归连接，将静态目标表示转化为行动可用的动力学
3. **反驳固定增益假设**: 实验证明STP效果源于在线历史依赖的突触调制，而非简单增益调整
4. **时间尺度优化**: 易化主导时间常数（τ_facil > τ_rec）匹配行为延迟时长（500ms-1s）

body:
## Phase 4c — Team & Roles/Permissions UI

Builds on Phase 4b (which enforces RBAC). Because the policies read **live DB permissions**, this UI plugs straight in — owners can now run their own staff and customise what each role can do, per client.

### 1. Team management — `/manage/operators`
- List, **invite**, and edit operator staff (the shared `User` model, scoped to `type=operator` in this client).
- Invites reuse the existing operator onboarding: temp password emailed (`OperatorCredentialsIssuedNotification`) + forced change on first sign-in.
- Set each member's **role**; deactivate via **status** (no hard-deletes of a login).
- **Gated by `team.manage`** (owner + manager).
- Safeguards: only an **owner** can grant the owner role (a manager can't mint owners); you **can't change your own role/status** (no self-lockout).

### 2. Roles & Permissions — `/manage/role-permissions`
- **Owner-only** page: a grid of View/Manage toggles per area for `manager` / `accountant` / `maintenance-staff`.
- Saves to **this client's** roles; takes effect immediately (policies read it live). Owner is always full and isn't shown.
- Defaults come from the approved matrix; fully customisable per client.

### Plumbing
- New **`team.manage`** permission (owner + manager); migration creates it and backfills existing clients' roles. New clients via `ClientObserver`.
- Both pages live under an **"Administration"** nav group.

### Testing it yourself
`/demo-seed/manage`, password `demo1234`:
- `owner@demo-seed.local` — sees **Team** + **Roles & Permissions**; can invite staff, change roles, and toggle each role's permissions.
- `manager@demo-seed.local` — sees **Team** (can invite/manage) but **not** Roles & Permissions.
- `accountant@` / `maintenance-staff@` — see neither.

Try: as owner, open **Roles & Permissions**, untick something for Accountant, save; sign in as the accountant and see it gone.

### Gate
- `sail pest` — **130 passed** (7 new: access gating per role + invite flow + permission-save)
- `sail pint` — clean · `sail phpstan` — no new errors (27 baseline)
- Migration applied to dev; demo re-seeded.

### Deploy note
Has a migration — run `php artisan migrate --force` after deploy (adds `team.manage` + backfills).

body:
## Resumen

Segunda parte de **Fase 2 (integridad de datos)** — tras el enum `EstadoRendicion` (#31).

### 1. Dinero en Decimal
El total de la orden de compra se acumulaba en punto flotante (`Number * Number`) antes de envolverse en `Prisma.Decimal`, con posible desfase de centavos respecto a los totales por ítem. Ahora se suma con `Prisma.Decimal` de extremo a extremo.

### 2. Soft-delete en lecturas
- `PartidasService.findAll` y `GruposService.findAll` no filtraban `deletedAt:null` → devolvían registros eliminados a los selectores en cadena. Corregido.
- `rendiciones.findOne` / `findBySolicitudId` pasan de `findUnique` a `findFirst` con `solicitud.deletedAt:null`, igual que `findAll`, para no exponer rendiciones de solicitudes eliminadas.

### 3. Centralización de constante crítica
`ESTADOS_COMPROMISO_ACTIVO` estaba duplicada (idéntica) en `poa.service`, `solicitudes.service` y `dashboard.service` — regla crítica del cálculo de saldo con riesgo de drift. Movida a `common/constants/financial.constants`.

### Verificación
- Lint limpio. Suite en verde (3 suites / 23 tests). Backend recompila y responde 200 (smoke-check en watch).

### Pendiente de Fase 2 (consistencia, menor)
`deletedAt` en `Rendicion`, `createdAt`/`updatedAt` faltantes y estandarización de `onDelete` — cambios de schema de menor valor; se pueden abordar después.

author: siddseethepalli
body:
## Summary
- macOS refetched the full paginated conversation list (~80 `GET /v1/conversations` requests across 3 parallel streams over 10k+ conversations) on *any* conversation sync tag, including the narrow per-conversation `metadata`/`messages` tags the daemon sends precisely to avoid full refetches. A few content-only changes per minute (seen/rename/attention, fired every turn) exhausted the daemon's 300 req/min per-IP limit and 429'd the whole app (all endpoints share one loopback bucket).
- Narrow `conversationMetadata` tags now patch a single row via `GET /v1/conversations/:id` (`ConversationDetailClient`) + an in-place merge mirroring the existing-row path in `appendConversations`/`handleConversationListResponse` (preserves local identity, archive state, and optimistic titles).
- `conversationMessages` tags no longer trigger a list refetch — only the active conversation's history is reconciled. Only the broad `conversationList` tag (created/deleted/reordered) still does a full refetch.
- Cold-start drain and `ConversationListStore` "load more" paths are unchanged.

## Original prompt
While investigating 429s from the daemon when running the macOS Swift app, we traced them to a `GET /v1/conversations` storm: the per-IP limiter (`rate-limiter.ts`, 300 req/min authenticated) was being exhausted because the macOS client did a full paginated list refetch on every conversation sync invalidation — amplified ~80x by pagination over 10k+ conversations. This is fix #1 of the plan: route the narrow per-conversation tags to a single-row fetch-and-patch so only genuine list-shape changes refetch the list.

author: rockfordlhotka
body:
## Why

Two related failures let `rockbot-agent` consume unbounded resources with nothing stopping it.

### 1. Non-terminating tool-result trim loop (the 2026-06-05 incident) — new in this PR

**Symptom (from the on-call investigation):** the agent pod pegged at ~2 cores with **407,597 identical "Trimmed tool result … (head 120, tail 80)" log lines in a 5-minute window**, re-processing the same ~5 call IDs forever. Every MCP session starved (todo was just the one the user noticed); the downstream MCP services were provably healthy. 0 restarts, 42h uptime → in-memory wedge. `kubectl delete pod` cleared it, but that's a band-aid.

**Root cause:** `TrimLargeToolResultsAsync` looped on `while(true)` until the estimated context fit the char budget, always re-trimming the single largest tool result. When the **non-tool** content alone (system prompt + injected skill bodies + the stash registry) already exceeded the budget, *and* every tool result was already at the ~200-char elision floor — where re-adding the elision marker keeps a result the same size or **larger** — the total never dropped below budget and the loop spun forever. (`head 120 / tail 80` is exactly the 200-char floor at the default `0.6` head ratio — the fingerprint of a loop stuck on floor-sized results.)

**Fix:** three independent termination guarantees —
1. stop when the budget is met (unchanged);
2. **stop when the largest tool result can no longer shrink** — since we always pick the largest, nothing smaller can reach the budget either;
3. a hard pass cap as defence-in-depth.

Also clamps the legacy slice length so the 200-char floor can't index past a short result and throw.

**De-duplication (requested in review):** the trim loop existed as two byte-identical copies — the native `RockBotFunctionInvokingChatClient` path and the text-based `AgentLoopRunner` path — that had already drifted. Both are now thin forwarders to a single canonical `ToolResultTrimmer.TrimAsync`, so this class of bug can't be half-fixed again.

### 2. Append-only JSONL log growth — earlier commits on this branch

A shared dream-driven retention pass caps the append-only JSONL logs, wired to k8s config, plus line-trimming of persistent session files.

## Tests

- Two new `[Timeout]` regression tests reproduce the wedge (huge non-tool content + a tiny budget) and **hang on the old loop, pass on the new one**.
- All `AgentLoopRunnerTrimStashTests` pass (11/11), confirming the head+tail+stash behaviour is unchanged for the normal trim path.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

The investigation surfaced adjacent gaps worth separate work: `spawn_wisps` results embed fresh GUIDs, so `RepetitiveToolCallDetector` (keyed on tool+args+result) never fires for wisp dispatch; there's no cross-loop/cross-session circuit breaker on wisp volume; and `FileWispExecutionLog.ReadAllAsync` re-parses the entire JSONL on every successful wisp (O(n²) under load).

author: smallwei0301
body:
## Summary

GH-1233 reports the **same** `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON` from `next/core-web-vitals` extend as GH-1195, but on a different env (daily check `/root/.openclaw/workspace/tour-platform` running node v24 + npm 11), ~8 hours after my [PR #1210](https://github.com/smallwei0301/tour-platform/pull/1210) merged.

Why my #1210 fix didn't catch it: the source-contract guard locked `major(eslint-config-next) === major(next)` in `apps/web/package.json`, but that's a **declared range** (`^15.5.3`). A different env with stale `node_modules` / npm cache / different peer-dep resolution can still install 16.x somehow. The source-level major-version pin doesn't prevent that.

This PR adds an actual lockdown: `overrides` in root `package.json` forcing `eslint-config-next` to exactly `15.5.15`. npm `overrides` (supported by npm 8.3+) apply to **all** resolution paths regardless of declared range, so even a clean `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` on node v24 + npm 11 must resolve to 15.5.15.

## Closes
- Closes #1233

## Changes (3 files, +34/-1)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | Add `overrides.eslint-config-next: "15.5.15"` |
| `package-lock.json` | Regenerated via `npm install --package-lock-only` so the constraint is embedded. Resolved version unchanged at 15.5.15. npm 10 also auto-added `engines: {"node":">=22"}` echoes to root + apps/web blocks and bumped the `eslint` range marker from `^9.37.0` → `^9.39.4` (matches installed 9.39.4) — both benign side effects, no security/runtime impact. |
| `apps/web/tests/api/issue1195-eslint-config-next-version-pin.test.mjs` | Extend the GH-1195 guard with a new GH-1233 assertion: root `package.json` must have `overrides.eslint-config-next` set, and its major must match next major. Any future PR that removes the override fails this test BEFORE lint breaks in CI. |

## Validation

```
$ npm run lint -w @tour/web
> ESLINT_USE_FLAT_CONFIG=false eslint app src --ignore-pattern '.next/**'
(only the legacy-rc deprecation warning — exit 0)

$ npm run typecheck -w @tour/web
> tsc --noEmit (exit 0)

$ node --test apps/web/tests/api/issue1195-eslint-config-next-version-pin.test.mjs
  ✓ apps/web package.json declares both `next` and `eslint-config-next`
  ✓ eslint-config-next major version matches next major version
  ✓ apps/web/.eslintrc.json still extends next/core-web-vitals
  ✓ GH-1233 — root package.json overrides pins eslint-config-next to a 15.x version
  4/4 PASS  (was 3/3 before #1233)
```

## Risk

Low. Override pins `eslint-config-next` to a SPECIFIC patch version (15.5.15) which is what we're already running. Anyone in a fresh env will get the same version we tested with. Anyone who wants to bump to a new 15.x patch will be forced to update the override AND the test override-major assertion, which forces a conscious decision.

## Out of scope

- Migrating `.eslintrc.json` to ESLint flat config (separate effort; the deprecation warning is logged but not blocking)
- Bumping Next to 16.x (out of cycle; would require updating the override version + reviewing 16.x ESLint compat)
- Root cause analysis of why the daily-check env had 16.x installed — out of our control; the override makes the question moot

## Safety

No production / runtime / database / payment / refund / settlement mutation. The change is a dependency-resolution constraint in build-tooling layer only.

Refs #1195, PR #1210

author: doka-nt
body:
## Summary

Fixes the macOS auto-update "Restart" action, which hid the app window instead of
installing the update.

## Root cause

`autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()` closes the main window to apply a staged update. The
window's `close` handler (`src/main/index.ts`) hides the window when `isQuitting` is
`false` (the app's hide-on-close / hotkey-toggle behavior). Because the updater quit
path never set `isQuitting`, clicking **Перезапустить** only hid the window
(restorable via the global show/hide hotkey) and the update never installed.

## Fix

- `update:install` now flips `isQuitting` via `beginQuit()` **before** the updater
  closes the window on the next tick, so the `close` handler quits + installs
  instead of hiding.
- It does so **only when an install actually starts**: `quitAndInstall()` now
  returns `boolean`, so a no-op call (no update downloaded) never leaves the app in
  a half-quitting state.

Minimal, targeted change in the main process; no renderer changes.

## Checks

- `npm run typecheck` ✅
- `npm run lint` ✅
- `npm test` ✅ (381 passed)
- `npm run build` ✅

## Manual QA

The updater is gated to packaged, signed macOS release builds
(`isUpdateSupported()` excludes dev/unsigned `0.0.0` builds), so the
quit-and-install path cannot be exercised in `npm run dev`. Runtime verification
requires a signed release pair (an older signed build offered a newer release):

1. Launch an older signed build; let it download the update; the "ready to install"
   banner appears.
2. Click **Перезапустить** → app quits and relaunches into the new version (no
   leftover hidden window restorable by the hotkey).
3. Confirm the running version matches the offered update and the banner no longer
   appears.

Note: closing the window (red traffic-light / `Cmd+W`) intentionally **hides** the
app (resident hotkey-toggle window); installing an update is done via **Перезапустить**.

Fixes #136

author: joshbermanssw
body:
## TL;DR

PageSpeed mobile flags the event pages at **Performance 36** with **1,650 ms Total Blocking Time** and ~3.2 MB of unused JS — driven by heavy client code loaded eagerly on every page, not by page content. This defers or trims the worst offenders (App Insights, framer-motion, GTM) so they stay off the critical path, plus two small content fixes.

**Files to review (7, behaviour-preserving):**

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `context/app-insight-client.tsx` *(start here)* | Dynamic-import the heavy `applicationinsights-web` core on idle; lightweight React plugin/context stays synchronous so `WebVitals` + error boundary keep working. |
| `components/layout/v2ComponentWrapper.tsx` | Replace framer-motion `useInView` with a small `IntersectionObserver` hook — drops the 2.9 MB package from the wrapper around every v2 block. |
| `app/components/deferred-gtm.tsx` *(new)* | Loads GTM on first interaction or idle, with a guaranteed ~3.5 s fallback. |
| `app/layout.tsx` | Swap `<GoogleTagManager>` for `<DeferredGoogleTagManager>`. |
| `components/blocks/imageComponents/ImageComponentLayout.tsx` | `sizes` cap `min(50vw, 640px)` to stop oversized image fetches. |
| `helpers/getTrimmedEvents.ts` | Guard null/empty slug so no `/events/null` link is prefetched. |
| `app/providers/query-provider.tsx` | `ReactQueryDevtools` → dynamic dev-only import. |

## Why

The page render chain itself is clean — the cost is global/eager client code. Confirmed in-repo: App Insights is instantiated in the root layout on every page; framer-motion is pulled into the wrapper that wraps every block just for one hook; and GTM (which injects Clarity, Hotjar, LinkedIn, FB Pixel) loads `afterInteractive`, contributing ~595 ms of third-party main-thread time.

## How

Each change moves work off the first-load critical path without changing behaviour:

- **App Insights / GTM / devtools** — same code runs, just later (on idle / interaction / dev-only), so they leave the initial bundle and main thread.
- **framer-motion** — the new hook reproduces `useInView(ref, { once: true, margin })` semantics via `IntersectionObserver` `rootMargin`; SSR/no-IO falls back to visible.
- **Images / `/events/null`** — pure correctness: tighter responsive `sizes`, and a slug guard that falls back to `/events`.

## Reviewer notes

- **GTM timing shifts.** Tags fire up to ~3.5 s later (usually sooner). Pageviews still captured for every session via the guaranteed idle/timeout fallback; no code depends on `sendGTMEvent`/`dataLayer`. Dial down `3500` if sub-second tag timing matters.
- **App Insights context intact.** Only the web SDK is lazy; the `ReactPlugin` context is provided immediately, and consumers call it null-safely.
- **Image cap is CSS-px.** Browser still picks the right candidate by DPR, so retina stays crisp; only oversized wide-screen fetches shrink.

## Tests

`tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint clean on changed files, `jest` 13/13 pass. No runtime/behaviour change to verify beyond the deferral timing above.

## Follow-up

Confirm the named 1.9 MB chunk with `BUNDLE_ANALYSE=true pnpm build` (analyzer already wired in `next.config.mjs`) — these fixes target the most likely contributors (App Insights, framer-motion), but the treemap will show anything else.

author: damien-robotsix
body:
## Why
The board's `/tickets` cost column was kept non-zero by a perpetual backend daemon (`_cost_warmer_loop` + `_cost_warmer_fast_loop`) that hit Langfuse for **every open ticket on a timer, forever** — gated, oddly, by a per-repo `.robotsix-mill/periodic/cost_warmer.yaml` presence file. That's a UI-display concern in the wrong layer: it runs even when nobody's viewing the board, and newly-registered repos silently miss the cost column until they ship the file.

## What
Demand-driven warming. The `/tickets` list route (which the board already polls every 5s) serves cost **cache-only** for speed, then fire-and-forgets a **background** warm of exactly the rows it just returned (`runtime/cost_warm.py`). The cache fills within a poll cycle, only for visible tickets, only while someone's watching, with **no backend timer** — and **every registered repo is covered automatically** (no presence file needed).

```
GET /tickets → cache-only costs (fast) → bg: warm those ids
next poll (5s) → cache warm → real $ shown
```

- **Removed:** both worker loops + fields/start/stop wiring; the `cost_warmer_*` Settings; the `cost_warmer`/`cost_warmer_fast` periodic_loader kinds; the `cost_warmer.yaml` presence file; the old daemon test.
- **Added:** `warm_ticket_costs` (single-flight lock so overlapping polls don't pile up threads; bounded thread pool) + tests. Updated the two cache-only API tests for the new background warm.

## Tests
Full `tests/runtime/` (382) + config + periodic_loader + bespoke_supervisor + new `test_cost_warm.py`: green. Ruff clean. Docker image builds.

## Problem
On the PIN-login page, "Sign in with your account" (SSO) failed for tenant admins and platform admins: they completed SSO successfully but landed **back on the PIN keypad** with no way forward.

## Root cause
Both SSO buttons passed `window.location.href` (the pin-login URL) as the post-login `returnTo`. After SSO, the callback/select-outlet redirected straight back to pin-login — a kiosk page that `AuthProvider` deliberately never advances, and that the org root (`/[orgSlug]`) also redirects into. So an authenticated SSO session had no path off the keypad.

## Fix
- Point both SSO buttons' `returnTo` at `/[orgSlug]/dashboard`.
- Add a guard that forwards an already-authenticated **non-terminal** (SSO) session off the kiosk to the dashboard; terminal PIN sessions stay put.

author: minorstep
body:
## Skill Improvement ($50-150 Bounty)

/claim #1027

### Skill Modified
**Skill name:** `iam-review`
**Skill path:** `skills/identity/iam-review/`

### What Was Wrong
Issue #1027 notes that the IAM review skill covered broad least-privilege checks, but did not force reviewers to prove cloud-specific privilege escalation paths or distinguish bounded wildcard permissions from exploitable access. That can miss `iam:PassRole` plus workload creation, Azure/Entra guest over-permissioning, GCP `actAs` chains, and long-lived/chained temporary credentials, while also over-reporting wildcard actions that are constrained by organization conditions or equivalent guardrails.

Fixes #1027.

### What This PR Fixes
- Adds cloud escalation checks for AWS `iam:PassRole`, `sts:AssumeRole`, policy-version, inline-policy, access-key, and service-linked-role edge cases.
- Adds Azure / Entra ID checks for guest privileged reach, app-registration credential ownership, managed identity overreach, PIM activation controls, and cross-tenant access settings.
- Adds GCP checks for `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs`, token creator grants, primitive roles, and broad Workload Identity Federation trust.
- Adds a false-positive guard so wildcard actions are not treated as exploitable when resources, organization conditions, permission boundaries, SCPs, PIM controls, or service-linked constraints prevent escalation.
- Expands severity guidance and the output schema with explicit escalation path and compensating-control fields.
- Updates the skill version and version history.

### Evidence

**Before (skill misses this):**
```json
{
  "Action": ["iam:PassRole", "ec2:RunInstances"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
A reviewer could classify this as only broad IAM access without documenting the privilege escalation chain through compute launched under a privileged role.

**After (now handled):**
```text
IAM-PRIV-AWS-01 requires PassRole plus workload-creation combinations to be checked and severity-ranked as Critical when the workload can assume a privileged role.
```

**Before (false positive risk):**
```json
{
```

## Policy: endast EU-lagret (Leonards val)
När en produkt har samma färg i flera lager-länder (färg × ships-from = N SKU:er) men butiken visar bara färg, ska per-variant-lagret spegla **endast EU-lagret** — i linje med "EU-lager"-löftet.

Bekräftat live på `1005010621208893`: "Smart No BOX" visade **0** för att importen tog **första** lagret (0), medan färgen har **180/264 i två andra lager**.

## Fix
- `getInventory` returnerar nu **`shipFrom`** per SKU (`getProduct` härleder det redan — det slängdes bara bort).
- `/api/import`-matchning: summera **EU-lagrets** saldo per optionskombo (`isEuCountry`) och adoptera ett **EU-skuId** så dagliga synken speglar EU-siffran. Faller tillbaka på befintlig kombo/position-logik när ship-from saknas eller inget EU-lager finns → andra produktformer opåverkade (ingen regression).

## Audit (utförd före merge, per rutin)
3-args `adopt` med alla anropare uppdaterade; prioritet exakt → EU-kombo → kombo → position; klockan (tomma skuProps) → position som förut; synken matchar adopterat EU-skuId. **Kvarstående:** verifiera efter deploy att `getProduct` fyller `shipFrom` för denna produkt (skuProps "Ships From" var tomt, men `shipFrom` är ett annat fält). author: joseph-isaacs
body:
This is more of an idea for now

## Summary

This PR introduces the `Compaction` encoding, a transient array wrapper that normalizes its child into a compact canonical form when executed. This is similar to the existing `Slice` encoding in that it's non-serializable and exists primarily to drive execution.

The `Compaction` encoding handles structural normalization of various array types:

- **`ListView`** arrays are rebuilt to be zero-copy convertible to Arrow-style `ListArray` (overlapping views deduplicated, leading/trailing garbage trimmed)
- **`VarBinView`** arrays have their data buffers garbage collected
- **`Dict`** arrays are either decoded to flat canonical form or garbage collected in place (dead values removed, codes remapped) based on a cost heuristic
- **`Struct`** fields are recursively compacted

author: lornestack
body:
## Summary

- Markdown **source** view lost its custom syntax highlighting (went near-monochrome) after #3204, even with clean `node_modules` — not a dependency-version issue.
- Root cause: Vite `optimizeDeps` pre-bundled **two copies** of `@codemirror/language` — one for our direct import (`markdownHighlightStyle.ts`), one nested under `@uiw/react-codemirror` + `@codemirror/lang-markdown`. CodeMirror's `highlighterFacet` is a module-level singleton, so our custom `HighlightStyle` registered on a facet the editor/parser never read, and was silently dropped. The split was non-deterministic across checkouts/cache states, which is why it appeared to work on the PR branch.
- Fix: add the CodeMirror/Lezer singleton packages to `resolve.dedupe` and the CodeMirror entry points to `optimizeDeps.include`, so all consumers share a single `@codemirror/language` copy.

- [x] `bun run format`, `bun run lint` (0 errors), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bunx vitest run` (1015 passed)
- [x] Cleared `packages/desktop/node_modules/.vite`, restarted dev — `grep -rlE 'class HighlightStyle' .vite/deps/*.js` now returns exactly one chunk (was two); our import, `@uiw/react-codemirror`, and `@codemirror/lang-markdown` all resolve to it

author: georges-arm
body:
Improve the existing AArch64 Neon and SVE DCT 16x16 and 32x32 implementations:

- For Neon: merge the first and second pass functions to avoid duplication.

- For Neon and SVE: merge the outer loops to avoid the need to maintain `O`/`EO`/`EEE`/`EEO` arrays on the stack and consistently process four rows at a time.

- Fix the `rev16` and `rev32` helper functions to use `TBL` instead of `TBX` instructions (`TBL` has slightly better performance on some CPUs).

Benchmarking on a range of Neoverse server platforms with LLVM 21, this change shows (depending on exact CPU micro-architecture):

- 7-12% improvement in Neon DCT16.
- 0-9% improvement in Neon DCT32.
- 10-15% improvement in SVE DCT16.
- 0-15% improvement in SVE DCT32.

With this change the Neon intrinsics implementation is now faster than the assembly implementation, so update `setupDCTPrimitives_neon` to use the intrinsics version instead.

The `aarch64/dct.S` file contains assembly implementations of DCT16 and IDCT16, however these are now unused since the existing intrinsics-based versions are faster and therefore preferred. Since this code is unused, delete it from the library.

## Summary

Third Phase 7 register. Captures third-party suppliers whose services or technology fall inside the audited boundary.

### Standards mapping

- **SOC 2 CC9.2** — third-party risk
- **PCI DSS 12.8** — service provider relationships
- **ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.19** — information security in supplier relationships
- **A.5.20** — addressing IS within supplier agreements
- **A.5.21** — managing IS in the ICT supply chain
- **A.5.22** — monitoring, review, change management of supplier services

### Migration

\`007_vendors.up.sql\` introduces three new enums + reuses one + adds the table:

| Enum | Values |
|---|---|
| \`vendor_type\` | saas, paas, iaas, processor, subprocessor, hardware, professional_services, other |
| \`vendor_criticality\` | low, medium *(default)*, high, critical |
| \`vendor_status\` | prospective, active *(default)*, terminated |
| \`data_classification\` | *reuses \`asset_classification\` from PR #91 — nullable* |

\`vendors\` table: name, vendor_type, criticality, status, data_classification, owner_id (FK personnel), website, contact_name, contact_email, description, onboarded_date, offboarded_date, assurance_report (free text — \"SOC 2 Type II 2025-Q3\"), last_review_date, next_review_date, tags, notes, audit columns.

Two CHECKs:

- \`offboarded_date >= onboarded_date\` when both are set
- \`status = terminated\` requires \`offboarded_date NOT NULL\`

Mirrors the personnel start_date / end_date / status invariants.

### Routes

| Verb | Path | Roles |
|---|---|---|
| GET | \`/api/v1/vendors\` | any org member (auditor included) |
| GET | \`/api/v1/vendors/:id\` | any org member |
| POST | \`/api/v1/vendors\` | admin, member |
| PATCH | \`/api/v1/vendors/:id\` | admin, member |
| DELETE | \`/api/v1/vendors/:id\` | admin, member |

List supports \`?vendor_type=...\`, \`?status=...\`, and **\`?review_due=true\`** filters. The review_due flag is the auditor-cadence helper: returns rows where \`next_review_date\` is null or on/before today.

### Validation

- \`name\` + \`vendor_type\` required on create

Every write emits an audit row (\`vendor.created\`, \`vendor.updated\`, \`vendor.deleted\`).

author: claus911
body:
This fixes two StarRocks compatibility issues observed on Metabase 0.61+/1.61+.

1. Field Filters with widget type "String contains" fail because Metabase generates explicit `LIKE ... ESCAPE '\'`, while StarRocks does not parse that syntax. This overrides `transform-literal-like-pattern-honeysql` for `:starrocks` so the generated LIKE pattern is left unchanged.
(started from metabase v59)

2. Query Builder -> Native SQL conversion corrupts MySQL-style backtick identifiers during prettification, e.g. `silver`.`table`.`field` becomes ` silver `.` table `.` field `. This disables native SQL prettification for StarRocks.

Validation:
- Built successfully with `clojure -T:build uber`
- Verified the generated jar contains both driver overrides

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Driver-only query/display overrides for StarRocks with no auth or shared core logic changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds two **StarRocks** driver overrides for Metabase 0.59+/0.61+ SQL generation behavior.
> 
> **String filters** (`contains` / `starts-with` / `ends-with`): the default SQL path now wraps literal `LIKE` patterns with explicit `ESCAPE '\'`, which StarRocks rejects. StarRocks is wired to leave the honeysql pattern unchanged (with `prefer-method` toward `:sql`), relying on its built-in backslash escaping.
> 
> **Native SQL display**: prettification for `/api/dataset/native` is turned off for StarRocks so MySQL-style backtick identifiers (e.g. `` `catalog`.`table`.`field` ``) are not rewritten with spurious spaces inside the quotes.
>

author: johnyaku
body:
Adds the two remaining `dt remote` transfer subcommands, completing the set designed alongside `dt remote verify`. Both operate on a locally-accessible DVC remote's blob tree and reuse the `remote_verify` walker.

## `dt remote copy [REMOTE] NEW_PATH [--as NAME] [--copy] [--group-writable]`
Duplicate a remote's blob tree.
- Default **reflink → hardlink → copy** (space-efficient dedup on the same filesystem); never symlinks.
- `--copy` forces **independent byte copies** — required cross-filesystem and when the duplicate must carry different/broader permissions (a hardlink shares the source inode and therefore its perms).
- `--group-writable` sets setgid + group-write on the destination dirs for shared access.
- `--as NAME` registers the duplicate as a new DVC remote.

## `dt remote move [REMOTE] NEW_PATH [--quick]`
Relocate a remote and repoint config.
- **Same filesystem → instant `os.rename`.**
- **Cross filesystem → copy → verify → delete source**, so the source is only removed once the copy passes. Full checksum verify (reuses `remote_verify.verify_remote`), or `--quick` for a size+presence check.
- Afterwards **repoints every `.dvc/config` remote** whose URL resolved to the old path, preserving scheme/host and editing the correct config scope (project vs local).

Both accept either `NEW_PATH` (default remote) or `REMOTE NEW_PATH`, parsed from a variadic positional (Click can't order an optional positional before a required one). Refuses non-local and archived (pruned) remotes via `resolve_local_remote`, and refuses a non-empty destination.

## Implementation
New module `dt/remote_ops.py`. Bulk transfer is parallelised per md5 prefix using the archive layout enumerator (`_enumerate_prefix_dirs`), and per-file transfer reuses `cache_ops` `_try_reflink`/`_try_hardlink`/`_try_copy`. Copied blobs are made read-only (DVC convention). The `.dt-verify` ledger is not copied (regenerates).

## Testing
- 15 unit tests in `test_remote_ops.py` (fs detection, transfer modes incl. hardlink-inode and read-only-skip, tree replication, group-writable setgid, size/presence detection, scope-aware repointing, copy/move high-level incl. forced cross-fs copy→verify→delete and `--quick`).
- Full remote suite: 82 passed (`test_remote_ops`, `test_remote_verify`, `test_remote`, `test_remote_cmd`).
- Validated end-to-end in a real DVC repo: copy produced an identical tree + registered `--as` remote; same-fs move renamed and repointed the default remote.

Version 0.10.0 → 0.11.0; `modules.json` reference updated.

## Summary
Two coupled improvements to how agent-authored documents are read, modelled on VS Code's "open a file":

- **File viewer tab** — new `file-viewer` ViewSpec kind (`{ wsId, path }`) that renders one workspace file read-only.
  - **Tracked backlinks** previously jumped to the whole *Workspace* (and didn't even locate the file). Now a backlink opens that exact file in the viewer.
  - **Workspace Files panel** file-click was a dead no-op; now it opens the file in the viewer (dirs still navigate).

Clicking one jumps to the **Tracked** activity and selects that entity. Default nav lives in a `useWikilinkHandler` hook (overridable per call site).

body:
Follow-up fixes discovered during manual testing of https://github.com/metasfresh/me03/issues/29966 on danthermuat.

### Fixes
1. **DD_Order picking replenishment — async event handler AD context.** The reconcile event handler ran on an EventBus pool thread with no `AD_Client_ID`/`AD_Org_ID` in `Env`, so `newInstance(I_DD_Order.class)` produced `AD_Client_ID=0` → `MDDOrder.beforeSave` threw `FillMandatoryException` (Mandant). body:
Scope: `src/renderer/styles/{tokens,agent-tool-rows,agent-runtime}.css`, `src/renderer/ui/agent/AgentMessageFrame.tsx` (agent streaming indicator visual, fast-track).

Replaces the flat rose streaming pulse with a richer brand mark — an SVG whose path morphs **triangle → square → circle** and back while rotating a full turn.

**Design**
- **Smooth, rounded morph**: all three shapes are 4-corner rounded polygons written with one command structure (`M, (L Q)×4, Z`), so the SVG `d` interpolates continuously; corners stay rounded throughout (no sharp points, including the triangle apex). Paths were generated offline by an area-normalization script.
- **Equal optical area**, centroid-centered at (24,24): the triangle no longer reads smaller than the square, and the apparent size "breathes" during the morph while the visual weight stays constant (this is what makes the transition read as natural).
- **Rotation** (0° triangle → 120° square → 240° circle → 360°) runs in lock-step with the morph — holds on each shape, turns during transitions.
- **Material depth**: top-lit rose gradient (light crown → `--accent` → `--accent-strong`) + a soft rose `drop-shadow` on the *non-rotating* wrapper so the lift falls consistently downward while the mark spins. Fully tokenized.
- **Size + alignment**: 20px (~0.77 of the 26px body line), centered on the **same 14px icon column** as the tool / thinking status icons (measured: icon center == mark center, light & dark).

Also restores `--caret` to brand rose (the neutralization from the prior pass was reverted per design intent) and drops the now-unused `agent-capsule` keyframe.

**Gate**: typecheck ✓ · `test:renderer` 354/0 ✓ · token/hex/box-shadow guard (`typography-tokens.spec.ts`) 8/8 ✓ · light+dark visual + column-alignment measurement ✓. No raw hex / non-token values (B11); `drop-shadow` is a filter (not box-shadow).

author: andrewaltimit
body:
## Summary

Adds two opt-in randomizer toggles aimed at fast-travel convenience, plus a CI fix.

- **`--door-of-wind [N]`** seeds Door of Wind (item `0x89`, the warp consumable) into the new game's starting bag. The count is user-settable and defaults to 10 (`--door-of-wind` bare = 10, `--door-of-wind 25` = 25, clamped to the 99 stack cap). It is additive: with no `--starting-items` reroll the vanilla Healing Leaf is kept alongside it; with a reroll the random consumables replace the Leaf and Door of Wind is forced on top.
- **`--all-warps`** presets the "visited towns" story-flag bitmask so Door of Wind can teleport to any town from the start. It writes the same `0x8008575C = 0xF77F` / `0x8008575E = 0xF8FF` values the well-known "Access All Towns" cheat uses.

Both toggles are mirrored in the in-browser ROM patcher (a count input + a checkbox) and the WASM bundle is rebuilt.

## How it works

There is no static starting-inventory or warp-flag table, so both presets are written into reclaimable code in the new-game data-init `FUN_80034A6C` (the same approach as the existing starting-item randomizer). Two key details:

- **The all-warps preset lives in its own reclaimable region**, so it does not reduce the starting-item count -- items keep all five slots. It reuses four redundant `sw $zero` stores at `0x80034adc` (writes the caller's `memset` has already zeroed), and uses `$v1` so it never clobbers the live `$v0 = 0x2dc0` constant the surrounding code carries into a global just below. The preset survives because the inventory seed's zero-loop, which would otherwise re-clear the bitmask, is always overwritten when the seed is rewritten; verified that the party-stat seeder called in between never touches the warp window. The patched code was disassembled to confirm `$v0` is preserved and the bytes match the cheat exactly.
- The forced Door of Wind item seeds through the same clean-room engine path (`World::seed_starting_inventory`) as any other starting item.

## Tests

- Disc-gated `door_of_wind_and_all_warps_round_trip_on_disc`: re-decodes the inventory and warp regions off the patched image, asserts 5 items + all-warps coexist, the warp preset is in its own region (not the inventory region), the live instruction flanking the warp region is byte-identical, both touched sectors stay EDC/ECC-valid, and a fixed seed is byte-deterministic.
- Engine runtime oracle `forced_door_of_wind_seeds_the_bag_at_runtime`: a New Game off the patched disc seeds Door of Wind into the bag alongside the preserved Healing Leaf base.
- New unit tests for the count (explicit / default / clamp / off), the two-region split, and the `$v0`-preserving `$v1` encoding.

The all-warps preset has no clean-room engine consumer yet (there is no Door-of-Wind warp menu in the port), so it is validated at the disc-round-trip level and matches the cheat write byte-for-byte. User-confirmed working in mednafen.

## Also in this PR

Fixes a main-branch CI failure: the real-memory-card decode test located the first name-matching `.mcr` in the mednafen save dir and panicked when an empty leftover playtest card sorted first. `locate_card` now returns the first card that actually holds an active save block, and skips when none do.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings`: clean
- Disc-gated + runtime tests: green (with `LEGAIA_DISC_BIN` set)
- No Sony bytes committed; disc-gated tests skip without the disc.

Hotfix for the failed production deploy of #80.

`npm run build` runs `tsc -b` (via `tsconfig.app.json`) which type-checks the app for real — unlike `tsc --noEmit` against the root `tsconfig.json` (`files: []`), which checks nothing. The merge of #80 failed at the Build step with:

```
RiderApp.tsx(154,11): TS2353 'battery_health_pct' does not exist in type 'Device'.
RiderApp.tsx(158,59): TS2551 Property 'device_imei' does not exist on type 'Device'.
```

`handleInspectionSubmit` writes the per-device verification fields onto `Device` objects, but the `Device` interface didn't declare them. This adds the optional fields. Verified locally with a full `npm ci && npm run build` (tsc -b + vite build) — passes.

Production rider app was unaffected (failed build = no deploy; old version still live).

author: mike773
body:
## Зачем

`metric_tree` через `WITH RECURSIVE` тянул **всё поддерево за один вызов**. На одной верхнеуровневой метрике это означало «дай все метрики»: напр. `Производительность` в реальном датасете имеет **38 прямых детей** и глубину 3 — старое поведение вываливало весь граф разом, упиралось в кап 80 строк и молча терял данные на глубоких/ветвистых деревьях.

Нужно было обрабатывать **по одному уровню за вызов**, чтобы агент вёл сильнейшую ветку вглубь адресно, а не получал перемешанных внуков всех узлов.

## Что сделано

**Данные — `sqlite_store.metric_tree`**
- Рекурсивный CTE со счётчиком уровня `lvl` → параметр `max_levels` (по умолчанию **1**: корень + прямые дети).
- Колонка `has_children` (1 — есть нераскрытые подкомпоненты, 0 — лист) — сигнал «куда ещё копать».
- В результат добавлен `levels_shown`.

**Инструмент — `tools.metric_tree`**
- Один уровень за вызов; `max_levels` клампится в `[1,3]` (защита от «дай всё дерево»).
- Docstring переписан под пошаговый спуск повторными вызовами на выбранном ребёнке.

**Промпты**
- `SYSTEM_PROMPT_RULES` п.7 — `metric_tree` = один уровень + `has_children`.
- `SYSTEM_PROMPT_RULES` п.10 — протокол доведения до корня: `find_flags` → топ-3 флага → `metric_tree` уровень за уровнем по сильнейшей ветке до `has_children=0` → `related_metrics` для внешнего драйвера.
- `SYNTHESIS_PROMPT` — каждый инсайт доводить до конечного драйвера (лист дерева / опережающая связь).

**Бюджет — `agent_classic`**
- `_TOOL_CALL_BUDGET` 18→**32**, `_RECURSION_LIMIT` 50→**80** под уровневый спуск (≈1 вызов на уровень дерева).

## Проверка

- **Юнит:** 59 зелёных, в т.ч. 6 новых (`tests/json_analyzer/test_metric_tree_levels.py`): уровни, `has_children`, пошаговый спуск, **корректность значений** — факт/план переносятся как есть, направление-зависимый `plan_status` верен и на верхнем уровне, и на листьях (обратная метрика: значение выше плана → `хуже_плана`).
- **E2E json_analyzer** на реальных кредах, метрика с 38 детьми: `find_flags → metric_tree` вернул один уровень (39 строк, `truncated=False`), `has_children=1` корректно у единственного узла с подуровнем; числа верны (12.05 vs план 18.0).
- **E2E оркестратор:** 5 ходов, без регрессий — json_analyzer пересчитывает каждый ход, опорный разбор стабилен.

author: dewet22
body:
Docstring-only correction. No code, logic, or test changes.

The prior wording stated the `0x31` special-case is "load-bearing" because HYBRID_GEN1 "answers identity-only at `0x11`". This was inferred from passive dongle captures — the dongle happened to poll inverter banks at `0x31`, and absence in the capture was mistaken for hardware inability.

Live hardware tests on HYBRID_GEN1 (ARM 449) show otherwise:
- `probe_read_address.py` (extended in #187) asked `0x11` for HR(0,60) and HR(60,60) — both returned 4/4 responses
- Value-equality check: `0x11` mirrors `0x31` across 114 HR registers (full facade; `system_time` RTC excluded as it ticks between sequential reads)
- The official GivEnergy app reads and writes config at `0x11`, firmware-invariant across ARM 449 and 451

The `0x31` alias is retained for now — live AC validation is still needed before the full unification can land (#189). This PR just stops the docstring from asserting something we know to be false.

Closes the docstring prerequisite from #189.

author: stephanj
body:
Supersedes #1046 with a **clean, minimal diff**. #1046's source fork is 37 commits behind `devoxx/master`, so it shows ~197 unrelated files. This branch is cut from current `master` with only the two credential commits cherry-picked, plus a commit addressing the code-review findings — so the diff is just the **7 credential files**.

## What this does
Moves all 19 credential fields (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Groq, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Grok, Kimi, GLM, Azure OpenAI, AWS access/secret/bearer, CustomOpenAI, Google Search, Google CSE, Tavily) out of plaintext `DevoxxGenieSettingsPlugin.xml` into IntelliJ's PasswordSafe (OS keychain / KeePass / KWallet).

- New `service/credentials` package: `CredentialKey` enum, `CredentialService` interface, `PasswordSafeCredentialService` impl with in-memory fallback for headless/test environments.
- `DevoxxGenieStateService`: Lombok accessors disabled on the 19 credential fields; hand-written `@Transient` accessors delegate to `CredentialService`; one-shot migration in `loadState` reads legacy plaintext, writes it to PasswordSafe, and wipes the XML fields.
- `CredentialMigrationStartupActivity`: belt-and-braces retry on every project open, idempotent via `credentialsMigratedV1`.
- `plugin.xml`: registers `CredentialService` and the startup activity.

## Review fixes (vs #1046)
Addresses the code-review findings on #1046:

1. **NPE guard** — `migrateCredentialsToPasswordSafe()` now checks `service == null || !service.isAvailable()`, since `getService()` can return `null` (rather than throw) on some IntelliJ versions / test environments.
2. **Migration log accuracy** — added a `skipped` counter so retry runs no longer report a misleading `migrated=0` when credentials were already safely in PasswordSafe.
3. **Javadoc** — fixed broken `{@link #subKey()}` → `{@link #getSubKey()}` in `CredentialKey`.
4. **Deprecation** — switched to the minimal `CredentialAttributes(serviceName)` constructor, away from the deprecated 4-arg form.
5. **Comment accuracy** — clarified that `memoryFallback` is a write-side cache (populated on `setCredential`, not on reads), not a read-through "write-through cache".

### Deliberately not changed
The review also flagged PasswordSafe I/O running on the EDT in `loadState()`. We **kept it synchronous** on purpose: the existing design guarantees callers never observe a window where the state holds plaintext but PasswordSafe does not yet. The `CredentialMigrationStartupActivity` already provides an async backstop on project open.

## Testing
`./gradlew compileJava` — green.

Closes #1046 once merged (can be closed manually in favour of this branch).
