💡 **What:** Replaced implicit `toLocaleString`, `toLocaleTimeString`, and `toLocaleDateString` calls with globally cached `Intl.NumberFormat` and `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instances across the codebase (`App.tsx`, `Flips.tsx`, `PriceChart.tsx`, `Status.tsx`, `FusionTree.tsx`).
🎯 **Why:** Creating new `Intl` instances is notoriously expensive in JavaScript and synchronously blocks the main thread. In high-frequency render components like `PriceChart` (during hover interactions), `FusionTree` (during recursive rendering), or `Status` (polling ticks), this implicit instantiation degrades UI responsiveness.
📊 **Impact:** Eliminates redundant `Intl` object instantiations, significantly reducing render time and preventing micro-stutters during interactions (like chart tooltips) and large list processing.
🔬 **Measurement:** Profile the React application using the Chrome DevTools Performance tab and observe the reduction in render script evaluation time during chart hovering or recursive max fusions calculations.

Builds on the canonical parameter database merged in #89 with scientifically-validated FDE updates for the highest-impact SP streams. Every changed FC, FCo, FS, FL, BMP, and η value carries a direct literature citation with correct `min ≤ medio ≤ max` ordering.

Motivated by closing the gap to the **FIESP/AMPLUN benchmark** (~16 M m³/day gross 2021; 6.4 M Nm³/day biomethane feasible per SEMIL/FIESP 2024) **without inflating parameters** — corrections are sourced, not optimistic.

- BAGACO FCo widened 0.164–0.200 → **0.15–0.38** (EPE BEN 2024: bagasse energy use −2%; modern 87–100 bar boilers leave 30–50% surplus)

## What is the purpose of the change
Fixes #15229

Fix the inconsistent A2A list query behavior between console UI and admin API when `agentName` is omitted.

Although both cases enter the same `blur` branch, they previously produced different `dataId` values:

- `agentName = ""` -> `dataId = "**"`
- `agentName = null` -> `dataId = "*null*"`

author: varashi
body:
## What

Adds one gateway HTTPRoute rule (via the plex app-template HelmRelease `route:` block) that **removes the `X-Plex-Client-Profile-Extra` header on the transcode *decision* request, scoped to Plex for Apple TV 8.45 only**.

## Why

Plex for Apple TV 8.45 "Enhanced Player" sends:

```
X-Plex-Client-Profile-Extra: add-transcode-target(...protocol=hls&container=mkv&replace=true)+...
```

`replace=true` overrides PMS's built-in tvOS profile → PMS decides `container=mkv protocol=hls`. tvOS's HLS player can't parse MKV-in-HLS → every **transcoded** title spins forever / crashes (direct play fine, other clients fine). Confirmed via PMS log scan: every Apple TV decision = `container=mkv protocol=hls`, zero mpegts. Upstream Plex client bug (fixed in ATV 2025.31.x, held by an EAC3 beta regression, not public). The client-side "disable Enhanced Player" workaround did **not** fix it for the affected user.

Stripping the header makes PMS fall back to its built-in `tvOS.xml` profile (HLS + **mpegts**).

## Why version-pinned (Product **AND** Version Exact match)

A wholesale strip on all Apple TV clients would drop **working** clients to the built-in `tvOS.xml` caps:

| | Enhanced Player | tvOS.xml fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Res | 4K | 1080p |
| Codec | h264+hevc | h264 only |
| Depth | 10-bit | 8-bit |
| Audio | ≤10ch eac3 | aac 2ch |
| Subs | srt | eia_608 only |

So the match is pinned to `X-Plex-Version: 8.45`. That build plays **nothing** needing transcode today, so the fallback is "1080p that plays" vs "crash" — strictly better — while every other Apple TV version keeps full Enhanced Player caps. Header-only + decision-only; `start.m3u8` carries just a `session=` token, so playback continuation is unaffected.

## Scope / safety

- Mirrors the existing `/library/streams` Range-strip primitive (native `RequestHeaderModifier`, no Lua/CEC).
- No other client, endpoint, or Apple TV version touched.
- Fully reversible (revert the rule).

## This is a probe

Validation step to confirm container is the root cause. After Dennis retries **with Enhanced Player ON**:
- **Plays** → container confirmed; build the permanent **surgical** fix (rewrite `container=mkv`→fMP4/mpegts, preserve raised caps — Lua/CEC or enhanced server-side tvOS profile).
- **Still broken** → diagnosis incomplete; revert + reopen scaleplex#122 with new evidence.

Refs Varashi/scaleplex#122

author: tellmemoree
body:
## Summary

Three interrelated bugs in the Thermal Strike AOI layer and news geolocator:

**1. Cyrillic suffix too short** (`news/route.ts`)
Ukrainian place adjectives like `-ський/-ської/-ськ ому` have 4–6 char endings; the old `\p{L}{0,4}` regex cut them off. "Краснодарськ**ому**" now matches correctly.

**2. Title ignored when description is present** (`news/route.ts`)
`findCoords(description || title)` ignored the headline when body text existed. Changed to `findCoords(title + ' ' + description)` so place names that only appear in the headline are not missed.

**3. Strike AOIs with no matching fire were silently dropped** (`strategic-thermal/route.ts`)
Drone/missile strikes often produce no FIRMS-detectable fire. Articles that passed the strike filter but had no nearby FIRMS hit were never emitted. Now they surface as `hit: false, confidence: 'news'` (dim marker, no glow, blue popup badge). If another article for the same ~1km cell has a fire hit, the marker upgrades.

**Also added to gazetteer:** Black Sea, Azov Sea, Constanta (RO), Berdyansk — all relevant for the current naval-drone campaign.

## Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| 2 news AOIs (both fire-confirmed) | 19 news AOIs (2 fire + 17 news-only) |
| "Краснодарськ ому" → no match | → Krasnodar [45.03, 38.97] |
| Constanta drone incident → invisible | → maritime pin [44.17, 28.64] |
| Belgorod/Kursk/Bryansk drone campaign → 0 markers | → 4 markers |

author: asce-d
body:
Fixes the open-redirection vulnerability reported in potpie-ai/potpie#596.

## Problem
The auth pages trusted attacker-controllable redirect parameters and acted on them after authentication:

1. **Open redirect** — `app/(auth)/layout.tsx` ran `router.push(decodeURIComponent(redirect))` on the raw `?redirect=` value, so `https://app.potpie.ai/sign-in?redirect=https://evil.com` navigated the authenticated user to an arbitrary external site.
2. **Token exfiltration (more severe)** — `lib/auth/vscode-callback.ts` used the `?redirect_uri=` value as the callback base and appended the Firebase **token + customToken** to it. A non-loopback `redirect_uri` (e.g. `?source=vscode&redirect_uri=https://evil.com`) would send the user's auth token to an attacker-controlled host.

## Fix
New shared validator `lib/auth/safe-redirect.ts`:
- **`getSafeInternalPath(raw, fallback)`** — accepts only same-origin relative paths. Absolute URLs, protocol-relative `//host`, backslash tricks, control characters and non-`/` values collapse to the fallback (`/`).
- **`isLoopbackCallbackUrl(raw)`** — true only for `http(s)` loopback callbacks (`localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / `::1`).

Wired in:
- `app/(auth)/layout.tsx` redirects via `getSafeInternalPath(redirectUrl, "/")`.
- `lib/auth/vscode-callback.ts` only honours `redirect_uri` when it is a loopback callback, otherwise keeps the default localhost base (token is never sent off-host).

## Tests
13 vitest tests covering external/encoded/protocol-relative/backslash/control-char/`javascript:` redirect rejection, internal-path preservation, loopback acceptance, and the VS Code token-leak case. `tsc --noEmit` clean on all changed files.

author: smottal
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LPD-83058

Why UNMODIFIABLE_ROLE_NAMES doesn't contain the system roles: these are not a fixed list, the base names live in RoleConstants, but a deployment can add its own via the system.roles, system.organization.roles, and system.site.roles portal properties, and PortalImpl merges those in at startup. The only reliable way to know whether a name is a system role is Role.isSystem() / PortalUtil.isSystemRole(...), which consults that merged, runtime-resolved set.

This keeps a single call site (isUnmodifiable(role)) while preserving the dynamic, property-aware system-role detection that a merged static array would lose.

author: v3ron
body:
## What is this?

This PR fixes Network Activity initiator symbolication for Hermes stacks that include internal bytecode frames. Mixed stacks could previously send pseudo-files like `address at InternalBytecode.js` to Metro, which made Metro try to read them as project files during code-frame generation.

Fixes #294.

## How does it work?

The initiator symbolication helper now sends only Metro-symbolicatable generated frames to `/symbolicate`, currently the frames backed by HTTP bundle URLs. It keeps track of each submitted frame's original stack index, then merges the symbolicated result back into the original initiator stack so internal Hermes frames remain available as generated context without being treated as source files.

## Why is this useful?

Network Activity keeps source-mapped request initiator details for real app frames while avoiding noisy Metro file-read failures for Hermes internals. The fix is narrow to symbolication payload construction, so existing initiator display behavior stays intact for valid Metro bundle frames.

author: akadlec
body:
## Summary

Aligns `/rides/stats` (Statistics) to the v2 design with shared `@tarmoto/ui` components, the Ride History filter model, a filter-aware distance chart, unified card headings, and three newly **backend-backed** cards: surface breakdown, curviness mix, and a 12-month quality trend.

### Screen alignment (companion)
- **Filter** — two `SegmentedControl`s (time window + ride type) matching Ride History's `TimeWindowPills`.
- **KPIs** — `MetricTile` bricks; distance leads on an ink/accent tile; distance values unit-aware (km/mi).
- **Distance chart** — filter-aware granularity: month bars for All time / This year, **day bars** for Last 90 / 30 days; unambiguous month/day axis labels; real dates in the tooltip; header copy follows the window.
- **Headings** — one shared `SectionHeading` (mono stamp → 20px title → optional mono caption) across the distance chart, heatmap, year-over-year and all-years cards.
- **Heatmap** — flexible `1fr` columns with a square aspect ratio (fills the card; no empty right gutter).
- **All-years table** → shared `DataTable`, unit-aware distance columns.

### New backend-backed cards
- **`GET /api/v1/rides/stats/breakdown`** (`RideBreakdownDto`) returns the **distance-weighted** surface and curviness mix for the active filter, derived **live** from each ride's snapped `ride_segments → road_segments` (`SUM(length_m)` per surface type / per curviness band). No migration, no backfill — a later correction to a segment's surface/curviness self-corrects the card. Reuses `applyRidesFilters` so the window/type exactly match the list + stats endpoints.
- **Curviness bands** sit on the canonical **0–5** `curviness_score` scale (the scale fun-zone clustering already uses: `>= 3.0`, `/ 5.0`). Buckets: straight `[0,1)` / flowing `[1,2)` / twisty `[2,3)` / tight `[3,4)` / hairpin `[4,5]`.
- **Surface breakdown** + **Curviness mix** cards fetch the endpoint, refetch on filter change, and render honest loading / empty / error states (empty when no segments are snapped).
- **Quality trend · 12 months** is computed **client-side** from the ride list's `avg_road_quality` (distance-weighted per month; unscored months render as gaps).

### Latent bug fixed
- The demo seeder wrote road `curviness_score` on a **0–1** scale (`round2(rng())`), so every demo segment read as "straight" and fun zones never met their `>= 3.0` gate. Now seeds **0–5**, matching the canonical scale used everywhere else.

## Contracts / schema impact
- No DB schema change, no migration. New read endpoint + DTO only.
- Regenerated `@tarmoto/openapi-client` via `pnpm openapi:gen`. The large `schema.d.ts` diff is **pre-existing ordering drift brought current** (a re-run is byte-identical); the meaningful addition is `RideBreakdownDto` + the new path.

## Risks / regression surface
- New per-filter network call for the breakdown (debounced via effect); KPIs/chart stay client-side.
- Curviness scale assumption (0–5) is called out above; the seeder fix also affects fun-zone seed data (for the better — it was previously starved).

## Test evidence
- Backend: `breakdown` service spec (distance weighting, canonical ordering, empty state); **1740 backend tests pass**.
- Companion: `computeDistanceSeries` + `computeQualityTrend` + window/filter unit tests; **990 companion tests pass**.
- e2e: mock-backend `stats/breakdown` handler + **T32** extended to assert the three cards. (Full Playwright run deferred to CI — a local `next dev` server is holding the companion `.next` lock.)
- `tsc --noEmit`, `next build`, `nest build`, and `eslint` — all clean.

## Souhrn

Doplnění chybějících publikovatelných článků pro **4. a 5. června 2026** — ruční publikace dvou hotových článků na pokyn redakce.

## Proč chyběly (diagnóza rutiny)

Cron `publish-scheduled.js` (workflow *Publish scheduled articles*) **oba dny řádně proběhl** — run 25 (4. 6., 08:24 UTC) i run 26 (5. 6., 08:12 UTC), oba `success`. **Nešlo o selhání rutiny.** Publisher ale publikuje jen články se statusem **`verified`/`partial`**; vše ostatní (`draft`, `review-pending`, `flagged`, `needs-rewrite`) drží v *review holdu* pro ruční schválení. Ve frontě 4.–5. 6. byly jen `review-pending`/`draft` kandidáti → publisher korektně vypsal „nic k publikaci". Chybějící články jsou tedy důsledek prázdné fronty *verified* článků, ne chyby cronu.

## Co PR dělá

Publikuje dva hotové články (dříve drafty, mergnuté v #515 a #517):

| Slug | Datum | Status |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `clanek-rizeni-podle-vysledku.html` — Řízení podle výsledků | **4. 6. 2026** | review-pending |
| `clanek-teorie-zmeny.html` — Teorie změny | **5. 6. 2026** | review-pending |

Změny u obou:
- `articles.json`: `published: true`, `date` + `scheduled_for` nastaveny, `audit-status: review-pending`, `ready_since`

## Poznámky
- **Audit-status `review-pending`** (ne `verified`): oba články mají v audit komentářích otevřené body k doplnění (RBM — kvantifikované cíle Zdraví 2030; ToC — citace z plného textu WHO příručky). Zobrazí se transparentní banner „čeká na ověření". Redakce může kdykoli povýšit na `verified`.
- **Obálky:** články zatím bez cover grafiky (hub degraduje gracefully). Lze dogenerovat — publish skript je generuje při auto-publikaci.
- Verifikace: `npm run validate:articles` → **OK** (publikační hygiena prošla).

author: wrenrichley
body:
## Summary

Two changes to the Reviewer's structured-output contract, driven by the foreman#100 dogfood:

1. **`minor` is no longer a structured finding** — it lives in `review_comment` prose, never in `findings`. Filing minor observations was creating per-ticket nit accumulation with no draining mechanism (Jeff's call: "we will just end up with thousands of tickets that we can never drain down to zero").
2. **`Important` flipped from non-blocking to blocking.** Outcome rule now reads "any critical OR any important → needs_fix" (was "two+ important"). "Important but clean" was leaking accumulating spec-vs-impl drift through the merge gate.

## What changed

**`packages/foreman/src/foreman/prompts/reviewer.md`** (spec PR Reviewer)
- Severity rubric: `minor` reclassed as "(NOT a structured finding)" with explicit rationale ("Letting them die in the review is by design").
- Outcome rule: any `important` → `needs_fix`.
- Field rules: `findings` MUST contain ONLY critical/important; MUST be empty when `clean`.

**`packages/foreman/src/foreman/prompts/reviewer_impl.md`** (impl PR Reviewer)
- `Important` flipped to blocking; added concrete example matching the foreman#100 finding pattern (AC partially satisfied — impl works but doesn't fully match what spec promised).
- Added explicit `Minor` section (was missing entirely).
- Outcome rule rewritten with rationale comment inline so the next reader knows why this changed.

**`packages/foreman/src/foreman/schemas/reviewer.py`**
- Field descriptions updated to match the new prompt contract.
- New `@model_validator(mode='after')` on `ReviewerOutput` enforces three rules programmatically: no `minor` in findings; `clean` ⇔ empty findings; `needs_fix` ⇔ non-empty findings. The SDK round-trips the LLM if it produces a contradictory shape, so a misbehaving model can't leak past the schema.

**`packages/foreman/tests/test_schemas_reviewer.py`**
- 4 new tests pinning the validator.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest packages/foreman/tests/test_schemas_reviewer.py` — 16/16 passing (12 existing + 4 new).
- [x] `pytest packages/foreman/tests -k "reviewer or fixer or worker or cli"` — 328 passed, 5 skipped.
- [x] Full pre-push pytest — 808 passed, 5 skipped (no regressions).
- [ ] Manual: next autonomous v3 run should produce fewer "needs_fix from minor noise" cycles AND should block on first important finding instead of accumulating.

## Why now

Surfaced during the foreman#100 v3 dogfood — the impl Reviewer flagged Important findings but set `outcome=clean`, which let an under-spec'd impl land. The combination (any important blocks; minor goes to prose only) closes that gap without inviting unbounded nit-ticket churn.

## Summary
- Skeleton ingest now spreads the parent document's free-form `metadata` onto each chunk's `metadata` dict, with chunk bookkeeping keys (`chunk_index`/`start_char`/`end_char`) still taking precedence on collision. This mirrors the VectorCypher engine and lets `metadata.<path>` recall filters match on the Skeleton-pgvector backend (previously they matched nothing because Skeleton chunks only carried bookkeeping keys).

body:
Three benchmark hotspots from issue #29 that caused GC pressure under
sustained 250 k ev/s load:

1. ShardedEventBuffer.PIDs() — O(log n) slice-growth reallocations
   Two-pass approach: count exact total across shards first, then allocate
   once and collect. BenchmarkPIDs: 140 672 B/11 allocs → 40 960 B/1 alloc.

2. RateLimiter.Cleanup() — map snapshot overhead (~4× vs slice)
   Replace map[string]*ruleState snapshot with []cleanupEntry (flat struct
   slice). Pre-allocate both snapshot and stale slices to their upper bound.
   BenchmarkRateLimiterCleanup: 46 056 B/11 allocs → 20 481 B/2 allocs.

3. RuleEngine OpIn/OpNotIn — valueSetKey() called on every Evaluate()
   valueSetKey() sorted+joined a 1000-element values slice per call (28 KB).
   Add RuleCondition.setKey (unexported), populated once by compilePatterns
   via index-based (pointer) iteration so setKey is written into the actual
   stored conditions, not range copies. Hot path now does a single map
   lookup with the pre-computed string key.
   BenchmarkOpInLargeSet: 28 672 B/3 allocs → 2 048 B/1 alloc (14×).

Acceptance criteria (issue #29):
  TestPerformanceRegression/MemoryUsage  18.7 MB  ≤ 100 MB ✓
  TestMemoryProfileAtLoad heap           34.8 MB  ≤ 100 MB ✓

body: ## What changed and why `MemoryImage` and `ProfileAvatar` already route their `src` prop through `toDisplayImageUrl` before rendering, so HEIC Supabase Storage URLs get rewritten to the `/storage/v1/render/image/public/...?format=jpeg&quality=85` transform endpoint — required because Chrome, Firefox, and (in some configurations) Safari can't decode `.heic` natively. The newer design-system primitives introduced in the UI refresh (PR #28) — `src/components/ui/PhotoFrame.tsx` and `src/components/ui/Avatar.tsx` — render `src` straight to `` without that step. Any caller that passes a raw `person.profilePhotoUrl` therefore shows the placeholder (PhotoFrame) or initials (Avatar) whenever the underlying photo was uploaded as HEIC. Reproducible bug locations (all pass `person.profilePhotoUrl` directly): | Page | Component | Site | |---|---|---| | `/profile/[id]` hero portrait | `PhotoFrame` | `src/app/profile/[id]/page.tsx:626` | | `/` "In memory" deceased relative | `PhotoFrame` | `src/app/page.tsx:732` | | `/family-tree` grid card | `PhotoFrame` | `src/app/family-tree/page.tsx:366` | | `/families/[id]` member list | `Avatar` | `src/app/families/[id]/page.tsx:233` | | `/profile/[id]` breadcrumb | `Avatar` | `src/app/profile/[id]/page.tsx:853` | | `/family-tree` list view | `Avatar` | `src/app/family-tree/page.tsx:465` | | `/` upcoming birthdays | `Avatar` | `src/app/page.tsx:620` | | `/` suggested people | `Avatar` | `src/app/page.tsx:845` | Other PhotoFrame callsites (timeline, memories, profile gallery, home featured memory) wrapped explicitly with `toDisplayImageUrl(...)` before passing, but that defense-in-depth lives at the wrong layer — a design-system primitive shouldn't depend on every caller remembering to pre-normalize the URL, especially when two of the four existing image primitives already handle it internally. **Fix:** route `src` through `toDisplayImageUrl` *inside* `PhotoFrame` and `Avatar`, matching the contract of `MemoryImage` and `ProfileAvatar`. `toDisplayImageUrl` is idempotent (it short-circuits unless the URL ends in `.heic`/`.heif` *and* contains `/storage/v1/object/public/`), so the callsites that already pre-wrapped are unaffected — `toDisplayImageUrl(toDisplayImageUrl(url)) === toDisplayImageUrl(url)`. ## How it was tested - **`yarn test`** — 559 tests pass / 5 skipped (was 555/5; +4 new). - **`yarn lint`** — 0 errors, 0 warnings. - **`yarn build`** — production Turbopack build succeeds; route table unchanged. - **4 new regression-pin tests** (2 in `PhotoFrame.test.tsx`, 2 in `Avatar.test.tsx`) pin: - HEIC Supabase URLs are rewritten to the render-image endpoint with `format=jpeg&quality=85` - Non-HEIC Supabase URLs pass through verbatim - Existing "retries the new image after a previous src errored (resets failed state on src change)" tests still pass — the `prev*` render-time reset pattern compares the raw `src` prop, not the derived `displayUrl`, so swapping HEIC↔JPG still resets the failed state correctly. ## Screenshots **Not attached.** This branch is a code-only fix; reproducing the visual diff requires a Supabase Storage backend with a real HEIC upload, which isn't available in this isolated environment. The fix is verified via unit tests that pin the exact URL transform. Flagging for manual smoke test on the affected pages before merge — pick a person whose `profilePhotoUrl` ends in `.heic` (or upload one from iOS via Safari) and confirm the portrait now renders on `/profile/[id]`, `/family-tree`, and the home page "In memory" panel. ## Self-review notes - **No `any` types** introduced. - **No `else` blocks** introduced. - **No unused imports** — `toDisplayImageUrl` is the only new import in each primitive. - **Removed `&& src` from JSX** — previously `{showImg && src ? `<img src={src}>`...}` was double-gating because `showImg = Boolean(src) && !failed`. After the change, `showImg = Boolean(displayUrl) && !failed`, so the JSX gate collapses to `{showImg ? `<img src={displayUrl}>`...}`. Same behavior, less noise. - **Edge cases checked:** - `src = null` / `undefined` → `toDisplayImageUrl` returns `""` → placeholder shown (same as before). - `src = ""` → returns `""` → placeholder (same as before). - `src = HEIC Supabase public-object URL` → rewritten to render endpoint (the fix). - `src = JPG Supabase public-object URL` → returned unchanged. - `src = blob:...` URL → no `/storage/v1/object/public/` substring → returned unchanged. Matches the pre-existing behavior used in `AddMemoryModal`'s thumbnail preview path. - `src = HEIC non-Supabase URL` (Firebase legacy) → returned unchanged. Matches MemoryImage's current behavior; a separate fallback would be needed for the Firebase host, but no such URL exists in the live data per the migration history. - **Comments explain WHY**, not what. Both new blocks call out iOS as the source of HEIC uploads and link the pattern to `MemoryImage` / `ProfileAvatar`. - **No behavior change for safe callers** — `toDisplayImageUrl` is idempotent, so the timeline / memories / featured-memory / gallery callsites that already pre-wrap continue to work exactly as before. ## Deferred / follow-ups - The explicit `toDisplayImageUrl()` wrappers at the safe callsites (`timeline/page.tsx:245`, `memories/page.tsx:289`, `memories/page.tsx:429`, `page.tsx:516`, `profile/[id]/page.tsx:1020`, `profile/[id]/page.tsx:1032`) are now redundant. **Kept in place this PR** — removing them is a pure cleanup that's better separated from a behavior fix so the diff doesn't mix concerns. Worth a follow-up PR once this lands. - T-3 in `TODOS.md` ("extend `next/image` adoption beyond `ProfileAvatar`") is the broader version of this work. This PR doesn't touch `next/image` — both UI primitives still use a plain `` — because adopting `next/image` here has a subtler tradeoff (the existing `ProfileAvatar` already falls back to native `` for Supabase storage URLs and blob URLs, which would need to be repeated here, plus `width`/`height` props are needed to avoid CLS). Worth its own scoping conversation. ## Uncertainty / flags for review - The fix assumes `toDisplayImageUrl` is the right canonical URL normalizer. It is, today — both `MemoryImage` and `ProfileAvatar` use it, and the `next.config.ts` `remotePatterns` block has the `render/image/public/**` pathname configured alongside the `object/public/**` one. If you ever swap to a different transform pipeline (e.g. Cloudflare Images, imgproxy), the single point of change is `src/utils/imageUrl.ts`, so this fix doesn't add additional coupling. - I scoped this to PhotoFrame + Avatar because those are the only two design-system primitives that render images. There's a fifth `` callsite — `AddMemoryModal.tsx:359`, the upload thumbnail preview — that takes a `blob:` URL by design and intentionally skips the transform; not touched here. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01ApwozM15XGrJZaHLNuMJbh)_

body:
## Summary

Applies the full-page dark-theme canvas pattern established in IngestPage to all remaining protected routes that still showed white viewport bands in dark mode.

## Linked Issue

Closes #208

## Issue Alignment

This PR implements the issue by:

- Adding `minHeight: calc(100vh - 60px)`, `backgroundColor: var(--color-surface-muted)`, and `color: var(--color-text)` to the root `<main>` element on all affected pages.
- Preserving existing inner content layouts by moving `maxWidth` / `margin` styles into an inner wrapper `<div>` where needed.
- Ensuring loading, error, empty, not-found, and loaded states all share the same themed full-page canvas behavior.
- Adding E2E tests for the newly covered routes to verify dark-theme background is not white/transparent.

Scope covered:

- `ProblemDetailPage` (loading, error, loaded)
- `ExamDetailPage` (loading, error, not-found, loaded)
- `ActiveExamPage` (loading, error, no-active-exam, no-items, loaded)
- `ActivePracticePage` (no-problem, loaded)
- `SettingsPage` (loading, error, loaded)
- `CoachingPage` (loading, not-found)

Out of scope / intentionally not included:

- Reworking #205 pages (not requested)
- Full redesign of detail/active/settings pages
- Changing dark theme palette tokens
- Changing business logic or API behavior

- Used a consistent local `pageCanvasStyle` object in each page component to avoid duplicating the same style values inline.

- Fixed a pre-existing test helper issue where `setTheme` used `page.evaluate` before `page.goto`, causing `SecurityError` on `localStorage` access. Changed to navigate first, then set localStorage.

author: bdunk881
body:
Closes HEL-656 — the spine of the dynamic connector-action library (HEL-647). Builds on HEL-650 (`ActionContext`) + HEL-651 (Slack `sendMessage`), both merged.

## What this is

The first piece of Brad's vision: a **library of available functions** the engine dispatches against generically, so a newly-built+connected connector's actions light up in the DAG without editing the engine. This replaces the hardcoded `actionRegistry.set("slack.notify", …)` per-action wiring.

## Change

- **New `src/engine/connectorActions/`** — `ConnectorActionDef { connectorKey, actionId, label, isWrite, connectionProvider?, invoke }` + `ConnectorActionInvocation { userId, connectionId?, inputs, config, step }` + a `Map`-backed registry (`register`/`get`/`list`).
- **`executeAction` consults the library first** (on HEL-650's `ActionContext`): a registered `actionId` dispatches to `invoke({ userId, connectionId, inputs, config, step })`, resolving credentials by the **run owner's `userId`** (`connectionId` from `step.config` selects among several). No run user → **honest throw** (step fails), never a fabricated success. Unmatched actions fall through to the legacy `actionRegistry` (`webhook.send` + the 4 stubs) unchanged.
- **Seeds real `slack.notify` / `slack.dispatchNotification`** → the run owner's connected Slack (`slackConnectorService.sendMessage`). The connector is imported **lazily inside `invoke`**, so registering the action stays cheap and never pulls the connector/credential vault into engine module-eval or unrelated engine tests.

## Scope (per Brad's calls)

- **Run-owner connections only** — resolve via `userId`; no workspace-scoped/cross-member resolution. `connectionId` is threaded for when the owner holds several Slack teams; resolving a *specific* connection (vs the active one) is a follow-up on the connector method.
- This PR is the **pattern + first real connector action**. Next: **catalog API** (`GET /api/connectors/actions`, connection-gated) → **builder** (dynamic palette + connection picker, replaces `CURATED_ACTIONS`/freetext) → **per-connector manifests** (HubSpot CRM, Gmail, Intercom, …) — each auto-appears in the catalog.

## Tests

`WorkflowEngine.connectorActions.test.ts` (7 cases): registry registers the slack actions; dispatch threads `userId`+`connectionId` to a probe action; `slack.notify` sends via the connector with the resolved channel/text; honest failures (not connected / no channel / no run user → no send); an action absent from the library falls through to the legacy registry.

- `npm run build` (tsc) clean
- engine suites green: `connectorActions` (new) + `actionHandlers` + `WorkflowEngine` + `replayFromStep` + `executeQueuedRun` + `lifecycle` + `stepHandlers` = **122 passed**
- CI guards: new registry `Map` carries the allowlist comment; no routes; no forbidden imports

author: nntin
body:
## Summary

Adds a per-project `mergeMethod` config option so users can choose how the dashboard merge action merges PRs. Default remains `"squash"` (backward compatible). Consumed by the dashboard merge route via `scm.mergePR`.

> **Note:** The `auto-merge` reaction is currently a notify-only stub and does not call `scm.mergePR`, so it does not consume `mergeMethod`. This option takes effect from the dashboard merge action.

### Strategies

| Method | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `squash` (default) | GitHub "Squash and merge" |
| `merge` | GitHub "Create a merge commit" |
| `rebase` | GitHub "Rebase and merge" |
| `merge-with-ff` | **AO composite strategy** (see below) |

### `merge-with-ff`

GitHub has **no fast-forward merge button** — `gh pr merge` only offers merge/squash/rebase, and `--merge` always creates a merge commit even when the branch could fast-forward. So `merge-with-ff` can't go through `gh pr merge`; it uses the Git Refs API directly:

1. Compare the PR head against base (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/compare/{base}...{head}`).
2. **If the branch is strictly ahead (no divergence):** fast-forward the base ref server-side — `PATCH /repos/{o}/{r}/git/refs/heads/{base}` with `force=false` (GitHub rejects anything that isn't a true fast-forward), then delete the head branch.
3. **If the branches have diverged:** fall back to a `--merge` commit.

This preserves linear history (no merge commit, no squash, no rebased SHAs) whenever possible.

### Config Usage

```yaml
projects:
  my-app:
    repo: owner/my-app
    path: ~/my-app
    mergeMethod: merge-with-ff   # fast-forward when possible, else merge commit
```

Options: `"squash"` (default), `"merge"`, `"rebase"`, `"merge-with-ff"`

## Files Changed

1. `packages/core/src/types.ts` — Add `"merge-with-ff"` to `MergeMethod` (with JSDoc), add `mergeMethod?` to `ProjectConfig`
2. `packages/core/src/config.ts` — Add `mergeMethod` to `ProjectConfigSchema` (default `"squash"`)
3. `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts` — `mergePR()` implements `merge-with-ff` via compare + Git Refs fast-forward, else merge commit
4. `packages/plugins/scm-gitlab/src/index.ts` — `mergePR()` throws for the unsupported `"merge-with-ff"` (no GitLab equivalent) instead of silently ignoring it
5. `packages/web/src/app/api/prs/[id]/merge/route.ts` — Reads `project.mergeMethod` instead of hardcoding `"squash"`

## Tests

- `scm-github`: `merge-with-ff` fast-forwards via Git Refs API when ahead (and never touches `gh pr merge`); falls back to `--merge` when diverged
- `scm-gitlab`: `merge-with-ff` throws and never shells out to `glab`
- web merge route: defaults to `squash`; reads and passes through `project.mergeMethod`

## Caveats

author: killov
body:
## Summary
- `@autowired` marked as `@deprecated` - it cannot work for code compiled with `useDefineForClassFields: true`. Native class fields are defined via `[[DefineOwnProperty]]` directly by the engine, the own property shadows the prototype accessor installed by the decorator and there is no runtime way to intercept it.
- instead of silently returning `undefined`, the container now throws: `Property a of class Bb is shadowed by class field, @autowired does not work for code compiled with useDefineForClassFields: true, use inject.lazy() instead.`
- new `ironbeanSettings.allowInjectOutsideComponent` - migration path for projects using `@autowired` in classes that are not `@component` (resolves from the base container, same as autowired did)
- every autowired test duplicated with an `inject.lazy` variant, running on all matrix targets including `es2022-define`

## Changes
**src**
- `useDefClassFiedsHack.ts` - `checkShadowedProps()` walks marked props and throws when an own property in field-init shape shadows the accessor (cached constants from the getter have a non-writable descriptor and never match)
- `classComponent.ts`, `component.ts`, `zaop.ts` - check called after construction in `ClassComponent.construct`, `Factory.construct` and the `createClassDecorator` construct trap
- `autowired.ts` - `@deprecated` JSDoc, propagates to `dist` typings
- `inject.ts`, `settings.ts` - `ironbeanSettings.allowInjectOutsideComponent` fallback to the base container, error message mentions the setting

**test**
- `emitMode.ts` - runtime detection of native field emit (probe class with a marked accessor; correctly returns false for the lowered `Object.defineProperty` emit which the monkeypatch intercepts)
- autowired tests skipped under native field emit via `itAutowired`, ~25 `\"... - inject\"` duplicates run everywhere

## Behavior differences of inject.lazy (encoded in tests)
- lazy proxy is not the raw bean - no `toBe`/`instanceof` against `getBean()` results, underlying instance is the same
- prototype components: `inject.lazy` resolves through its own component container, so constructor params get a different instance than the field (autowired shared it)
- `inject` outside `@component` throws unless `ironbeanSettings.allowInjectOutsideComponent` is enabled
- plugin `getContextForClassInstance` is bypassed by inject - the two plugin tests in `api.spec.ts` have no inject variant

## Test plan
- [x] `test:es5`, `test:es6`, `test:es2022` - 114 passed, 1 skipped (native-only exception test)
- [x] `test:es2022-define` - 76 passed, 39 skipped (autowired originals)
- [x] `tsc` build

author: kostandinang
body:
## Summary

A series of improvements hardening the brunch ⇄ Petrinaut integration — the live SSE view a cook run drives on Petrinaut's read-only "actual/live" canvas (`brunch cook --petrinaut-stream`). Each wire seam is locked behind an oracle so it can't regress silently. Read-only, one-way; no write-back.

## What Changed

- **Plain-graph wire contract** — Petrinaut narrowed its `definition` route to a `.strict()` schema (plain places/transitions/arcs). `NetDefinition` / `projectNetDefinition` slimmed to match, dropping `types` and all SDCPN-only fields that would otherwise be rejected; backed by an in-repo schema mirror + a compile-time drift pin.
- **Arc-scoped delta firings** — every `transition_firing` carries only the transition's consume/produce delta (`input` = tokens consumed from input-arc places, `output` = the **new tokens** to add to output-arc places), never places the transition isn't connected to. `initialState` is the single full marking; Petrinaut reconstructs the running net state by folding each delta onto it. Count-only. _(Reverses an earlier full-marking approach per the Petrinaut team's confirmation — SPEC A99.)_
- **Run-state legibility** — leading `status` frame, `terminal` carries `{ state, reason }`, halts re-emit a status-suffixed title; synthetic `run:completed` / `run:halted` places + a `run:finish` firing surface the outcome on the flat canvas. Presentation-only.
- **Mechanical lane projection** — `--petrinaut-lanes=mechanical` hides the semantic lane for a smaller demo graph; execution unchanged (frames restrict to surviving nodes).
- **Launcher** — `--petrinaut-base-url` → `--petrinaut-url` (full route, no alias); link is `{PETRINAUT_URL}?runId=…&sse=…`; `.env` is shell-wins. Help lists every flag.

## Consequence

Colour-fold slice identity has no carrier on this interface — identity fold is the only meaningful stream fold until the standardized protocol lands in Petrinaut Core. SPEC §Lexicon + decisions/invariants reconciled.

**Open follow-up (A99 watch):** re-verify on staging that delta firings don't regress the 2026-06-05 "pools/budgets empty mid-run" rendering — i.e. confirm Petrinaut folds deltas onto `initialState` rather than treating `output` as a whole frame.

## Verification

`npm run verify` passes (format/lint, full suite, build). Oracles: schema-mirror validation + compile-time pin (definition), arc-scoped delta oracle + replay-equivalence (markings), lane-projection tests, flag-completeness test (CLI).

author: stanfish06
body:
## What

`lua/config/plugin_config.lua:115` had a version-guarded opts table for the `gd` buffer-local keymap that contained a bug on two levels:

```lua
-- before
local opts = vim.fn.has('nvim-0.12') == 1 and { buf = ev.buf } or { buffer = ev.buf }
vim.keymap.set("n", "gd", vim.lsp.buf.definition, opts)
```

**Problem 1 — invalid key `buf`**: `vim.keymap.set` accepts `buffer` for a buffer-local keymap, not `buf`. Passing `{ buf = ev.buf }` is silently ignored, so on nvim-0.12+ `gd` was registered as a *global* map rather than buffer-local — it would apply in every buffer regardless of which LSP was attached.

**Problem 2 — inverted condition**: the branch that returned the *wrong* key (`buf`) was guarded by `has('nvim-0.12') == 1`, i.e. the newest code path was also the broken one.

## Where

`lua/config/plugin_config.lua`, lines 115–116 (inside the `LspAttach` autocmd callback).

## Fix

```lua
-- after
vim.keymap.set("n", "gd", vim.lsp.buf.definition, { buffer = ev.buf })
```

`buffer` is the correct, documented key for buffer-local keymaps in `vim.keymap.set` and has been so since Neovim 0.7. The version check is unnecessary and removed.

## Risk

Low — this restores the *intended* behaviour (buffer-local `gd`). The only visible change is that `gd` no longer leaks into buffers that have no LSP attached.

body:
## Summary

Last wave of the [full-project review](./CODE_REVIEW.md) — quality / performance / dead-code findings. Mostly small, low-risk janitorial changes; a few sit on a hot path.

### Perf / correctness
- **rustls `install_default` runs once.** `TuicOutbound::new` previously called it on every construction and silently swallowed the post-first `Err`. Now guarded by `static OnceLock<()>`.
- **`tuic-server::acl` zero-alloc Display.** `format_protocol` returns `&'static str`; `format_optional_parts` returns a `Display` wrapper. Both were on the rule-pretty-print hot path.
- **`wind-tuic::quinn::inbound::acceptor_loop`**: `ApplicationClosed`/`LocallyClosed`/`TimedOut` no longer logged as `ERROR` (they're benign connection-lifecycle events). Demoted to `DEBUG`.

### Quality / safety
- **`wind::log` filter** now lists every wind crate; `wind_acme`/`wind_base`/`wind_dns`/`wind_naive` were missing and silently fell through to the default INFO.
- **`WIND_OVERRIVE_VERSION` typo fixed.** Canonical name is now `WIND_OVERRIDE_VERSION`; old (misspelled) name kept as a fallback for one release.
- **`tuic-client::wind_adapter` SNI**: when no `sni` is configured AND `relay.server.0` is an IP literal, emit a loud warning and use a placeholder instead of stuffing the IP into the TLS SNI extension.
- **`wind/main.rs` clap parsing**: actual errors go to stderr with non-zero exit via `Error::exit()`. Version/help still go to stdout with exit 0.
- **`wind-socks::SocksInbound::new`** is no longer `async` — never awaited anything. Two callers updated.
- **`wind-socks::ext` UDP proxy**: replaced misleading `warn!(\"unreachable\")` with `debug!(\"completed cleanly\")` on the happy path.
- **`wind-tuic::proto::cmd`**: dropped the typo'd rebind `assoc_id: assos_id` in encode arms.

### Dead code removed (~150 lines net)

body:
## Summary

A menu document — not a queue — synthesised from a five-agent fan-out across the four cohorts you flagged as worth comparing against. Captures **what Hummingbird could borrow** from other OSS + commercial AI / chat / agent products, with verified primary sources and concrete fits to existing surfaces.

## Three top picks (from the executive summary)

1. **Workspace-level system prompt that layers under the agent persona** (Claude / ChatGPT Projects pattern). Smallest delta, fills a real gap, foundation for everything below. Days, not weeks.
2. **Letta-style three-tier self-editing memory** (closes the planned cross-conversation memory with a known-working contract rather than reinventing). The "agent edits its own memory via `core_memory_*` and `archival_memory_*` tools" shape is the part embed-on-write retrieval misses. Maps onto Supabase pgvector that's already wired for `searchFiles`.
3. **Langfuse self-hosted** for tracing + prompt management + LLM-as-judge evals across all three backends. Single Docker stack covers cost visibility, distributed-trace debugging across Next.js + agent-py + agent-ts, and a regression net before every Anthropic model swap.

Honourable mention: **Msty Flowchat-style canvas-of-branches** — wire conversation forks to land as nodes on the existing workspace canvas. Pure composition of two surfaces Hummingbird already has; no other chat client in the cohort ships this.

## Plan structure (in the file)

- **Executive summary** — three top picks + rationale.
- **By-cohort sections** — 2–4 standouts per cohort with one-line "why for Hummingbird" + a verified primary source.
- **Prioritised plan** — 10 headline items + 4 stretch items, each scoped S/M/L and tagged with the existing Hummingbird surfaces it composes with and the product(s) that inspired it.
- **Skip list** — 7 explicitly-rejected patterns with reasoning.
- **Open questions** — 3 strategic decisions to make before committing to specific items.
- **Sources + Verification notes** — every external claim cited; 8 vendor-marketing-vs-shipped-reality discrepancies flagged.

## Notable skip-list entries

- **Helicone** — acquired by Mintlify 2026-03-03, maintenance-mode. Don't take a code dep; borrow the `Helicone-Property-*` custom-property header pattern only.
- **AutoGen Studio** — explicitly "not production-ready"; Microsoft is steering users to Agent Framework.
- **CrewAI hierarchical delegation** — documented "Delegation Ping-Pong" OOM crash mode where two `allow_delegation=True` agents bounce a task until process death.
- **Mem.ai-style "AI auto-linking"** as a headline feature — reviewers consistently report the linker is too inconsistent for power users; retrieval quality (FTS + reranker + eventually vectors) is the actual product.
- **Browser-extension companion** — Chrome Web Store ops + cross-browser maintenance is a substantial side-business.

## Open questions

The doc surfaces three strategic decisions that gate specific items:

1. **Multi-tenant timeline** — gates Open WebUI Channels, LiteLLM per-workspace virtual keys, ChatGPT-Projects-style sharing.
2. **Eval-writing investment** — gates Langfuse value (a trace/cost dashboard with no eval suite is measurable productivity-loss).
3. **Memory editor surface** — visible blocks (Letta) vs hidden (ChatGPT Memory); decide before coding Letta-style memory.

## What's NOT in this PR

No code changes. No new PLAN-*.md spawned for any individual item — that comes when capacity opens up. Treat as a menu to draw from, not a sequenced roadmap.

author: liranfarhi
body:
## Summary

The persona carousel felt "stuck" when dragging left/right. The drag updated the track's transform through React state (`setTx`) on **every `pointermove`**, forcing a full render per frame and dropping frames on touch devices.

### Fix
- **Drive the transform imperatively on the DOM during the drag** (no React renders per frame) so it follows the pointer 1:1.
- **Hand control back to React for the animated snap on release.** `flushSync` primes the CSS transition before the snap, so releasing right after a settle still animates instead of jumping (a transition/transform same-frame race).
- Add `will-change: transform` for GPU compositing.

### Verification
Scripted Playwright drag test confirms: transform follows the pointer exactly each step, `transition` is `none` while dragging and restored after, and three consecutive drags (incl. the race-prone path) each animate and land on the correct persona.

author: chrismatix
body:
Stacked on top of #159. **Merge that first.**

## What it does

Push plans used to call `SetStatus` once and then run silently while `remote.Write` streamed bytes. On a 1 GB image the tea UI sat on the same line for tens of seconds. After this, the tea UI shows a byte-progress bar for the active push, matching what cache writes already do via \`consumeDockerProgress\`.

## How

- \`oci_push.Options.Progress\` is a new \`chan<- v1.Update\` field. \`Copy\` forwards it to \`remote.Write\` via \`remote.WithProgress\`.
- Both backends' \`PushImage\` spin a \`pushProgressBridge\` (new) that drains the channel into a \`SubTracker(total)\`. \`go-containerregistry\` reports one \`(Total, Complete)\` pair across the whole copy — no per-blob breakdown — so a single \`SubTracker\` is the right granularity.
- The bridge handles initial \`Total=0\` events, monotonic byte growth, and the rare retry-resets-Complete edge case. \`stop()\` is idempotent and drains queued updates before returning so the final byte count always reaches the parent tracker.

## Tests

Unit tests for the bridge: \`AggregatesByteUpdates\` (the happy path), \`NilParent_NoCrash\` (parent==nil disables cleanly), \`IgnoresZeroTotal\` (waits for go-containerregistry to figure out the manifest before creating the sub-tracker).

body:
This PR does two different but related things:
- Changes the names of arguments in functions and events to their Wiki names.
- Completes and improves the tooltips for functions, events, their arguments, and constants.

I originally wanted to make two separate PRs, but some of the tooltips refer to the argument names, so they have to go together. 
Everything was generated by script, so there shouldn't be any manual typos, only potential scripting errors.

Why change the argument names to match the Wiki?
- Avoids keyword conflicts: Some current Yaml arguments are named Key, Vector, or Rotation. If we lowercase them directly, they become reserved keywords in LSL/Lua and break. Using the Wiki names avoids this.
- Standardization: Yaml names currently start with an uppercase letter, which isn't standard in Lua.
- Accuracy: Wiki names have been heavily checked and corrected by the community over time.
- Conciseness: Wiki names are often shorter, whereas some of the current Yaml names are too verbose.
- Documentation consistency: The Wiki texts already use these argument names (Although hey could be changed, since usually they are in bold).

author: dotts-h
body:
## What

Implements **NEXT_FEATURES item 1.2 — Pre-flight turn cost estimate** (Tier 1, "make cost active").

Before a turn runs, the chat statusline now shows **`next turn ~N cr`**, derived from the price book × the live context-window fill, so the decision to *send* vs. *abort-and-compact* is informed instead of blind. Today the meter only observes spend after the fact; this is the first step in turning the gauge into a guardrail.

## How

- **`telemetry.EstimateTurn(pb, model, contextTokens) Cost`** — pure, total (nil price book or non-positive context → zero, never panics), a thin wrapper over `Price` that prices the current context as *fresh input* at the model's rate. **`Meter.EstimateTurn`** delegates with the meter's (settings-overridable) price book.
- **`renderStatline`** renders the estimate once a context reading has arrived (`ctxCurrent > 0`), refreshed by the existing `stat` SSE fragment on `EvContextWindow` / `EvUsage` / tool starts. No new route, event, or persisted schema — domain logic stays pure, no SDK surface.

Why price context as fresh input (vs. modelling cache hits + projected output): output length and cache-hit ratio are both unknowable before the turn; the resent context priced at the input rate is the one knowable, dominant component. Framed as `~` and "next turn" so it reads as a projection, not a bill. Full rationale in **ADR-0007**.

## Verification

End-to-end against the offline demo: after a scripted turn (18.4k context tokens, gpt-5) the statusline renders `next turn ~2.30 cr` (18,400 × $1.25/Mtok = $0.023 = 2.30 credits).

## Tests

- `internal/telemetry`: `TestEstimateTurn`, `TestEstimateTurnUnknownModelUsesFallback`, `TestEstimateTurnNonPositiveContextIsZero`, `TestEstimateTurnNilPriceBookIsZero`, `TestMeterEstimateTurnUsesItsPriceBook`.
- `internal/web`: `TestStatlineShowsPreflightEstimateAtCurrentContext`.
- `e2e`: "the statusline shows a pre-flight cost estimate once context is known".
- Gates: `make lint` clean, `make test` green (total coverage 77.8%, floor 65%), `make fuzz` green.

## Docs (folded into this branch per ADR-0004)

- **ADR-0007** — pre-flight estimate prices the live context as fresh input.
- `docs/issues/` — seeds the cost-awareness epic (0001) and closes item 1.2 (0002).

> Note: this branch also carries the two roadmap-research doc commits the effort is sequenced from (`NEXT_FEATURES.md`).

body:
Follow-up to #507 addressing the **Codex P2 review** (the review landed as #507 was merging, so this is a separate fix).

## 問題（codex review）
#507 の float 変数追跡は per-function の**名前セット**（`float_binding_names`）だったため、**同名・別型の shadowing を誤分類**:
- `let x = 1.5; let y = { let x = 1; x + 2 }; y` — 内側の整数 `x + 2` が外側の float `x` にマッチして f64 経路に
- if/match 分岐でも同様（`local_names` は分岐間で truncate されるが名前セットはされない → スロット再利用でリーク）

## 修正: 名前ではなく**スロット**で追跡
- `CompileCtx.float_binding_names` → `float_local_slots : Array[Int]`。float な `let`/`let mut` はその**スロット**（local_idx）を登録
- `expr_is_floatish` は `local_names` を受け取り、`EIdent` をスロット解決（最新束縛優先、codegen と同じ）→ スロット membership で判定。**高いスロットの別型 shadow は正しく非 float**
- `float_local_slots` を **scope 境界（if 分岐・match arm）で `local_names` と一緒に truncate** → 兄弟 scope のスロット再利用でリークしない

## 検証（全 green）
- 回帰テスト（default + RC）: 内側 int shadow → 整数 `3`、if 分岐でのスロット再利用 → `6`
- **heap-e2e 100/100**、**byte-parity 74/74**、**selfbuild/bootstrap** deterministic、`moon check` clean

## 残る限界（AST 無型）
`Double` 型の関数パラメータ・lambda キャプチャ float は未追跡（完全一般化には型推論 thread が必要）。ローカル束縛の一般ケースは正しく動作。

author: noanflaherty
body:
## Summary
- Removed `mirrorCsrfCookie` which tried to set cookies on the `app://` scheme (unsupported by Chromium's cookie store, causing an unhandled rejection that crashed the protocol handler)
- Replaced with main-side CSRF injection: `captureCsrfToken` extracts the token from platform `Set-Cookie` headers into a module-level cache, and `forwardPlatformRequest` injects `X-CSRFToken` into forwarded requests before they hit the platform
- `net.fetch`'s own cookie jar handles the cookie side of Django's CSRF check; the cached token supplies the header side — no renderer-side cookie access needed

## Original prompt
The Electron DMG build was showing a blank white screen on launch. Debugging revealed a terminal error: `Failed to set cookie - Attempted to set a cookie from a scheme that does not support cookies.EXCLUDE_NONCOOKIEABLE_SCHEME`. The `app://` protocol scheme isn't cookieable in Chromium, so the old `mirrorCsrfCookie` approach (writing the CSRF token into the renderer's cookie jar) threw an unhandled rejection that crashed the protocol handler. This broke all platform API calls, preventing the web UI from rendering. The fix needed to work in both packaged DMG builds and local dev-from-source, and avoid changes to the platform repo.

body:
This PR implements the full set of applicant-facing requirements for the AI Interview plugin.

Key features:
1. **Applicant Navigation**: End-to-end flow from job details to application success.
2. **Eligibility Gates**: Blocks applications if the required minimum score (highest of all attempts) is not met.
3. **Credit/Sponsor Gating**: Integrates with the credit system and sponsor invites to control access to interviews.
4. **Enhanced Tracking**: My Applications now shows attempt counts, latest score dates, and supports various sort orders.
5. **Automated Notifications**: Sends emails to applicants and vendors upon interview completion, application submission, and status updates.
6. **UI Integration**: Uses a ViewComponent Widget to display contextual messages (e.g., insufficient credits) on the core nopCommerce product details page.

Architectural improvements:
- Resolved decoupling issues by avoiding direct dependencies on Nop.Web models.
- Correctly implemented IWidgetPlugin and IEventConsumer interfaces.
- Ensured vendor notifications can identify context even before a JobApplication exists by capturing ProductId in the InterviewSession.
- All validation messages and notifications are now fully localizable.

author: bbolek
body:
The terminal's buildTheme() read --text-primary / --bg-primary, CSS
variables that are never defined, so it always fell back to hardcoded
dark colors regardless of the selected theme — under GitHub Light the
terminal stayed dark.

Read the real theme tokens (--color-bg / --color-text) instead, and
select a light or dark ANSI 16-color palette from the resolved scheme
(data-scheme on <html>) so colors stay legible on a light background.
A MutationObserver on data-theme / data-scheme recolors open terminals
live when the theme or light/dark mode changes.

author: kallilsouza
body:
### What
This branch increases the effective throughput of the room-archiving pipeline and removes a class of duplicate-processing races. Three coordinated changes:
1. **Dispatch-time repointing** in `_create_pending_records` (`chats/apps/archive_chats/tasks.py`). The function now runs inside a single `transaction.atomic()` block and, before bulk-creating PENDING rows for new rooms, issues an `update(job=current_job)` against every existing non-FINISHED `RoomArchivedConversation` row in the dispatch batch. After this, the scheduler's 24-hour filter on `archived_conversations__job__started_at` reliably excludes those rooms on subsequent runs.
2. **Worker-side claim with soft lock** in `chats/apps/archive_chats/services.py`. `archive_room_history` no longer calls `_get_or_create_room_archived_conversation`. It now calls a new `_claim_room_for_archive` that:
   - Opens a short transaction and runs `select_for_update(skip_locked=True)` against the room's row.
   - Returns `None` (skip) when another worker holds the row, when the row is in an in-progress status with a recent `archive_process_started_at`, or when an `IntegrityError` proves a concurrent create lost the race.
   - Treats `FINISHED` as a short-circuit and `FAILED` as resumable.
   - Stamps `archive_process_started_at = now()`, re-points `job` if needed, commits, and only then runs the heavy work (`process_messages`, S3 upload, batched message deletion).
   - Reclaims rows whose `archive_process_started_at` exceeds `ARCHIVE_CHATS_IN_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_HOURS` so a crashed worker's row does not stay locked forever.
3. **New setting** `ARCHIVE_CHATS_IN_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_HOURS` (default `12`) in `chats/settings.py`, env-overridable, controlling the soft-lock window.
Tests: `tests/test_services.py` adds coverage for row-locked skip, recent in-progress soft-lock, stale-row reclaim, FAILED retry, `IntegrityError` race on create, and an explicit assertion that the heavy work runs outside the claim transaction. `tests/test_tasks.py` adds repoint-of-non-finished, no-repoint-of-finished, and a mixed create-and-repoint scenario. No migrations.
### Why
The scheduler caps each run at `ARCHIVE_CHATS_MAX_ROOMS` and excludes rooms whose `RoomArchivedConversation.job.started_at` is within the last 24 hours. Previously, `_create_pending_records` only created rows for rooms that had no `RoomArchivedConversation` at all — existing non-FINISHED rows kept pointing to whatever job dispatched them last. As soon as that job aged past 24 hours without the worker reaching FINISHED (long task, transient error, worker scale-down, crash), the scheduler picked the same room up again on the next run. The result was twofold:
- Per-run dispatch slots were spent re-queuing the same backlog instead of advancing through new candidates ordered by `ended_at`, so the number of rooms actually archived per run was lower than `ARCHIVE_CHATS_MAX_ROOMS` would suggest.
- When a duplicate task did fire while a previous attempt was still running, both workers ran the full archive pipeline against the same row with no row lock and no soft lock — overlapping S3 uploads and overlapping message deletions, which can produce a corrupted archive file (a worker reads messages that the other has just deleted).
Repointing at dispatch time closes the scheduler-side leak so the 24h filter does its job, and the row-level `select_for_update(skip_locked=True)` plus a configurable soft-lock window closes the worker-side race for the cases where a duplicate still slips through (overlapping scheduler runs, manual replay, retry-after-crash). Moving the heavy I/O outside the transaction keeps the row lock to milliseconds rather than holding it open for the duration of an S3 upload.
### Sequence diagram
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Sched as Scheduler task
    participant DB as Database
    participant Q as Celery queue
    participant W as Worker (archive_room_messages)
    participant Svc as ArchiveChatsService
    participant S3 as S3
    Sched->>DB: Select rooms (ended >1y, not FINISHED, job.started < now-24h)
    Sched->>DB: BEGIN
    Sched->>DB: UPDATE non-FINISHED rows SET job = current_job
    Sched->>DB: BULK INSERT PENDING rows for rooms with no row
    Sched->>DB: COMMIT
    Sched->>Q: Dispatch archive_room_messages(room, job) per room
    Q->>W: Deliver task
    W->>Svc: archive_room_history(room, job)
    Svc->>DB: BEGIN (claim transaction)
    Svc->>DB: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED WHERE room = ?
    alt Row locked by another worker
        DB-->>Svc: no row returned, but row exists
        Svc->>DB: ROLLBACK
        Svc-->>W: return None (skip)
    else Row missing entirely
        Svc->>DB: INSERT RoomArchivedConversation (PENDING)
        opt Concurrent insert wins the race
            DB-->>Svc: IntegrityError
            Svc->>DB: ROLLBACK
            Svc-->>W: return None (skip)
        end
    else Row already FINISHED
        Svc->>DB: COMMIT
        Svc-->>W: return row (caller short-circuits)
    else Row in-progress and started_at within timeout
        Svc->>DB: COMMIT
        Svc-->>W: return None (soft-lock skip)
    else Row reclaimable (PENDING, FAILED, or stale in-progress)
        Svc->>DB: UPDATE archive_process_started_at = now, job = current_job
        Svc->>DB: COMMIT (lock released)
        Svc->>DB: Iterate messages in batches
        Svc->>S3: Upload archive file
        S3-->>Svc: OK
        Svc->>DB: Mark MESSAGES_FILE_UPLOADED
        Svc->>DB: Batched delete of messages
        Svc->>DB: Mark FINISHED + archive_process_finished_at
        Svc-->>W: return row
    end
```

author: segattihall-ops
body:
## Problem

On the homepage "Live Demo" section, **both** the live demo and the scripted sample stopped working. Root cause:

- The widget connected with a **public `agentId` over WebRTC**. If the agent requires auth, `startSession` sets status to `connecting` and never resolves.
- That `connecting` state renders the live view (only "End conversation"), which **hides the "watch a sample call" button** — so the sample becomes unreachable too. There was no `onError` or timeout to recover.

## Fix

- Switch the homepage widget to the **signed-URL method** (`/api/demo/conversation-token` + `@elevenlabs/client`) — the exact approach already proven to return `200` and work on `/demo/[slug]`.
- Add a **12s connection timeout** + `onError` handling that **always falls back to the scripted sample**, so the section can never get stuck. "Connecting…" now also has a **Cancel** button.
- Re-add the `home` demo persona ("Apex Home Services") so the agent has a natural name.

## Note / follow-up

The floating `VoiceAgent` button still uses the public-`agentId` WebRTC method. If it also fails to connect, it has the same root cause and should be switched to signed-URL too — happy to do that in a follow-up (kept out here to avoid changing that agent's behavior without confirmation).

## Verification

`npm run build` passes. Requires `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` + `ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID` (already set — `conversation-token` returns 200 in prod).

author: mikemaccana
body:
## Summary

`basics/realloc/native` and `basics/cross-program-invocation/native` were excluded in `.github/.ghaignore` as "build and test error". I investigated — the real cause was their LiteSVM Rust tests pointing `include_bytes!()` at `target/deploy/<program>.so`, while `build-and-test` compiles the program `.so` into `tests/fixtures/`. So `cargo test` failed to even compile (file not found).

## Fixes

**`realloc/native`**
- Fix the `include_bytes!()` path → `../../tests/fixtures/realloc_program.so`. Test passes.

**`cross-program-invocation/native`**
- Fix both `include_bytes!()` paths → `tests/fixtures/`.
- A second, subtler bug: `hand` depends on `lever` with the `cpi` (= `no-entrypoint`) feature. Building the whole workspace in one `cargo build-sbf` unified that feature onto `lever`, producing an **entrypoint-less `lever.so` (896 bytes)** that LiteSVM rejected with `InvalidAccountData`. `build-and-test` now builds each program **separately**, so `lever.so` keeps its entrypoint (81 KB) and the CPI test passes.

**Both**
- Remove the dead TypeScript suites: realloc's was a false-green `node:test`-under-`ts-mocha` suite (plus its now-unused `ts/` client helpers); cpi's was a localnet-only test (reads `~/.config/solana/id.json`). Strip their JS tooling, regenerate the lockfiles, and rewire `build-and-test` to just build the fixtures the LiteSVM `cargo test` consumes.
- Drop both from `.github/.ghaignore` so CI builds and tests them.

All verified locally against the CI toolchain (Solana 3.1.14 / platform-tools v1.52): full `install → build-and-test → cargo test` is green for both. `realloc-program` (a root workspace member) also passes `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy -D warnings`.

> Note: `cross-program-invocation/native` is its own cargo workspace (not a member of the root workspace), so `rust.yml`'s clippy doesn't lint it; its CI is build + test via `native.yml`, which is green.

body:
## What does this PR do?

The engine simulates **emotion, memory and goals** (Week 3 — Trajectory), but the facade did not expose them, so the inspection panel could only show traits and needs. This surfaces the trajectory through the read-only DTO and uses it in the panel — the narrative hook "same traits, different history → different mood/behavior" is now visible.

- **`dto`**: `PersonDTO` gains `emotion`, `memory` (`MemoryTraceDTO`) and `goals` (`GoalDTO`).
  - `emotion` is **recomputed from memory** via `systems.emotion` at DTO-build time and never stored — honors **ADR-0006** ("no stored mood").
  - `memory`/`goals` are copied into frozen DTOs, preserving DTO isolation (**ADR-0011**, covered by the existing mutation test).
- **`facade/__init__`**: export `MemoryTraceDTO` and `GoalDTO`.
- **`view`**: bipolar **Ánimo** meter (`[-1,1]`, warm on the negative side / green on the positive, with a zero center mark) + an **Objetivos** section listing active goals and their progress.

### Verification
- `ruff` clean, **55** green tests (1 new facade test: DTO emotion equals the pure function; memory/goals form over a 60-day run).
- Probed seed 42 / 60 days: 7 agents with memory, 34 with active/!inactive goals — trajectory leaves a population trace.
- Rendered the enriched panel headless and reviewed the layout (everything fits the panel height).

## Type of change

body:
## Incident Details
- **ServiceNow Incident:** INC0010175
- **Service:** inventory-service
- **Severity:** P1 Critical
- **Error:** HighErrorRate_InventoryService

## Root Cause
The inventory-service contained a deliberate random failure mechanism on line 24 of `inventory-service/app.py`:
```python
failure = random.choice([True, False])
```

This caused approximately 50% of all requests to the `/inventory/<item>` endpoint to fail with:
- ConnectionPoolExhausted errors
- Database Connection Timeout failures
- HTTP 500 responses

This resulted in order placement failures in the order-service, as it depends on inventory checks.

## Fix Applied
Removed the random failure logic and associated error handling code. The service now:
- Always returns successful responses for valid inventory requests
- Properly logs all requests
- Maintains Prometheus metrics for monitoring
- Returns consistent HTTP 200 responses with inventory data

## Changes Made
- Removed `import random` (no longer needed)
- Removed `failure = random.choice([True, False])` logic
- Removed the conditional error block that simulated database failures
- Simplified the endpoint to always return successful inventory data

## Testing
After this fix:
- All requests to `/inventory/<item>` will return HTTP 200
- Error rate will drop from 50% to 0%
- Order-service will be able to successfully place orders
- No more ConnectionPoolExhausted or Database Connection Timeout errors

## Related
- Incident: INC0010175
- Branch: fix/inc0010175-connection-pool-exhausted

## RFC #6 — Feature relation chain

- **New `/pdlc-relate`** — `set` / `query` / `impact` / `orphans` / `rebuild` / `validate`. The `impact <fid>` command reports a change's blast radius (direct / transitive / historical).

author: jsiek
body:
## Summary

Fixes #857. Inside an `equations` block, neither side of a step could carry a low-precedence logical connective (`or`, `and`, `iff`) without parentheses — the parser stopped at the connective expecting `=`/`by`:

```deduce
equations
  P or (Q or R)  = (P or Q) or R   by .   // previously a parse error
```

The root cause is that the step-separator `=` shares its token with the boolean-equality `=` operator, which binds *more tightly* than `and`/`or`/`iff`. So there was no precedence level that included those connectives but excluded the separator `=`.

## Fix

Introduce an `equation_side` nonterminal that parses `iff`/`and`/`or` directly on top of comparison terms, leaving the top-level `=` to separate the two sides of the step:

```
?equation: equation_side "=" equation_side reason
?equation_side: eqs_iff_term
?eqs_iff_term:     eqs_iff_term ("iff"|"<=>"|"⇔") eqs_logical_term | eqs_logical_term
?eqs_logical_term: eqs_logical_term ("and"|"or") comparison_term  | comparison_term
```

Both parsers implement this (LALR grammar + recursive-descent `parse_equation_side`), left-associatively, and produce **identical ASTs** (checked by `test-deduce.py --equiv`). The change also removes a latent RD/LALR asymmetry: the LALR grammar previously restricted the equation RHS to `additive_term` while recursive-descent allowed `comparison_term`; both now use `equation_side`.

No new keywords or tokens are introduced (the connectives already existed), so the highlighting/keyword files are unaffected. The Reference.md equation grammar is updated to match (verified by `gh_pages/scripts/reference_grammar.py`).

## Testing

- New `test/should-validate/equation-logic-connectives.pf` exercises `or`, `and`, and `iff` on both sides plus a chained `... =` step; validates under both parsers.
- `make static` clean; full `test-deduce.py` green (lib + should-validate + should-error + prelude + equiv); `--parser` and `--site` suites green.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
Fixes the three independent correctness-review findings for `skills/re-frame2-pair` (bead rf2-a85bb2). All three are distinct from merged **rf2-pok18**, which scoped only the re-authoring `spec/*` + `docs/initial-spec.md` drift gate (verified: that gate's `SCOPED_FILES` does not include any file touched here).

## Findings + fixes

**1. Missing public preload-package install (high)** — `README.md` / `SKILL.md`
The install flow installed only the MCP server (`@day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp`, global) but pointed `:source-paths` at `node_modules/@day8/re-frame2-pair/preload` — a package never installed. The preload lives in the **separate** `@day8/re-frame2-pair` package (the skill's own `package.json`, which ships `preload/`). A clean consumer following the README configured the server correctly but failed every session with `:runtime-not-preloaded`.
- Added `npm install -D @day8/re-frame2-pair` as an explicit install step (README §Install, SKILL.md §Setup).
- Qualified the over-broad "No extra deps" / "no changes to your code/project" claims to name the one build-config (preload) change.
- Noted in `LOCAL_DEV.md` that the clone/symlink path needs no package install (preload comes off the linked skill dir).

**2. wire-size-budget.md subscribe-dedup slot (high)** — `references/wire-size-budget.md`
Said dedup fires on the per-tick `:events` vector only. The subscribe payload slot is **topic-dependent** (per `streaming-subscriptions.md`): `:events` for flat topics (`:epoch` / `:frameless`), `:cascades` for cascade-bundle topics (`:trace` / `:fx` / `:error`). A host decoding off `:events` alone would leave trace/fx/error dedup ticks unexpanded. Updated to name both slots; added a prompt-regression guard mirroring the existing `streaming-progress-payload-matches-impl` test.

**3. render-key handler-meta resolution (high)** — `references/recipes.md`, `docs/capabilities.md`
The dispatch-explanation recipe told an agent to pass the whole `:render-key` to `handler-meta {kind: \"view\"}`. The schema (`Spec-Schemas.md` `:rf/epoch-record` `:renders`) defines `:render-key` as the tuple `[<view-id-or-:rf.view/anonymous> <instance-token>]`; `handler-meta :view` is keyed by the **first** slot. Passing the tuple yields `:not-registered`. Recipe now resolves coords from `(first render-key)`, handles `:rf.view/anonymous` via `read-ui`'s `:source-coord` fallback; `capabilities.md` no longer calls `:render-key` "opaque pending spec finalisation". Added a structural guard.

## Quality gates
- `bb tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` — **19 tests, 72 assertions, 0 failures** (17 pre-existing + 2 new: `wire-size-budget-names-both-subscribe-slots`, `render-key-recipe-uses-first-tuple-slot`).
- `check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py` (incl. `--self-test`), `check_skill_mcp_drift.py`, `check_skill_package_refs.py`, `check_skill_redirect_anchors.py`, `check_skill_migration_cites.py` — all exit 0.
- `check_doc_slugs.py` — exit 0.
- `evals.json` untouched (no reference to changed content).

## Disposition
All three findings reproduced against current source and fixed; none was already resolved by rf2-pok18. Lane respected: changes scoped entirely to `skills/re-frame2-pair/**`. GENERIC (applies to any consumer app). No back-compat shims, no day8 coupling.

Closes rf2-a85bb2.

## 概要

E2EE 移行 E7 (#114) §16.5 鍵未設定ロックの **最終段 (PR-4b-3)**。`migration-lock-stale` (PR-4b-2 #372) でロックされてから猶予 60 日を過ぎても鍵設定も退会もしなかったユーザーを自動退会させる運用 CLI を追加する。これで §16.5 の運用フローが **3 段すべて (ロック解決UI 4b-1 / 30日自動ロック 4b-2 / 60日自動退会 4b-3)** 揃って完結する。

## 変更内容

- **`flask migration-purge-locked`**: 対象 = `personal` ・ `is_active=False` ・ `public_key IS NULL` ・ `locked_at < now - MIGRATION_PURGE_GRACE_DAYS(既定60)日`。各対象を `delete_user_account` (既存サービス) で物理削除 (電帳法対象の `VoucherAuditLog` は匿名化保持)。

## Description

Closes #23930.

Adds a clean collapse toggle for the Explore view's left sidebar so the chart and results area can use the full width.

- **Collapse** button in the sidebar header — works in both the field-selector view (`ExplorePanel`) and the Tables view (`BasePanel`).
- When collapsed, the sidebar fully hides and the content reclaims the width; a persistent **full-height gutter** holds an "Open sidebar" control to bring it back.
- Mirrors the existing **SqlRunner** pattern (plain `isSidebarOpen` show/hide) rather than the Settings pin/peek floating-overlay pattern (#23623) — no hover-to-reveal.
- Saved-chart view keeps this scoped to **edit mode** (view mode behaviour unchanged).

## Implementation

- New `SidebarToggleButtons.tsx`: `CollapseSidebarButton` (header) + `SidebarOpenGutter` (collapsed rail).
- `Explorer.tsx` / `SavedExplorer.tsx`: local `isSidebarOpen` state wired to `Page`'s `isSidebarOpen`; collapse handler threaded through `ExploreSideBar` → `ExplorePanel`/`BasePanel`.
- Storybook story (`ExplorerSidebarCollapse.stories.tsx`) documenting button placement, icon, and the collapsed gutter.

## How to test

1. Open an Explore (`/projects/:uuid/tables` or a saved chart in edit mode).
2. Click the collapse button at the top-right of the sidebar header → sidebar hides, content goes full width, an "Open sidebar" rail appears on the left.
3. Click "Open sidebar" → sidebar returns. Hovering the edge does nothing (no peek).

author: broomva
body:
## What

Every newly-bootstrapped workspace now inherits an explicit **Development Philosophy** section in its scaffolded `AGENTS.md` (+ a short anchor in `CLAUDE.md`), so downstream development follows the philosophy by default — cohesively with the user's own project. Previously the scaffold deployed the *mechanism* (the P1–P20 contract) without the *intent*.

Closes BRO-1406.

## Why

The 20 primitives are the *how*; new repos got no *why*. The most-starred public CLAUDE.md (`multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills`, ~168k★) proves enormous demand for four guiding principles — Think Before Coding · Simplicity First · Surgical Changes · Goal-Driven Execution — but leaves them as **prose ritual**. bstack's edge is the Ritual-vs-Substance rule: each principle is bound to the primitive that makes it machine-checkable (Think→P14+P15, Simplicity→P20, Surgical→P10, Goal→P11+P19).

## Changes

- `assets/templates/AGENTS.md.template` — new `## Development Philosophy` section between Self-Meta Definition and the primitives table (the *why* frames the *how*): 4-principle → enforcing-primitive table + the binding Ritual-vs-Substance rule + an explicit "extend it with your own principles" invitation.
- `assets/templates/CLAUDE.md.template` — short philosophy anchor → `AGENTS.md#development-philosophy`.
- `references/new-workspace-flow.md` — deployed-files note updated.
- `CHANGELOG.md` + `VERSION` → 0.24.0.

## Dep-chain

- **Upstream:** the four principles (Karpathy lineage + Ritual-vs-Substance rule), mapped to existing primitives. KG: `research/entities/tool/karpathy-claude-md-guidelines.md`.
- **Downstream:** `scripts/bootstrap.sh` Phase 2 (`scaffold_governance_file`) copies templates verbatim → **no code change needed**. Idempotent-never-overwrite → **new** installs get it; existing workspaces unaffected (backfill is a deferred `bstack doctor`/`repair` follow-up).
- Primitive count unchanged (**20**) — governance-substrate content, not a P-row (respects L3 stability budget λ₃≈0.006).

## Verification (P11)

Ran the real scaffold into a temp git repo (`BSTACK_SKIP_SKILLS/RCS=1`): both `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` contain the section, all 4 principle rows present, `{{WORKSPACE_NAME}}` substituted (`# fresh-repo — Agent Guidelines`).

## Deferred (follow-ups, not in this PR)

1. `bstack doctor` lint for the section (makes it contract-enforced; lets `repair` backfill existing workspaces).
2. Dogfood into bstack's own root governance + `~/broomva`.

body:
Mirrors blemees-agent's GitHub Actions setup — the universally-applicable parts (CI + templates). Release / Homebrew-tap / docs-sync are intentionally out of scope (see below).

## Added

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — three jobs, matching blemees-agent:
  - **lint**: `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .`
  - **test**: pytest matrix — py3.10/3.11/3.12 on Linux + 3.12 on macOS (adapted to this project's `requires-python>=3.10`; no OS-specific code paths, so no full grid)
  - **package**: `uv build` → sdist + wheel artifact
- **PR + issue templates** (`PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug_report,feature_request,config}`), adapted to this project (state-machine model, `validate-workflow`, tracker-agnostic scope, security policy).

## Lint/format prep (first commit)

The lint job gates on a clean tree, so this also fixes the pre-existing ruff findings and formats the repo. Two were **real bugs already on `main`**:

- **F821** — `registry` was undefined in `cli.py:_do_collect_into` on the `collects.process is None` path; now built via `build_registry` like sibling handlers.
- **F811** — a duplicate `test_collects_forbidden_on_working` (a rename collision from the ADR-0002 work) that silently shadowed the original test.
- Plus B904, unused-import / quoted-annotation / `collections.abc.Sequence` cleanups, and `ruff format` across the tree.

## Verified locally

`ruff check` clean · `ruff format --check` clean · `pytest` green · `uv build` produces sdist+wheel.

## Intentionally NOT mirrored

`release.yml` / `bump-tap.yml` / `docs-sync.yml` — there's no `workflow.rb` tap formula, no PyPI Trusted Publisher (package name is the generic `workflow`), and no GitHub Pages setup. Happy to add these in a follow-up once those prerequisites are decided.
