author: jklondon
body:
## Problem

Mainnet execution fails at block **25202264** (Osaka) with:

```
[4/6 Execution] invalid block, txnIdx=338, gas used by execution: 33961963, in header: 33888325, headerNum=25202264
```

EIP-7778 (*Block Gas Accounting without Refunds*) ships in **Osaka**, but the block-level gas accounting in `TransitionDb` was gated on `rules.IsAmsterdam`. On Osaka mainnet (`IsOsaka=true`, `IsAmsterdam=false` — mainnet has no `amsterdamTime`) block gas fell through to the post-refund, EIP-7623-floored per-tx value:

```go
if rules.IsAmsterdam {          // never true on Osaka mainnet
    st.blockGasUsed = max(floor, st.blockGasUsed)
} else {
    st.blockGasUsed = gasUsed   // post-refund, WITH the EIP-7623 floor
}
```

For calldata-heavy txns the EIP-7623 floor exceeds actual execution gas, so summing the floored per-tx values over-counts the block vs. the canonical header. At block 25202264 the accumulated floor premium was **+73638** (33961963 vs 33888325).

## Fix

Gate the EIP-7778 accounting on `rules.IsOsaka` and use the actual **pre-refund** execution gas for block accounting: SSTORE refunds do not free up block capacity, and the EIP-7623 calldata floor is a minimum ETH payment only — it must not inflate block gas. The receipt (what the user pays) still uses the post-refund, floored value via `ReceiptGasUsed`, so receipts and `receiptHash` are unchanged.

This is the `release/3.4` equivalent of the `txn_executor.go` change on `main` (companion PR).

## Tests

Un-skips the `eip7778_block_gas_accounting_without_refunds` EEST fixtures, which were previously skipped with this exact error pattern (e.g. `test_varying_calldata_costs`: execution 51122 vs header 33800).

`make erigon` ✓ · `gofmt` / `go vet` ✓. (EEST fixtures run in CI.)

author: jrandallsexton
body:
## Summary

Two small mobile parity / screenshot-polish fixes that both fold into the same PR (same surface area, same intent: make the mobile app screenshot-ready).

### 1. Drop \`Picks Made\` label from the picks-counter chip

The header counter on the picks tab read \`X/Y Picks Made\`. The label suffix took real estate, made the chip visually heavy, and crowded marketing screenshots. Dropped the suffix; \`X/Y\` by itself is unambiguous in context (the user is already on the picks tab).

The \`All Picks Made\` celebration text on the completion branch is intentionally untouched — that copy is the success affordance and reads correctly without a counter.

### 2. Match web's inset team-row visual offset in MatchupCard

Web's \`.matchup-card\` uses \`var(--bg-primary)\` as the outer background while the inner \`.team-row\` uses \`var(--bg-card)\`. The team rows visually pop as inset cards inside the bordered outer container. Mobile didn't have that layering — the outer card used \`theme.card\` and team rows were transparent, so the matchup card looked flat next to its web counterpart.

Three coordinated changes:

- Outer card \`backgroundColor\` flipped from \`theme.card\` to \`theme.background\` (matches web's outer \`--bg-primary\`).
- Team row inline gets \`backgroundColor: theme.card\` (matches web's inner \`--bg-card\`).
- \`teamRow\` StyleSheet adds \`borderRadius: 8\` and \`marginBottom: 6\` (matches web's \`border-radius: 8px\` and \`margin-bottom: 0.5rem\`).

Net effect: the matchup card now reads as a bordered container holding two raised team-row cards inside, parity with the web gold standard.

## Test plan

- [ ] Picks tab header shows \`X/Y\` only while picks are in progress
- [ ] Completion banner still shows \`All Picks Made\` after the final pick
- [ ] Hide-picked toggle still renders and toggles correctly
- [ ] MatchupCard's away + home team rows now visually pop as inset cards on both light and dark themes
- [ ] Border / shadow on the outer MatchupCard still reads correctly with the new background

author: atstvi
body:
## Problem

Firebase free tier (50k reads / 20k writes per day) was being exhausted because every single auto-save:
1. Called `ref.collection('data').get()` — 54 reads per save
2. Wrote all 54 localStorage keys unconditionally — 54 writes per save
3. Also called `fbSaveCloudSettings` (1 extra write) on every save
4. `RETURN_ENTITY_DUALWRITE` defaulted `true` — doubled the write cost

With saves triggering every ~450ms during active use, this easily consumed the daily quota within hours.

## Changes

### `RETURN_ENTITY_DUALWRITE` default → `false`
- Was silently doubling every save's write cost (54 → 108 ops)
- The entity sync model is still experimental (`RETURN_SYNC_MODEL === 'legacy'`)
- Opt in via `localStorage.setItem('return_entity_dualwrite','true')`

### `_fbCloudDocCache` — eliminate per-save `collection.get()`
- `fbReadSplitData` (called once at login and by each onSnapshot) now populates `_fbCloudDocCache` as a free side-effect of the read we already paid for
- `fbSaveNow` reads from the cache instead of calling `collection.get()` — saves **54 reads per save**
- Cold-path fallback reads live and seeds the cache if it's not ready yet

### `_fbLastPushedSnapshot` — delta writes
- `fbLoadAll` seeds this snapshot from cloud state after login
- `fbSaveNow` only writes keys whose value differs from the last confirmed write
- Typical user edits 1-3 keys — saves go from **54 writes down to 1-3**
- Early exit if nothing changed and nothing was absorbed from cloud

### `fbSaveCloudSettings` throttle
- Was writing `settings/main` on every save
- Now throttled to once per 2 minutes; force-syncs always write immediately

## Impact

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Auto-save (1 key changed) | 54 reads + 55 writes | 0 reads + 2 writes |
| Auto-save (no change) | 54 reads + 55 writes | 0 reads + 0 writes (early exit) |
| Force sync | 54 reads + 55 writes | 0 reads + ~3 writes |
| Daily quota at 1 save/minute | ~79,200 reads + 79,200 writes | ~0 reads + ~4,320 writes |

Cross-device image sync (theme avatars, stickers, app icon) will start working correctly once saves are no longer quota-blocked.

## Safety

- Cache fallback path ensures correctness even if cache is cold
- Delta filter is skipped on `opts.force` — manual sync always writes all changed keys
- Cache is updated after every successful write so deltas stay accurate
- onSnapshot listener already refreshes `_fbCloudDocCache` via `fbReadSplitData` on every remote change

author: scolladon
body:
## Summary

`status` and `diff` returned unrelated shapes, so a consumer wanting "for this path, the staged change, the unstaged change, and the actual hunks" had to re-derive HEAD's tree, the index, and the working file by hand (23.4 API review finding **M3**). This makes every `status` change **self-describing**, finishing for the staged & working-tree columns what 23.2c (ADR-256) did for `unmerged`.

`StatusResult` is restructured to **one correlated `ChangedPath` record per path** — the structured form of `git status --porcelain=v2`'s ordinary line:

```ts
interface ChangedPath {
  readonly path: FilePath;
  readonly staged?: ChangeKind;     // X — index vs HEAD
  readonly unstaged?: ChangeKind;   // Y — working tree vs index
  readonly head?: BlobSide;         // hH / mH   ({ id, mode })
  readonly index?: BlobSide;        // hI / mI
  readonly worktree?: WorktreeSide; // mW only — no working oid (git prints no hW)
}
interface StatusResult {
  branch; detached;
  changes:   ReadonlyArray<ChangedPath>;
  untracked: ReadonlyArray<FilePath>;   // git's separate `?` lines
  unmerged:  ReadonlyArray<UnmergedEntry>;
  clean;
}
```

The hunks for any path are one read away — staged: `readBlob(head)` ↔ `readBlob(index)`; unstaged: `readBlob(index)` ↔ the working file at `path`. **Endpoints only, no `withHunks`** (ADR-269) — keeps `status`, a hot command, free of folded-in Myers.

The endpoints are data `status` already computed and discarded: the staged side from the existing `diffIndexAgainstTree`, the working side from a new richer `compareWorkingTreeDelta` core (`{ status, worktreeMode }`) with the enum `compareWorkingTreeEntry` as a one-line projection — so its four enum-only consumers (`rm` / `stash` / clean-work-tree / apply-merge) are untouched.

### Breaking changes (23.4 window — no release-bundling, ADR-260)

- `indexChanges` / `workingTreeChanges` → collapsed into **`changes`** (one record per path).
- **`untracked`** is now its own `ReadonlyArray<FilePath>` field (was folded into the working column). Keeps the `git rm --cached` case (`D ` + `??`) as two clean sources.
- `ChangeKind` drops `'untracked'`.
- `ChangeEntry` removed; `ConflictStage` renamed/unified to the shared **`BlobSide`** (reused for `head`/`index`/`base`/`ours`/`theirs`).
- `describe --dirty/--broken` simplifies to `changes.length > 0 || unmerged.length > 0` (behaviour-preserving).

No git-observable behaviour changes — SHAs, refs, reflogs, on-disk state, refusals identical.

## Commits

- `refactor(primitives)`: richer `compareWorkingTreeDelta` core + enum projection
- `feat(status)!`: correlated `ChangedPath` record per path with diff endpoints
- `test(status)`: reconstruct `git status --porcelain=v2` from the change endpoints
- `docs(status)`: per-path model, 23.4h done, log follow-up 23.4m
- `chore(deps)`: bump knip 6.15→6.16 (keep `check:deps` green)

## Test plan

- [x] `status-interop` reconstructs **both** `git status --porcelain` (v1) and `--porcelain=v2` (the ordinary `mH mI mW hH hI` endpoints) **byte-for-byte** vs real git, across add/modify/delete/MM/cached-delete/type-change/exec-mode/unborn/clean.
- [x] Unit: per-path records for every staged/unstaged combination, endpoint assertions (not just kinds), `rm --cached` two-source case, unborn HEAD, conflicted index (only under `unmerged`), corrupt-index propagation.
- [x] `compareWorkingTreeDelta` worktree-mode cases + enum projection.
- [x] **100% mutation** on `status.ts` + `compare-working-tree-entry.ts` (0 survivors).
- [x] `npm run validate` green (lint, types, unit, integration, coverage, parity, spelling, dead-code, test-pyramid, api.json).
- [x] Architecture pass: no-op (justified — unifying `BlobSide` with the domain `FlatTreeEntry` would cross the hexagonal boundary).

Follow-up logged: **23.4m** — add the conflicted path's worktree mode (`mW`) to `UnmergedEntry` to close full porcelain-v2 `u`-line reconstruction.

ADR-269 · `docs/design/status-diff-correlation.md`

author: umran666
body:
Hi there,

This PR resolves issue #311 where the progress output can display "Running trial N of M" where N > M.

### The Problem
When the user chooses "Run additional trials" from the trial selection menu:
1. `settings.n_trials` is incremented.
2. `study.optimize()` is called again to run the new trials.
3. However, the trial progress variables (`trial_index`, `start_index`, and `start_time`) are not re-initialized before the new optimize run.
4. Since `trial_index` retains its old value from the end of the previous run, the count of attempted trials exceeds the new total trial budget if any previous trials were pruned or failed.

### The Solution
Re-initialized `start_index`, `trial_index`, and `start_time` right before calling `study.optimize()` in the "Run additional trials" block. This keeps the progress and estimated remaining time calculations correct for the new set of trials.

Thanks for taking a look!

author: jklondon
body:
## Problem

EIP-7778 (*Block Gas Accounting without Refunds*) ships in **Osaka**, but the Prague branch of `TxnExecutor.Execute` used the post-refund, EIP-7623-floored `txnGasUsed` for `blockRegularGasUsed` on Osaka as well:

```go
} else if rules.IsPrague {
    ...
    st.txnGasUsed = max(intrinsicGasResult.FloorGasCost, st.txnGasUsedB4Refunds-refund)
    st.blockRegularGasUsed = st.txnGasUsed   // wrong for Osaka
}
```

That inflates the block gas counter and causes `gas used by execution: X, in header: Y` failures on Osaka mainnet (observed at block **25202264**: execution 33961963 vs header 33888325, diff **+73638** — the accumulated EIP-7623 calldata-floor premium).

## Fix

For Osaka (non-Amsterdam) use `txnGasUsedB4Refunds` for block accounting: SSTORE refunds do not free up block capacity, and the EIP-7623 calldata floor is a minimum ETH payment only — it must not inflate block gas. The receipt (`txnGasUsed`) is unchanged.

Companion PR backports the equivalent change to `release/3.4` (where this logic lives in `state_transition.go`).

body:
## Summary

Consolidates all 4 commits from stale PR #648 (unmergeable due to CHANGELOG conflict) plus tier-3 sprite size fix. Addresses the most impactful active playtest-feedback issues.

### 1. Script-identity guard for projectiles (fixes kills=0)

**Root cause:** `has_method("setup")` is unreliable in headless Godot 4 at 8× time_scale under GDScript VM pressure — it can return `false` for structurally valid nodes during scene transitions, causing every tower shot to hit the error path and the playtester to report 0 kills.

**Fix:** Replace `has_method()` guards with `get_script() == _expected_script` identity checks:
- `ProjectilePool.acquire()` — guard against detached-script nodes
- `ProjectilePool.release()` — guard against scene-transition races
- `BaseTower._attack()` — new `_is_valid_projectile()` helper + CACHE_MODE_IGNORE reload as last-resort fallback when even a fresh instantiation fails

Closes playtest-feedback #653, #602, #647.

### 2. Tint visibility fix (closes #660)

**Root cause:** T1 brightness was 1.0 (no darkening), making the hue shift imperceptible on bright friend-photo sprites. Only T3 (brightness=0.72) was clearly visible.

**Fix:** Brightness LUT updated — T1: 0.88, T2: 0.80, T3: 0.70. The 12–30% brightness reduction per tier makes path-color shifts readable at a glance.

Also fixes `_maybe_swap_tier3_sprite()` target size 90px→130px (tier-3 art appeared 30% smaller than base tier).

### 3. Playtester accuracy fix (closes #640)

Healthy-level wave cap reduced 8×2.5s=20s → 6×2.0s=12s real time, so 3 consecutive level scenarios fit within the 120s Godot process budget without L3 being truncated.

### 4. Swiss German polish

`S/Sek` → `Schad/Sek` (Schade pro Sekunde = unambiguous DPS label) in shop cards and tower-info stats panel.

## Verification

- `validate.sh` passes cleanly
- All ext_resource and preload paths resolve
- Logic traced manually: script identity checks correctly guard pool acquire/release, `_is_valid_projectile` falls back to `has_method` when `_projectile_script` is null (early init)

Closes stale PR #648.

author: mariesqu
body:
## What

PR6a of the HTTP-transport phase: per-writer HMAC authentication foundation.

**Purely additive — no enforcement.** The server still accepts unauthenticated requests. Enforcement (middleware, client signing) is PR6b.

### internal/wireauth (new package)

Stdlib-only HMAC-SHA256 request-signing primitives (no HTTP, no storage):

- `Canonical(method, path, body)` — signing string: `method + "\n" + path + "\n" + body`
- `Sign(key, method, path, body)` — `hex(HMAC-SHA256(key, Canonical(...)))`
- `Verify(key, method, path, body, sig)` — decode hex → compare raw MACs via `hmac.Equal` (constant-time; never `==` on hex strings)
- `NewKey()` — 32 random bytes from `crypto/rand`
- `HeaderWriterID = "X-Writer-Id"`, `HeaderSignature = "X-Signature"` constants

### centralstore: cloud_writer_keys table

Added to `ApplySchema` (idempotent, `IF NOT EXISTS`, same pattern as `cloud_sync_audit`):

```sql
cloud_writer_keys(
  writer_id  TEXT        PRIMARY KEY,
  secret     BYTEA       NOT NULL,   -- raw key; DB is the trust boundary
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  active     BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT true
)
```

### centralstore: key store methods (`writer_keys.go`)

- `UpsertWriterKey(ctx, writerID, secret)` — provision and rotate (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE)
- `WriterKey(ctx, writerID)` — returns secret or `ErrWriterKeyNotFound` when absent or inactive
- `DeactivateWriterKey(ctx, writerID)` — revoke by setting `active = false`

## Why

PR6a establishes the auth building blocks chosen for the transport phase: per-writer HMAC-SHA256 request signing. All cryptographic primitives are stdlib only (`crypto/hmac`, `crypto/sha256`, `crypto/rand`). The decision to store keys as raw BYTEA (rather than a hash) is intentional — HMAC verification requires the recoverable key; the DB is the trust boundary. Envelope encryption is deferred to a future PR.

## Verify results

- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` ✓
- `go vet ./...` ✓  
- `go vet -tags acceptance ./...` ✓
- `go test ./...` — all packages green (including new `wireauth` unit tests)
- `go test -tags acceptance -count=2 ./...` — all packages green both runs; existing convergence/acceptance suites unchanged

## Additive-only checklist

- No existing endpoint changed
- No existing client (`internal/remote`) changed
- No existing test modified (except the pre-existing `fastCfg` regression fix from the Copilot Autofix commit that merged with PR #27)
- Server still accepts unauthenticated requests — enforcement is PR6b

body:
cudaq.dem_from_kernel runs the kernel under a dlopen'd `stim` analysis plugin. A non-Clifford gate makes Stim throw `std::runtime_error` from inside that plugin; on macOS the exception escapes uncaught at the binding boundary and the process aborts (SIGABRT / "Fatal Python error: Aborted"), crashing the test worker instead of raising in Python.

author: nickderobertis
body:
## Why

The repo-write recommended profile denies `just dev > /tmp/dev-server.log 2>&1` with:

> `redirection '> /tmp/dev-server.log' not permitted by any matching allow rule (checked 1)`

This is by design, not a bug: the allowlister grants redirection targets **per-rule**, and the rule that allows `make`/`just` carries no `redirections` policy (a rule with no `write_glob` denies all `>`/`>>` writes). The profile *does* permit `/tmp` redirects, but only on the text-filter rule (`echo|cat|grep|…`), which doesn't match `just`. There was no way to say "any already-allowed command may write to `/tmp`" without either repeating a redirect policy on every rule or adding a blanket `match:"*"` allow that would authorize *every* command and neuter the allowlist.

## What

A new **redirection-only rule type**: `grants: "redirections"`. Such a rule contributes redirection targets but **never authorizes a command on its own**.

- `src/domain/rule.rs` — `Grant { Command, Redirections }` enum (default `Command`), a `grant` field on `Rule`, a `with_grant` builder, and `is_redirection_only()`.
- `src/config.rs` — parse + validate `grants` (unknown value errors; `redirections` requires `action:"allow"` and a present `redirections` block).
- `src/domain/decision.rs` — `decide_fragment` splits matched allow rules into **authorizers** vs **redirection-grants**. With no authorizer it defers; redirection-only rules are only consulted to widen targets for a command an authorizer already permitted. Deny-is-supreme and "a redirection never grants execution" invariants are preserved.
- `examples/recommended/repo-write.json` — one leading scratch rule (`argv:["**"]`, `grants:"redirections"`, `write_glob` for `/tmp` + macOS `/private/tmp`, top-level and nested). `read-only.json` and all existing rules untouched.

Existing configs are unaffected: `grants` is optional and defaults to `Command`.

## Tests

- `decision.rs` units: redir-only alone → defer; authorizer + redir-only → `/tmp` allowed; non-`/tmp` target → deny; deny still wins; baseline (no grant) → deny.
- `config.rs` units: parse OK; unknown grant; `deny` + redir-only; missing `redirections` block.
- `tests/recommended.rs`: profile-level cases incl. the motivating `just dev > /tmp/dev-server.log 2>&1 → Allow`, `/private/tmp` allow, non-`/tmp`/`..`-escape deny, `rm -rf / > /tmp/x → Deny`, unauthorized command → defer.

## Verification

`rustfmt --check` is clean and `repo-write.json` validates. The full gate (`just full-check`: clippy `-D warnings`, nextest, coverage floor) was **not** run locally — the dev box I authored on has no C toolchain to link cargo build scripts. Relying on CI to run the gate across platforms; happy to address any findings.

author: ychtao
body:
The main theorem of translation soundness is `translation_is_sound` in `./Cedar/Thm/Translation.lean`. 

The supporting files are as follows:
+ `./Cedar/Thm/Translation/Aux.lean` contains auxiliary lemmas for proofs elsewhere.
+ `./Cedar/Thm/Translation/ExprTranslation.lean` are proofs about expression translation. The main theorem in this file is `expr_to_expr_agrees`, which states that given a CST expression `e`, if it translates to the AST expression`aexp`, then they evaluate to the same result given the same request and entities.
+ `./Cedar/Thm/Translation/PolicyToExpr.lean` are proofs about policy evalution. The main theorem in this file is `policy_to_expr_agrees`, which states that given a CST policy, the following two paths yield expressions that evaluate to the same result:
    1. CST policy -> AST policy -> AST expression
    2. CST policy -> CST expression -> AST expression
+ `./Cedar/Thm/Translation.lean` puts together the partial results and proves the final theorem.

### Motivation

- Provide a small, configurable .NET 8 console tool to import CSV data into PostgreSQL with configurable connection, table, columns and logging. 
- Support robust CSV parsing (including quoted fields with newlines) and safe identifier quoting to avoid SQL-injection-like table/column issues. 
- Use PostgreSQL `COPY … FROM STDIN` text mode for efficient bulk import and provide unit test coverage for core components.

- Implement import orchestration in `CsvImportService` which validates options, reads header or configured columns, converts empty strings to `null`, logs progress, and writes rows via an `IPostgresImporter` abstraction.  
- Add `NpgsqlPostgresImporterFactory` (uses `COPY … FROM STDIN` text import), `PostgresCopyTextEncoder` for COPY text escaping, and `PostgresIdentifier` for identifier validation/quoting.

author: pgherveou
body:
## Feature: Fix failing "Codegen" GitHub Actions job

### Summary

The "Codegen" CI job was failing because `npm ci` (without `--ignore-scripts`) caused npm to run `prepare` lifecycle scripts for all workspace packages during installation — before codegen had generated the required TypeScript files and before `@parity/truapi`'s `dist/` directory was built. This resulted in TypeScript compilation errors (`Cannot find module '@parity/truapi'`) when building `@parity/truapi-host`.

### Checklist

- [ ] Added `docs/features/short-descriptive-name.md` with completed frontmatter
- [ ] Updated `docs/features/_index.md` with a link to the new proposal
- [ ] Added labels: `feature-request`, `proposal`

### Use Cases

CI pipelines for the `paritytech/truapi` repository need to reliably build and verify the generated TypeScript client and host packages without spurious failures caused by incorrect build ordering during `npm ci`.

### Proposed Solution

- Made `prepare` scripts in both `@parity/truapi` and `@parity/truapi-host` conditional on `TRUAPI_SKIP_PACKAGE_BUILD`: `if [ "${TRUAPI_SKIP_PACKAGE_BUILD:-0}" != "1" ]; then npm run build; fi`
- Changed all CI jobs to use `TRUAPI_SKIP_PACKAGE_BUILD=1 npm ci --ignore-scripts` to skip lifecycle scripts during installation
- For jobs that need `@parity/truapi` built (ts-client, playground, explorer, dotli), added an explicit `npm run build --prefix js/packages/truapi` step after install to ensure the package is built in the correct order before dependent packages

author: gmadsen
body:
## What

Cycle 4 — a **second home for the `sketch-curve-2d` draw engine** (demonstrating reuse across topics with a new transform), in `convex-optimization §convex-sets-functions`.

Drag to sketch `f(x)`; the widget computes its **convex envelope** (greatest convex minorant, via a lower convex hull) and flags in **pink** every stretch where `f` rises above the envelope — exactly where a chord dips below the graph and convexity fails. The readout gives the verdict + the max gap, and states Jensen's inequality on the convex side.

## Complementary, not duplicative

The section's existing widget is "Epigraph & supporting line" — a **first-order** view (tangent stays below) on a **fixed** convex function. This is the **zeroth-order chord / Jensen** definition the prose actually leads with ("every chord between two points stays inside"), on a function **you draw yourself**. Different order of the convexity characterization, different interaction.

## Verification

- Node-checked the detector: parabola & affine → convex (gap 0); concave `−x²/2` → gap 4.5; Gaussian bump → gap 1.5 → not convex.
- Browser-verified via synthesized drags: default parabola → **"convex ✓"** (shows `f(tx+(1−t)y) ≤ t f(x)+(1−t) f(y)`); drawn concave bump → **"not convex, max gap 2.26"** with the whole hump pink above its chord-envelope. Console clean.

author: elkayee
body:
### 💡 What
Replaced memory-intensive `len(text.splitlines())` calls with the significantly faster, O(1)-memory `text.count('\n') + (1 if text and not text.endswith('\n') else 0)` calculation for counting lines in large text documents (like assembled markdown).

### 🎯 Why
`str.splitlines()` eagerly allocates an entire list of all split lines in memory, causing unnecessary O(N) memory allocation overhead for large chapter strings just to get the total count. `count('\n')` works entirely in C and has virtually zero memory overhead.

### 📊 Impact
Measured ~10x speedup for line counting large strings with no additional memory allocation. 

### 🔬 Measurement
See the learning entry in `.jules/bolt.md` and performance benchmark logs. Tests verify correct edge case handling matching `splitlines()`.

author: tabularasa31
body:
## What

**Phase 1 of the edge-hardening track** (follow-up to #146). Shrinks the public `:443` surface to exactly "serve tenants + liveness" and moves observability to a stdout→Loki push stream. No private management listener — with the endpoints gone there is nothing to relocate.

## Why

Traffic to the raw edge IP / a non-tenant Host is, by construction, never a legitimate client visit (a real visitor always arrives with a known tenant Host). Operational/debug endpoints sitting on that same public surface are: info leaks that help an attacker calibrate (`/metrics`), an evasion oracle (`/__fp` — test a forged TLS stack against our fingerprinter), an unauthenticated cascade-bypass to a tenant origin (`/baseline/`), and flood-contention risk. This removes all of them so the public surface is tenant-only — which also makes the Phase 3 unconditional no-SNI/non-tenant deny safe.

## Removed from the public edge

| Endpoint | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `/__admin` + `/__admin/recover_ip` | Deleted (`admin.lua`, `recovery.lua`, `recovery_test.lua`, env `DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN`/`ADMIN_ACL_CIDR`). False-positive recovery is the dashboard's job via the Policy API; the edge does not mutate policy. |
| `/metrics` | Deleted (`metrics.lua`). Counters now pushed as `EDGE_STATS`. |
| `/__version` | Deploy metadata (`commit` / `cascade_version` / `challenge_secret_fp`) folded into `EDGE_STATS`. |
| `/__policy` | Debug-only — removed. |
| `/baseline/` | Unauthenticated cascade-bypass passthrough to a tenant origin — deleted. |
| `/__fp` | TLS-fingerprint oracle — unrouted; returns on a controlled measurement surface when the browser farm is built (Phase 4, see `docs/research/positive-fp-catalog-design.md`). |

**Kept public:** `/__health` (static "ok" — leaks nothing, mutates nothing; the only public ops endpoint, for an external uptime/LB check).

## Observability: stdout → Loki (push, not expose)

New [`edge_stats.lua`](infra/demo-stand/lua/edge_stats.lua): a worker-0 timer writes one `EDGE_STATS {json}` line every 30s to stdout. It carries the signals that have no other window once `/metrics` is gone:

- the edge-deny lever counters (`edge_nontenant_dropped_total`, `edge_sni_rejected_total`) — these bypass `BAC_LOG` by design (the 444 fires before the cascade; the TLS reject is in the handshake);
- cache hit ratio, `fp_unique`, blocklist size;
- BAC_LOG shipper health + per-catalog Channel-C staleness (the dead-channel alert — promtail drops nginx error.log lines, so this would otherwise be invisible in Loki);
- the old `/__version` deploy metadata.

`promtail-config.yaml` is extended to capture **both** `BAC_LOG` and `EDGE_STATS` prefixes under a `kind` label: `{kind="edge_stats"}` for counters, `{kind="bac_log"}` for requests. Aggregate (one line / 30s), so it adds no per-request log I/O — safe under a flood — and there is no pull endpoint to scan or flood.

## Tests / validation

- `tests/edge_stats_test.lua` — `snapshot` + `iso8601` (18 cases). Makefile + CI updated (drop `recovery_test`, add `edge_stats_test`).
- Full host unit suite green; `luac` clean.
- `openresty -t` green on the built project image (config + `init_by_lua`); runtime smoke confirmed `EDGE_STATS` emission, `/__health` 200, and removed endpoints now resolving through `location /`.
- **Note:** a final in-container re-run after the catalog-staleness addition to `edge_stats.lua` is pending a local Docker outage (the addition is `pcall`-guarded and host-tested; `nginx.demo.conf` is unchanged since the last green `openresty -t`). CI runs `luacheck` + the unit suite in the openresty container.

## Not in this PR (next phases)

Phase 2 (provision `turboshield.ru` / `свиннар.рф` as active-mode tenants + drop `bac.turboshield.ru`), Phase 3 (tenant-only edge + no-SNI rejection by default), Phase 4 (browser-farm `/__fp` access — mTLS vs WireGuard bastion).

author: digi-scrypt
body:
1. `parse_decimal` builds the result straight from `decimal.Decimal(...)`, which happily accepts `nan`, `inf`, `Infinity` and `sNaN`, so those parse instead of being rejected.
2. a `NaN` result then slips past range checks (every comparison against NaN is False), and a signaling NaN throws `InvalidOperation` the first time anything does arithmetic with it.

Added an `is_finite()` check so non-finite input raises `NumberFormatError` like any other non-decimal string. What happens today if someone feeds `"inf"` from a form field straight into a `> limit` guard? It passes. Kept it in the parser since that's the layer that already promises to reject things that aren't localized decimals.

author: wcpeixoto
body:
## What this is

Adds **one file** — the minimal function-local Deno resolver config for the `sync-wodify-retention` Edge Function:

```
supabase/functions/sync-wodify-retention/deno.json
```
```json
{"unstable":["sloppy-imports"]}
```

This lets Deno resolve the extensionless **transitive** `./silentChurn` import inside the shared aggregate module (`src/lib/gym/wodifyRetentionAggregate.ts:24`) **without** forking the locked classifier/date logic and **without** a `tsconfig` change.

## ⚠️ This PR does NOT close the live gate

It **only** adds the minimal function-local Deno resolver config. The remaining live-gate proof is still **Supabase deploy / eszip resolution**, specifically:

1. whether `supabase functions deploy` **discovers** the function-local `deno.json`,
2. whether deploy **honors** `unstable:["sloppy-imports"]`, and
3. whether **eszip resolves the graph the same way** the offline Deno proof did.

Those three remain **UNPROVEN** here — they can only be confirmed by a real deploy/eszip bundle (a separate, still-gated step). Supabase docs confirm a per-function `deno.json` is read and "configures Deno-specific settings" ([Managing dependencies](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/dependencies)), but do **not** document `sloppy-imports` being honored at deploy, and deploy-time import resolution is a known divergence point.

## Offline proof reproduced (clean copy — bytes only, no `package.json`/`node_modules`, no network)

The in-repo `deno check` **falsely passes** (root `package.json`/`node_modules` flips Deno into node-resolution), so the proof is run on a clean copy of the exact bytes:

- **strict `deno check` WITHOUT this `deno.json`** → **FAILS**: `TS2307 [ERROR]: Cannot find module '.../silentChurn'` at `wodifyRetentionAggregate.ts:24`.
- **`deno check` WITH this `deno.json`** → **PASSES** (resolves the whole local graph offline).

`sloppy-imports` is a global resolver toggle, so the function-local `deno.json` covers the transitive import even though it lives under `src/`.

## CI run locally

- `npm test` → **661 passed (42 files)**.
- `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) → **green** (pre-existing >500 kB chunk-size warning only).

## Safety attestations

- **No secrets were set.**
- **No Wodify call was made.**
- **No deploy / serve / invoke occurred. No POST.**
- **No locked classifier logic was changed or duplicated** — `silentChurn.ts` untouched, no `.ts` added to the shared `./silentChurn` import, no fork/mirror/vendor/duplicate, no `tsconfig` change.
- No PR2 / SPA wiring.

## Boss Monster — guided tutorial mode

A contextual, **learn-by-doing** tutorial, as requested.

### How it works
- A **📖 Tutorial** button on the menu (it **pulses** for first-timers who haven't done it yet).
- Starting it launches a guided run: it auto-picks a boss + default abilities (skips the menus), preloads a **3-card hand + 2 slots**, and shows a **coach banner** that walks you through, one real action at a time:
  1. **Tap a room card** to select it (hand pulses)
  2. **Tap the glowing empty slot** to build it (slot ring pulses on the canvas)
  3. **Start the wave** (button pulses)
  4. **Blast the hero with a boss ability** (ability pulses) — advances when you slay them
  5. **Level a room** by selecting a matching card and tapping the room — taught with the duplicate cards you're given
  6. Wrap-up tip (inspect anything) + **Got it ✓**
- Each step advances from your **actual gameplay** (select / place / wave / kill / upgrade), with the relevant control highlighted. **Skip** anytime; completion is saved to localStorage so the menu button stops pulsing.

### Also fixes
A latent **`renderPanel` ↔ `updateRunPanel` recursion** (the run panel called update, whose mismatch-fallback re-called render). The run panel's boss HP/mana bars are now rendered inline; the frame loop keeps them fresh.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the Qwen 3.6 35B Slime tutorial path so bridge-mode training can complete on `joy-dev`:

- Keeps bridge-mode actor/ref loading on HF checkpoints instead of feeding torch-dist checkpoint paths back into Megatron Bridge.
- Reduces Qwen35B rollout/eval response length and skips optimizer state in tutorial checkpoints to avoid OOM/disk pressure on 16×H100 runs.
- Hardens Ray health checks/checkpoint conversion polling around large checkpoint saves.
- Patches Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 bridge checkpoint HF conversion names, including linear-attention split `query`/`key`/`value` tensors and unused vision params.
- Skips the unnecessary final rollout weight sync after the last train/save step when no eval/next rollout needs updated rollout weights.

Validation so far:

- `uv run --with ruff ruff check modal_training_gym/frameworks/slime/modal_helpers/patches/patch_skip_final_weight_update.py`
- `uv run --with ruff ruff format --check modal_training_gym/frameworks/slime/modal_helpers/patches/patch_skip_final_weight_update.py`
- `uv run python -m compileall modal_training_gym/frameworks/slime/modal_helpers/patches/patch_skip_final_weight_update.py`

author: ganeshkumarashok
body:
## What

`nvidia-modprobe.service` runs `ExecStartPre=dkms autoinstall --verbose` on **every** GPU node boot, ordered `Before=kubelet.service`. On AKS GPU VHDs the NVIDIA driver is pre-built via DKMS and baked into the image (`modules.dep` is generated at image-bake time), so this re-scan/rebuild is **redundant work (~5s measured)** that sits on the provisioning critical path and gates kubelet on every boot.

This guards the autoinstall so it only runs when the kernel modules `ExecStart` (`nvidia-modprobe -u -c0`) actually needs are missing for the **running** kernel:

```ini
ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c "if modinfo nvidia >/dev/null 2>&1 && modinfo nvidia-uvm >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'nvidia kernel modules already built for running kernel; skipping dkms autoinstall'; else dkms autoinstall --verbose; fi"
```

## Why it's correct across kernel upgrades

`modinfo` resolves modules from `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)`. If the running kernel changed (e.g. an unattended kernel upgrade so the baked module no longer matches), that tree has no nvidia modules → `modinfo` fails → `dkms autoinstall` still runs and rebuilds. So behavior is **identical to today on exactly the path where the rebuild is genuinely needed**; we only skip the redundant rebuild in the common baked-and-unchanged-kernel case.

## Design notes
- **Checks both `nvidia` and `nvidia-uvm`.** The `-u` flag in `ExecStart` sets up the UVM device node, so the UVM module is required. Checking only `nvidia` could false-positive on a partial module set and then fail `ExecStart`, blocking kubelet.
- **No shell variables in the predicate**, so systemd does not perform unintended `$`-expansion on the Exec line. Parses cleanly under `/bin/sh` (dash).
- **CSE-install path** (driver installed at provision time via the privileged driver container) is unaffected: if `depmod` hasn't indexed the module yet, `modinfo` fails and we fall back to `dkms autoinstall` — same as today.
- DKMS registration for future kernel upgrades is unchanged (registration comes from driver/package install, not from `autoinstall`).

## Lifecycle / compatibility
- File is **VHD-resident** (copied by `vhdbuilder/packer/packer_source.sh`), not embedded in CSE custom data — no old-VHD/new-CSE skew concern. The unit is started only on Ubuntu by `ensureGPUDrivers`.
- `make generate` produces no testdata diff (the unit is not embedded in CSE snapshots).
- Works on Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 (`modinfo`/`dkms` standard).

## Testing
- `GENERATE_TEST_DATA=true go test ./pkg/agent...` — pass, no snapshot drift.
- Predicate validated under `/bin/sh -n` (POSIX parse OK).
- Existing GPU e2e coverage exercises resulting node state: `e2e/validators.go` runs `sudo nvidia-modprobe`; `e2e/scenario_test.go` asserts the unit does not restart kubelet / cause unschedulability.

## Risk
🟢 Low / ⚡ node provisioning latency improvement. Fallback path is byte-for-byte the original behavior; the only new behavior is skipping a provably-redundant rebuild.

author: xiaoxiaotest9527-bit
body:
## 背景

应用在启动新的 Codex provider session 时崩溃，日志显示 panic：

`repeated read on failed websocket connection`

堆栈落在 `internal/provider/codexapp` 的 WebSocket initialize 路径：连接读失败后继续对同一条失败 WebSocket 调用 `ReadMessage()`，触发 gorilla/websocket 的保护性 panic。

## 改动

- initialize 阶段读失败后直接返回错误，不再重复读取失败连接。
- initialize 读 deadline 改为服从外层启动 context；没有 context deadline 时使用已有启动超时。
- 新增回归测试，覆盖 initialize 无响应时返回错误而不是 panic。

## 验证

- 临时 worktree A/B 复现：
  - 未修改生产代码：`go test ./internal/provider/codexapp -run TestTransportInitializeTimeoutUncaughtPanicRepro -count=1` 复现 `panic: repeated read on failed websocket connection`。
  - 应用补丁后：同一复现测试 exit 0。
- `./scripts/test_with_guard.sh internal/provider/codexapp/transport_helpers.go`
- `./scripts/test_with_guard.sh internal/provider/codexapp/recovery_transport_test.go`
- `./scripts/test_with_guard.sh ./internal/provider/codexapp -count=1`
- push 前 hook 自动复跑 affected package：`./internal/provider/codexapp` 通过。

## 说明

这不是 OOM 兜底，也不会吞掉资源级故障；它只把 provider initialize 的普通读失败从进程级 panic 修正为可返回的启动错误。

author: mr-raj12
body:
## Description

`PackWriter` buffers `(chunk_id, cdata)` pairs and flushes them as a pack file via borgstore once `max_count` chunks accumulate. At N=1 (`max_count=1`), `pack_id == chunk_id` and pack files land at `packs/{chunk_id_hex}`. No changes needed to `get()` or `delete()`. `UNKNOWN_INT32 = 0xFFFFFFFF` is the sentinel for pack location fields that are not yet written. 0xFFFFFFFF is above MAX_DATA_SIZE (~20 MB), so it can never collide with a real `obj_offset`. `chunks.add()` writes the placeholder; `update_pack_info()` fills in real values after `flush()`.

`flush()` clears `_pieces` in a `try/finally`. Without this, a store failure would leave the chunk in the buffer and it would get re-bundled with the next chunk, pushing the N>1 code path and writing under a hash-derived key instead of the chunk's own id.

Changes:
- `repository.py`: add `PackWriter`; `put()` delegates to
  `_pack_writer.add()` and returns pack results.
- `constants.py`: add `UNKNOWN_INT32 = 0xFFFFFFFF`.
- `hashindex.pyx`: `add()` uses `UNKNOWN_INT32` placeholders; new
  `update_pack_info()`.
- `hashindex.pyi`: type stub for `update_pack_info()`.
- `cache.py`: `add_chunk()` calls `update_pack_info()` from pack results.
- `archive.py`: `add_reference()` in `rebuild_archives()` does the same.

refs #8572

author: jimjafar
body:
## What

Spec **2C** from `docs/research/self-improving-curator-brainstorm.md` (decisions **D4–D9**) — the capstone. The admin teaches *this install's* curator by editing its per-job prompt **addendum** through a dashboard **chat** with the curator LLM, safely:

- **Addendum → two committed vault files** (`.curator/intake-addendum.md` / `grooming-addendum.md`) → git diff / revert / backup for free (D7), one per job (D6). And **intake finally reads its addendum** (closes the long-standing I5 gap).
- **Under-evaluation lifecycle** (D8): an edited addendum is live but **probationary** — everything it produces is forced to `proposed` until the admin **accepts** or **rolls back** (git). Grooming additionally gets an **on-demand dry-run over the corpus** before committing (D9). **No automated eval** (D4) — the vault has no stable ground truth, so the admin judges *real results*, guarded by code-re-check + the 2 KB cap + git revert.
- **A dashboard chat** (per-memory "discuss this memory" + general entry) that can **fix the memory now** (including **reverse a bad merge** — net-new) and **co-author an addendum edit**; fix-now applies directly, addendum-edit rides the lifecycle (D5).

## Encouraging audit findings

- The vault already has a non-memory write-and-commit primitive → addendum-as-git-file is cheap.
- The LLM client already takes a `messages` array → the chat reuses it; **request/response, no streaming infra** needed for v1.
- Both apply paths have clean `forcePropose` seams for under-evaluation.

The genuinely net-new/hard parts (flagged in the spec): the chat endpoint, **reverse-a-groom/unmerge** (no primitive today), and the under-evaluation wiring.

## Build-ready

Every D4–D9 decision settled (D-1…D-11), laid out as **eight ordered increments** (one PR each, `main` green throughout), each with acceptance criteria:

| | |
|---|---|
| PR-1 | Addendum → committed vault files (+migration) |
| PR-2 | Intake reads its addendum (close I5 gap) |
| PR-3 | Under-evaluation force-propose + status + tagging |
| PR-4 | Grooming dry-run over the corpus |
| PR-5 | Admin merge/split/update/**unmerge** mutations |
| PR-6 | Curator chat endpoint + 3rd consumer config |
| PR-7 | Dashboard chat UI + entry points + lifecycle controls |
| PR-8 | Docs + CHANGELOG + status surfacing |

## Scope / sequencing

- **Docs only** — Specify-phase draft.
- **Server + dashboard only — no plugin changes.**
- **Depends on 2A** (the `curator.chat.*` consumer config) **and 2B** (intake decision log for grounding, triggerable grooming for the dry-run, one dashboard). Recommended order 2A → 2B → 2C.

body:
## task-011 — non-ADLS access-policy enforcement (warehouse + KQL)

Makes Governance → Policies **Access** grants real beyond ADLS. Previously warehouse/KQL scopes returned a `pending` no-op; now they're enforced as real Azure-native data-plane grants (no Fabric/Purview-policy dependency).

### Enforcement (`access-policy-client.ts`)
- **warehouse** → Synapse **Dedicated SQL**: `CREATE USER [upn] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER` (if absent) + `ALTER ROLE db_datareader|db_datawriter|db_owner ADD MEMBER`. Honest `pending` gate if `LOOM_SYNAPSE_WORKSPACE`/`_DEDICATED_POOL` unset.
- **kql-database** → ADX `.add database ["db"] viewers|users|admins ('<aad token>')`. Token = `aaduser=<UPN>` (no tenant needed) or `aaduser|aadgroup|aadapp=<oid>;AZURE_TENANT_ID`; honest gate when tenant id is required but unset. Honest `pending` gate if `LOOM_KUSTO_CLUSTER_URI` unset.
- SQL identifiers bracket-escaped + literals quote-escaped (no injection); role names from fixed maps only.
- **Symmetric revoke** — new `revokeStructuredGrant` (`ALTER ROLE … DROP MEMBER` / `.drop database … role`), wired into the policy DELETE for warehouse/kql (ADLS still revokes by role-assignment id). Best-effort, never blocks the delete.

### Route + UI
- `policies` route: `scopeType` enum + validation extended to `warehouse` / `kql-database`; passes `principalName` (UPN) to enforcement; DELETE revokes structured grants.
- `/governance/policies` Access form: new **"Scope (data plane)"** dropdown (ADLS container / Warehouse (Synapse SQL) / KQL database (ADX)) with conditional, **all-dropdown** targets (container input · KQL-database dropdown from `by-type` · warehouse caption). Passes the principal's UPN. `loom-no-freeform-config` compliant.

### Rule compliance
- **no-vaporware:** real SQL/ADX commands; failures surface verbatim as enforcement `error`; only honest `pending` gates remain for unconfigured backends + workspace/item/collection scopes.
- **no-fabric-dependency:** Synapse dedicated SQL + ADX — both Azure-native.

`tsc --noEmit` clean on touched files (only pre-existing px noise in the untouched `useStyles`). LIVE-VERIFY is the operator step: needs the Synapse pool + ADX cluster reachable and the Console UAMI as SQL `db_owner` / ADX `AllDatabasesAdmin` to execute the grants. parity doc `governance.md` updated.

## Summary

Two participant-protection changes to the Treasure Hunt study, both motivated by accidental data loss observed during pilot runs.

- **`beforeunload` warning while step === 'game'** (`frontend/src/pages/study/GameFrame.jsx`) — registers/cleans up a beforeunload handler so a participant who accidentally closes the tab mid-game gets the browser's "Leave site?" prompt instead of silently losing their in-progress session. Gated on `step === 'game'` so the warning doesn't appear on consent, demographics, debrief, or done.
- **Two-stage confirm on the extinction QUIT button** (`frontend/public/study-games/experiment1/index.html`) — confused participants were quitting at trial 1, contaminating the primary DV (`extinction_chests_opened`). The red "I'M DONE HUNTING" button now relabels to "Are you sure? Click again to end." on first click, reverts after 4 s, and only actually ends the timeline on a second click within that window. Capture-phase listener with `stopImmediatePropagation()` swallows the first click before jsPsych's own handler can fire.
- **Stimulus copy update** on the extinction transition screen makes the irreversibility explicit ("Once you stop, the hunt is over and you can't return.").
- **4 new vitest cases** in `src/tests/pages/study/GameFrame.test.jsx` covering the new effect: registers only when `step === 'game'`, removes on unmount, and the handler sets `returnValue` + calls `preventDefault`.

author: richardafolayan
body:
## Context
Companion to **#497**, which fixed the Lanre double-send bug (the same physical iMessage persisted as two rows — a synthetic-key send row + a guid-key scan row — whose text differed only by chat.db whitespace normalisation, `…heard.\n So` vs `…heard.\nSo`). #497 stops **new** duplicates and self-heals a thread on its **next scan**.

This PR adds the **immediate, cross-thread** cleanup tool for rows already persisted, so they don't have to wait for a re-scan.

## `apps/runner/src/scripts/dedupe-outbound-whitespace.ts`
- **Dry-run by default**; `--apply` writes a timestamped `.bak-…` copy of the sqlite **before** any mutation.
- Self-contained — does **not** read `chat.db`, so it can be dry-run against a copy of the DB.
- Finds synthetic-key (stableHash) `automation` OUT rows that have a **guid-keyed** OUT twin in the same or a sibling iMessage thread, within ±5 min, matched by `normalizeOutboundTextForDedup` (the exact comparison #497's dedup uses).
- Carries `sentVia=automation` / `replyToMessageId` onto the guid survivor, then deletes only the synthetic duplicate. `--thread <cuid>` narrows scope.

## Verification
- Runner builds clean against #497's `scan-queue.ts`.
- Dry-run → apply → re-dry-run is idempotent. Verified on a DB copy first, then run on the live DB (with backup): collapsed **4** real dups (2× Lanre incl. the reported one, 2× Serena), left **26** synthetic singles untouched.
- After running on live, the runner API for Lanre's thread returns **1** copy (was 2) and the dashboard renders the message once, tagged "sent via automation ✓".

## Note
The forward fix + unit tests originally in this branch were **superseded by #497** (identical approach) and have been dropped; this PR is now just the additive backfill tool. The live duplicates have **already been cleaned** by running this script — merging this only commits the tool for reuse.

author: kaviru2
body:
## Summary

- Adds `eval/dirichlet_analysis.py`: pure analysis of Phase 6/7 results, no API calls
- Updates `STATUS.md`: all phases complete, findings documented with honest limitations

## What this produces

**Three key paper findings:**
1. Distribution framing + thinking=1024 reduces ECE 17.6% (0.205 → 0.169) vs point-prediction baseline
2. Model entropy tracks nondeterminism level — Spearman rho=0.412, p=0.007
3. Anomaly scores (KL(pred||uniform)) show weak/non-significant separation of buggy vs correct programs (Cohen's d=0.294, p=0.503) — underpowered at n=9 buggy groups

**Headline finding — goroutine leak signature:**
P(GoUnblock)=0 at all trace depths for goroutine leak programs (06, 14), vs P(GoUnblock)≈0.15–0.18 for all success programs. Zero false positives. Causally motivated: a permanently blocked goroutine cannot be unblocked.

**Scope clarification (from post-implementation analysis):**
The race program (05) also shows P(GoUnblock)=0 but for a different reason — its buggy path uses no blocking primitives and the WaitGroup unblock falls outside all split windows. This is documented as a confound, not a generalisation of the leak signature. The headline claim is scoped to goroutine leaks.

**Additional findings:**
- Model entropy decreases monotonically with trace depth (rho=-0.314, p=0.043) — model incorporates trace history into uncertainty
- Empirical entropy stable across depths (~1.1 bits), confirming the confidence gain is context-driven

## Test plan
- [ ] `uv run python eval/dirichlet_analysis.py` runs cleanly, writes `eval/results/dirichlet_analysis.json`
- [ ] Three paper findings printed to stdout with correct values
- [ ] Race condition confound note visible in distribution signatures section

## Summary

Browsers discard the query string of GET forms when they are submitted. EasyAdmin already works around this for:

# What does this implement/fix?

The visual editor could not round-trip unicode escape sequences in font glyph fields. A flow list such as `glyphs: ["\U000F058F","\U000F0F19"]` loaded as an empty field, and a typed glyph was emitted as a bare unquoted scalar that ESPHome then read character by character.

The form parser now decodes double quoted escapes, a list nested inside a list item serializes as a flow list instead of collapsing to a scalar, and Private Use and control code points are quoted on emit and shown as editable escapes in the input.

- `js/utils/helpers.js`: `formatDate('long')` month long → short ("Sunday, Jun 4, 2026"); `formatSessionDateTime` separator " • " → ", " — time portion still respects the 12/24h user setting ("Jun 4, 2026, 6:42 PM" / "Jun 4, 2026, 14:30")

author: bonatoneto
body:
## O que foi feito

A mídia de chat (imagem/áudio/vídeo) sobe para o Cloudinary como `type: 'authenticated'` (privada, entregue só via URL assinada), mas as operações do **Admin API** ainda rodavam no namespace público `'upload'` (default do SDK). Como os dois namespaces são separados no Cloudinary, isso causava dois bugs:

- **`getAsset`** (verificação do vídeo no envio direto) buscava em `'upload'` → **404 no asset privado** → o envio de vídeo falhava com 400. Além disso, sem `media_metadata` o Cloudinary **não retorna `duration`** → `durationMs` era persistido como `null`.
- **`delete`** (`destroy`) mirava `'upload'` → **não apagava o asset privado** (o `destroy` retorna `{ result: 'not found' }` sem lançar) → **órfão pago** em toda limpeza de mídia de chat (cota, falha pós-upload, deleção de mensagem).

Correções:
- **`getAsset`**: `type: 'authenticated'` + `media_metadata: true` + coerção de `duration` string→número (o SDK tipa `duration` como `number | string`; `"4.035"` virava `null`).
- **`delete`**: novo param `deliveryType` (default `'upload'` preserva avatar/evento públicos) + `invalidate: true` (purga o asset **e seus derivados**, ex. o poster do vídeo, do cache do CDN) + log quando o `destroy` retorna `'not found'` (torna o namespace errado observável em vez de silencioso).
- **Helper `deleteChatMedia`**: centraliza o `'authenticated'` nos 6 callers de chat, para a correção não depender de lembrar o param em cada call site (o default silencioso era a mesma raiz do bug original). O `'authenticated'` fica **só** no helper de chat, nunca no `delete`/`deleteUploaded` genérico — senão avatar/evento (públicos) regrediriam.
- **Testes**: contrato real do SDK via `vi.spyOn` no singleton do Cloudinary (única camada onde o namespace importa, já que a suíte de integração usa o `FakeStorageService`) + asserção de `deliveryType` por call site no Fake (chat = `authenticated`, avatar/evento = `upload`).

## Por que foi feito

O delivery type é uma dimensão **ortogonal** ao `resource_type` e precisa bater no `destroy`/`resource`. O PR #52 (mídia privada) cobriu o **upload** (`deliveryType: 'authenticated'`) e a **entrega** (`signedUrl`), mas deixou o **Admin API** (`getAsset`/`delete`) no namespace público — então a privacidade "funcionava" na entrega mas quebrava na verificação e na limpeza.

Confirmado ao vivo contra o Cloudinary real: assets de chat existentes estão como `type: upload`; a URL `authenticated` que o backend serve retorna **404**; `resource()` só devolve `duration` com `media_metadata: true`.

> A causa raiz (Admin API no namespace errado) foi atacada diretamente, não remendada. O risco de regressão em mídia pública e a fragilidade do default foram travados por testes. Achados levantados por uma auditoria adversarial multi-agente (duração como string, poster órfão no CDN, falha silenciosa do `destroy`) foram todos incorporados.

## Como testar

```bash
pnpm db:generate                 # client estava defasado (drift conhecido)
pnpm test                        # 471 verdes (22 arquivos)
npx tsc --noEmit                 # 0 erros
pnpm check                       # Biome limpo
```

Cobertura específica:
- `src/lib/storage/cloudinary-storage.service.test.ts` — prova que `delete` chama `destroy` com `{ type: 'authenticated', invalidate: true }`, que `getAsset` chama `resource` com `{ type: 'authenticated', media_metadata: true }`, a coerção de `duration` string e o aviso de `'not found'`.
- `chat.test.ts` — deleção de mensagem (imagem/áudio/vídeo) e limpeza de áudio truncado/inválido deletam com `deliveryType: 'authenticated'`.
- `users.test.ts` — troca de avatar deleta com `deliveryType: 'upload'` (guarda contra regressão na mídia pública).

> ⚠️ Mídia de chat **antiga** (subida como pública antes do #52/deste fix) deixa de resolver no `getAsset`/`delete` após este PR. Em dev é descartável; produção é greenfield (chat é feature nova) — sem migração `rename to_type` por ora.

author: schenlong
body:
## What

The `chroma`, `qdrant`, `llamaindex`, `pinecone`, and `weaviate` connectors are ESM-only (`"type": "module"`), but their `test-d/` type-surface suites still described them as a **"CommonJS package"** in the header JSDoc. This corrects the stale lead-in to **"ESM package"** in all five.

## Why

The connectors were converted to ESM-only in an earlier PR; these five header comments were never updated. This is the `test-d/` sibling of the `src/types.ts` CJS→ESM comment sweep in #37 — split out so that PR's diff stayed minimal.

## Scope (deliberately surgical)

- **Comments only** — one JSDoc line per file (`CommonJS package` → `ESM package`). No code, type, import, or assertion changes (`5 files changed, 5 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)`).
- The trailing tsd **`composite` / `"tsd"`-override rationale is left intact**. It is module-system-agnostic (the override exists because the package tsconfig sets `composite: true`, which is orthogonal to CJS vs ESM) and was verified factually accurate against each `package.json` + `tsconfig.json`:
  - chroma / llamaindex / pinecone / weaviate — `package.json` carries `"tsd": { compilerOptions: { composite: false } }`; package `tsconfig` sets `composite: true`. ✔
  - qdrant — no `"tsd"` block, `tsconfig` is not composite, inherits `NodeNext` from the root `tsconfig`. ✔
- `huggingface` + `vercel` test-d never carried this comment — left untouched.

## No changeset

`test-d/` is excluded from the npm tarball (`files: ["dist", "README.md", "LICENSE"]`), so the change is not user-visible and no changeset is required.

## Verification

- `pnpm quality-gate` (full): **PASS** — typecheck, lint, format:check, test+coverage, build, **test:types (tsd 52/52)**, test:pack, uat, benchmark, sandbox-gate, sandbox-report-determinism. (`dep-audit` advisory WARN is pre-existing upstream peer-dep noise, unaffected by a comment change.)
- Senior-persona audit loop (6 read-only reviewers — developer, architect, adversarial, security, documentation, adherence): converged with **zero findings against the change**.

## Deferred (out of scope)

Reviewers flagged a **pre-existing** cosmetic asymmetry in the *retained* rationale (pinecone/weaviate omit the "because composite: true" clause that chroma/llamaindex carry; minor period drift). It is not introduced by this change and is outside the "correct the CommonJS framing only" scope, so it is tracked separately rather than folded in here.

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds backward-compatible periodic padding support to the existing `NCSNpp` stack, so 3D users can opt into circular boundary behavior without forking the architecture. Default behavior is unchanged (`padding_mode="zeros"`), while `padding_mode="circular"` enables periodic convolutions for voxel/cosmology-style domains.

- **API extension (backward-compatible)**
  - Added `padding_mode` to `NCSNpp` (`"zeros"` default, `"circular"` supported).
  - `padding_mode` is included in model hyperparameters.
  - Circular mode is explicitly scoped to 3D (`dimensions=3`).

- **3D padding semantics wired through NCSNpp path**
  - Threaded `padding_mode` through convolution/resampling helpers used by NCSNpp:
    - `conv3x3` / `conv1x1`
    - `DDPMResnetBlock`
    - `ResnetBlockBigGANpp`
    - `UpsampleLayer` / `DownsampleLayer`
  - Updated manual pre-convolution padding paths to honor circular mode (instead of implicit zero padding).

- **Critical 3D same-padding fix**
  - `Conv3dSame` manual stride>1 path now applies `F.pad(..., mode=padding_mode)` (with correct zero/circular handling), so strided 3D convs no longer silently break periodic boundaries.

- **Unsupported resampling combination is explicit**
  - Added a clear error for `padding_mode="circular"` with `fir=True` in BigGAN-style resampling path, where boundary handling is not periodic-safe in current implementation.

- **Docs + usage**
  - README now includes a periodic 3D `NCSNpp` example.

```python
net = NCSNpp(
    channels=1,
    dimensions=3,
    nf=128,
    ch_mult=[2, 2, 2, 2],
    attention=False,
    fir=False,
    padding_mode="circular",
)
```

author: brokenstandards
body:
## M3 — Storage mirror

A local mirror matching copyparty's layout, written **crash-safely**, plus an offline scan that reuses M2's `group_segments` verbatim.

### What's here
- **`storage::MirrorStore` / `PartFile`** — the crash-safe write primitive M4 streams downloads into: `create_part` → write → `commit` (`flush` → fsync data → atomic `rename` → best-effort parent-dir fsync). `PartFile::writer()` plugs straight into the existing `client.download_to(rel, &mut W)`. Plus `write_all` convenience, `is_complete`/`local_size`, `abort`, and `..`-traversal rejection.
- **`storage::paths`** — `file_rel` / `parse_file_rel` (rel ↔ (segment, file) round-trip) + `safe_join`.
- **`storage::scan::scan_segments`** — the local twin of `list_segments`: same classification, **skips `*.part`**, `rlog.lock` → `recording`, sorts files; `mtime_s`/`remote_size` computed identically to the mock server (`as_secs()` / `len()`).
- **`drive_grouping::local::group_local`** — `Ok(group_segments(scan_segments(dir)?))`, the offline twin of `group_remote`.
- **Cargo:** `tokio` + `fs` feature.

### Headline guarantee
`it_offline_grouping`: for `single_drive`/`gap_split`/`partial`, **`group_local(scan) == group_remote(server)`** as a full `Vec<Drive>` equality — both read the same inodes, so sizes and second-truncated mtimes match exactly. The `.part`-exclusion case is scan-only (the mock server lists `.part` and the client keeps it as `FileKind::Other`, so a remote==local assertion would fail for a harness reason, not a product bug).

### Tests (72 pass; fmt + clippy `-D warnings` clean)
paths round-trip (on-disk + legacy names, traversal/mismatch rejection); MirrorStore atomic-write (pre/post-commit state, dir creation, abort, traversal reject, `write_all`); scan (`.part`/lock exclusion, sizes/mtimes, sorting); `group_local` (empty/missing dir); `it_offline_grouping` (3 fixtures + `.part` scan-only).

### Scope notes
No DB writes in M3 — `seg_file.local_size`/`download_state` reconciliation and partial/resume *classification* are **M5**; deletion/retention is **M6**; per-device mirror subdir + `list_drives(offline)` wiring is **M8**. `SegmentFile.remote_size` carries the on-disk length in the local-scan context (documented).

Plan: `.claude/plans/m3-storage-mirror.md`

author: sean-reid
body:
## What

After Play Again, the host couldn't move — WASD did nothing while the camera worked, and the player jittered as if forced back into place. Repeatable. This is the real fix for that; the earlier seq-reset change was necessary but incomplete.

## Root cause (from a playtest trace)

A client-side trace during the stuck state was decisive:

```
server_pos=-12.27,3.22 frozen=false ackSeq=3150.0 pending=1 pred=-12.27,3.22 seq=23
```

- `ackSeq` pinned at **3150** — the prior match's final input seq.
- New `seq` only 23–44, server position constant, `frozen=false`.

The server gates inputs with `if (input.seq <= lastSeq) continue`. The prior fix cleared `lastAppliedSeq` on replay, but the prior match's **undrained input backlog** (seqs up to 3150) was still sitting in `inputQueues`. On the next match the sim drains that backlog first, which re-raises `lastAppliedSeq` straight back to 3150 — undoing the clear. The rebuilt arena streams `input_seq` from 0, so every new frame is `<= 3150` and rejected. Because those rejects are all `<= ack`, the client prunes its pending buffer and re-bases to the stale server position each tick — that's the jitter.

## Fix

Clear `inputQueues` alongside `lastAppliedSeq` (and the position maps) in `resetForReplay`, so no stale backlog survives into the restarted match and the seq-from-0 stream is accepted.

## Test

`simulate.test.ts` gains a case that leaves a high-seq backlog (3148–3150) **undrained** in the queue, calls `resetForReplay`, then feeds a fresh `seq=1` and asserts it's applied and the player moves. It fails without the clear (backlog drains, mark jumps to 3150, seq-1 rejected) and passes with it. Full room suite: 222 passing.

body:
## Fatia: primeiro runbook operacional "quando o dado real chega" (§8.1.5 / LGPD Art. 18)

Com ingestão + consentimento no lugar, o banco passa a ter dado real. Esta fatia leva o isolamento
de PII (invariantes 1–2) para **também valer em repouso/backup**, sem afrouxar nada.

### O que entra
- **`scripts/backup.sh` + `scripts/restore.sh`** — DOIS artefatos por classe, retenção própria:
  - `acervo-analitico` (sem PII): `pg_dump --exclude-schema=app` rodando como **`role_analitica`**,
    que **estruturalmente não lê `app`** (defesa em profundidade sobre o flag). Retenção 30d.
  - `app-pii` (PII): `pg_dump --schema=app --enable-row-security` como **`role_consentimento`**,
    canalizado direto para **`gpg --symmetric` (AES256)** — nunca toca o disco em claro. Retenção
    **7d** (minimização: a eliminação Art. 18 se propaga ao podar artefatos antigos).
  - Dump **só de dados** (o esquema vem de `alembic upgrade head`); **manifesto** com `sha256`/
    proveniência; restauração privilegiada (admin) com `--disable-triggers` (FKs circulares de
    `territorio`); IVM é recomputado, não restaurado.
- **Migração `0012`** (aditiva): `SELECT` nas sequences do próprio schema para cada role, p/ o
  `pg_dump` ler o estado das colunas IDENTITY rodando como a role de menor privilégio. Nada cruza a
  fronteira §8.1 — `role_analitica` segue sem acesso a `app` (continua testado).
- **`DAGSTER_HOME`**: volume nomeado `dagster_home` no `orchestrator` → histórico de runs/agendamentos
  sobrevive a restart.
- **Docs**: `docs/runbooks/{backup-restore,rotacao-de-segredos,dagster-home}.md` + **ADR-0013**. A
  rotação da `APP_FIELD_KEY` exige anel de chaves (re-chaveamento) — **sinalizado**, não implementado.

### Verificação (Postgres 16 + PostGIS real)
- **Round-trip de DR completo** validado localmente: analítico + app restauram em banco novo migrado,
  contagens batem (valor/territorio/linhagem/assinante_alerta), e o marcador de PII sobrevive ao
  ciclo backup→cifra→restore.
- **CI**: `tests/unit/test_backup_separa_pii.py` (separação **mecânica**, estática) +
  `tests/integration/test_backup_restore.py` (**prova viva**: insere marcador de PII, faz o backup,
  confirma que **não** vaza no dump analítico e **está** no de PII cifrado). `shellcheck` dos
  runbooks; `pg_dump 16` + `gpg` no job de integração. Suíte: **86 testes**, cobertura 95%
  (supressão+ouro **100%**). OpenAPI inalterado.

### A evoluir
Anel de chaves p/ rotacionar `APP_FIELD_KEY`; rotação graciosa do `JWT_SECRET`; storage do Dagster em
Postgres ao escalar; backups off-box + cifragem por destinatário + game-day de restauração.

author: graydawnc
body:
## What Adds the desktop-side half of the OAuth contract whose backend half landed in #357. The renderer asks the main process to sign in; the main process runs the full PKCE dance against the system browser via a loopback callback; the resulting `id_token + nonce` is POSTed to share-backend's `/api/auth/sign-in-with-id-token`; the returned session token is stored in OS keychain. Files: - `src/main/auth/loopback-server.ts` — ephemeral `http.Server` bound to `127.0.0.1:0`, accepts exactly one OAuth callback, validates `state` before painting the success page, 5-minute hard timeout - `src/main/auth/oauth.ts` — provider-agnostic PKCE flow; one `PROVIDERS` entry per protocol (currently just `google`) - `src/main/auth/session-store.ts` — `safeStorage` + `electron-store` wrapper; session token encrypted at rest using the OS keychain (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows, libsecret on Linux) - `src/main/ipc/share-auth.ts` — IPC bridge exposed to the renderer (`shareAuth.signIn / signOut / me / getToken`); revokes any prior session before starting a fresh sign-in - `src/renderer/hooks/useShareAuth.ts` — module-scope `EventTarget` so every component that calls the hook re-syncs on sign-in/sign-out without a navigation - `electron.vite.config.ts` — `inlineMainEnvPlugin` for build-time env inlining (`process.env['SPOOL_*']` → string literal) - `.env.development.local.example` — documents the env vars contributors need to set ## Why Two flows, one identity. The web flow (#357) issues a session cookie scoped to `spool.pro`; the desktop flow needs an opaque bearer string a long-lived Electron process can attach to every API call. Both terminate at `upsertUserByIdentity()` in the backend so the same Google account yields the same `users.id` whether the user signs in via the browser or the app. PKCE-by-loopback is the RFC 8252 prescription for a confidential-client-impersonating native app. The renderer never sees the client secret; even though Google's "installed app" flow requires `client_secret` at the token endpoint, that secret is **inlined into the main bundle at build time** — per Google's own docs it isn't truly confidential for distributed binaries, and the security perimeter is PKCE + `nonce`, not the secret. A loopback callback page that uses `window.close()` would lie to the user — only scripts that themselves opened a window via `window.open()` can close it, and this tab was opened by `shell.openExternal` from the main process. So the success page tells the user to close it manually. That's an aesthetic choice with a correctness reason behind it. ## Sign-in flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant R as Renderer participant M as Main participant LB as Loopback :randomPort participant B as System Browser participant G as Google participant API as share-backend participant KC as OS Keychain R->>M: ipc.shareAuth.signIn('google') M->>M: clear any prior session (sign-out IPC) M->>LB: start, generate state + nonce + PKCE M->>B: shell.openExternal(authorize URL) B->>G: user consents G-->>LB: 302 callback?code&state LB->>LB: validate state (mismatch → 400) LB->>LB: swap code for id_token
(client_id + client_secret + verifier) LB->>M: { id_token, nonce } M->>API: POST /api/auth/sign-in-with-id-token
{ provider:'google', id_token, nonce } API-->>M: { session_token, user } M->>KC: safeStorage.encryptString(session_token) KC-->>M: ciphertext → electron-store M-->>R: { user } R->>R: useShareAuth EventTarget.dispatch('auth-change') ``` ## Trust boundaries ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph build["Build time"] ENV[".env.development.local"] -->|inlineMainEnvPlugin| BUNDLE[main.cjs] end subgraph desktop["Electron process"] M[Main] R[Renderer] KC[(OS keychain)] end BUNDLE --> M R -. IPC only .-> M M --> KC R -. cannot reach .-> KC R -. cannot reach .-> ENV M -->|loopback :random| LB[127.0.0.1] LB -->|state-checked| M M -->|HTTPS + id_token + nonce| API[share-backend] ``` The renderer never sees: the client secret, the PKCE verifier, the OAuth state, or the session token. The main process is the only place those values live; the renderer only knows whether it's signed in and the user's display profile. ## Build-time env inlining The main bundle is plain CJS — it has no `import.meta.env` equivalent. `process.env` lookups against a double-clicked `.app` resolve against a stripped shell environment (often no `PATH`). So `inlineMainEnvPlugin` walks the source AST during build and substitutes: - `process.env.SPOOL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID_DESKTOP` → `"123-xyz.apps.googleusercontent.com"` - `process.env['SPOOL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET_DESKTOP']` → `"GOCSPX-…"` - `process.env['SPOOL_SHARE_BACKEND']` → `"https://spool.pro"` (or dev's `http://localhost:8788`) Empty / missing values are intentionally **omitted** from the substitution map — that lets the runtime fallback fire (e.g. `?? 'https://spool.pro'`). Inlining `""` would silently strand a broken default. ## Gating (prod-safe) The Electron loopback + the renderer's `useShareAuth` are wired up by this PR, but the UI that actually calls `signIn()` is gated behind `useSharePublish()` (lands later in the stack at #ShareLaunchPrep). That hook reads `import.meta.env['VITE_FEATURE_SHAREPUBLISH']` — Vite inlines the value at build time, prod CI doesn't set it, and Terser dead-code-eliminates every guarded branch. Without that flag set, the main-process IPC handlers exist but no renderer code reaches them. Contributors opt in via: ``` # packages/app/.env.development.local (gitignored) VITE_FEATURE_SHAREPUBLISH=1 SPOOL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID_DESKTOP=… SPOOL_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET_DESKTOP=… SPOOL_SHARE_BACKEND=http://localhost:8788 ``` ## Verification - `pnpm --filter @spool-lab/app test:unit` — loopback-server.test.ts (timeout, state-mismatch 400, exactly-one-callback), oauth.test.ts (token exchange shape, nonce binding), session-store.test.ts (round-trip, missing-keychain fallback), share-auth.test.ts (IPC contract, sign-out clears keychain) - Manual: dev build with the env above, click "Sign in with Google" in the published UI, complete the browser dance, return to app → toolbar reflects signed-in user, devtools shows no session token in renderer scope - TOCTOU regression: a hand-crafted callback that swaps `state` for a forged value lands a 400 from the loopback server, not the success page ## Risk Renderer surface invisible to prod builds (see Gating above). Main-process additions are inert until the IPC is invoked. Pure additive — no existing behaviour changes. Submitted by @graydawnc.

##### SUMMARY

When `state: absent` the module required the local bucket, remote credential and target connection to still exist before it would remove a replica link. If the buckets were deleted first, the link could no longer be removed ("Selected local bucket ... does not exist").

Handle `state:absent` immediately after looking up the replica link, before any create-oriented validation. Deletion works purely from the link object, so none of those resources are required. Also makes absent idempotent and able to remove an unhealthy link.

author: andrewn617
body:
### Motivation / Background

While working on https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/57123 @matthewd caught an existing bug on main. When we reload a model with `all_queries` default scopes, we call `all(all_queries)`. But `all` includes queries from the `current_scope` which means we can leak non `all_queries` scopes into what should be an all queries only query.

### Detail

Instead we should call `default_scoped(all_queries: true)` directly. Then we can check the `current_global_scope` to include any current `all_queries` scopes.

author: serjoscha-ir
body:
The image-generation guide tells users to pass `result.merged_grid.tolist()` to `gen_grid_image`, but that **crashes at runtime** whenever the grid has `NaN` cells (no-data cells outside the polygon or inside building footprints — common):

```
requests.exceptions.InvalidJSONError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan
```

`.tolist()` keeps Python `float("nan")`, which `requests` rejects when serialising the JSON body. The pitfall note even acknowledged "NaN do not serialize directly" yet still prescribed `.tolist()`.

**Fix:** use `grid_to_list(result.merged_grid)` (from `infrared_sdk.tiling.merger`), which converts `NaN -> None`. Updated both the example and the pitfall in `07-images.md`.

Hit live while running a UTCI + daylight render smoke against prod during infrared-api-sdk PR #178.

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses follow-up hardening items from the skill propagation council review: bounded tail-read enforcement, clearer scoring-limit semantics, automatic log growth control, and a first-class config toggle for skill propagation. Scope is intentionally narrow to the confirmed findings and existing runtime paths.

- **Bounded tail-read guarantees**
  - `readSkillUsageEntriesTail` now clamps caller-provided `maxBytes` to an internal upper bound (`MAX_TAIL_BYTES`) and normalizes non-finite input.
  - Preserves bounded-memory behavior even if future callers pass oversized values.

- **Windowed scoring-limit clarity**
  - Updated scoring guard language in `skill-propagation-gate` to explicitly state the limit applies to the **tail window** entry count, not total historical session entries.
  - Aligns operator/debug logs with actual behavior.

- **Automatic skill-usage log compaction**
  - Added size-based best-effort compaction trigger in append flow: when `.swarm/skill-usage.jsonl` exceeds 1MB, pruning is invoked with existing retention policy (`500` entries per skill).
  - Uses existing prune logic; no new storage format or migration.

- **Configurable skill propagation**
  - Added `skillPropagation` schema section with `enabled` (default `true`).
  - Wired `src/index.ts` to honor this flag for both:
    - task-time propagation gate (`skillPropagationGateBefore`)
    - reviewer transform scan (`skillPropagationTransformScan`)

```ts
const skillPropagationConfig = SkillPropagationConfigSchema.parse(
  config.skillPropagation ?? {},
);

const skillResult = skillPropagationConfig.enabled
  ? await skillPropagationGateBefore(ctx.directory, inputShape, skillPropagationConfig)
  : { blocked: false, reason: null, recommendedSkills: undefined };
```

author: sohailshafii
body:
## What

A **per-account log of auth events** (§6) so a "recent activity" view can be surfaced later. Nothing recorded these before. This wires the events whose endpoints exist server-side **today**: `login`, `login_failure`, `password_reset`.

## How

- **migration 008 `auth_audit_log`** — `(id, account_id, event, ip inet, created_at)`, indexed `(account_id, created_at DESC)`.
- **`src/auth/audit.ts`** — `recordAuthEvent(log, event, {accountId, ip})`: best-effort (a failed insert is `log.error`'d, never thrown, so auditing can't 500 a login), and `await`ed so the row is ordered before the response (single indexed insert; argon2 already dominates auth latency).
- **`routes/auth.ts`** — wired into login (success → `login`; wrong-password and unverified → `login_failure`, with `account_id` null for an unknown username) and password-reset/confirm (→ `password_reset`).

## Decisions

- **`account_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, not CASCADE** — the audit log must *outlive* the account (account deletion is itself an audited event; §6 keeps audit logs ~180 days). After a delete the rows remain with a null account.
- **`event` is plain `text`** validated by the TS `AuthEvent` union — so the reserved events below need no migration to start emitting.
- **Reserved, not wired:** `account_deletion` and `push_subscription_added`/`_removed` — those endpoints don't exist server-side yet (the web shipped account-deletion UI ahead of the server; push is the upcoming §5 server work).
- **Out of scope (follow-ups):** retention pruning (~180d, pairs with the session sweeper) and the user-facing recent-activity view (§6 explicitly defers it).

## Tests

- `src/auth/audit.test.ts` — insert (event/account/ip), null account, **survives account deletion** (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), best-effort swallow (bad `inet` → resolves + logs, never throws).
- `src/routes/auth.test.ts` — end-to-end via `app.inject()`: successful login → `login`; wrong password → `login_failure` (account set); unknown username → `login_failure` (null account); completed reset → `password_reset`.
