author: lmliam
body:
## Summary

Closes #41.

Adds optional Linux power-source metrics collected from `/sys/class/power_supply` and carries them through the sampler, parser, local model, JSONL export, text output, and TUI dashboard.

## What Changed

- Added a normalized `PowerSupplyStat` model plus sample-level summary fields for external power, battery percent/status, estimated draw, UPS presence, and source name.
- Added a `power.sh` sampler module that discovers all sysfs power supplies, reports all supplies in structured JSON, treats any online external supply as external power online, selects the lowest reported battery percentage for the concise battery summary, and detects UPS supplies.
- Added power draw support from `power_now`, with `current_now` and `voltage_now` as the documented fallback.
- Added a conditional Power panel to the TUI and a compact `Power ...` suffix to text output only when power data exists.
- Added normalized JSONL fields including `power_supplies`, `external_power_online`, `battery_percent`, `battery_status`, `power_draw_w`, `ups_present`, and `power_source_name`.
- Documented sysfs requirements, supported fields, multiple-battery behavior, unavailable-field behavior, and known limitations in the README.

## User Impact

Remote laptops, mini PCs, and UPS-backed Linux hosts can now surface AC/USB/mains/UPS state, battery percentage/status, and estimated power draw when the kernel exposes those fields. Hosts without power-supply sysfs data continue to emit valid samples and do not gain noisy text/TUI rows.

author: boujonlaurin-dotcom
body:
## Contexte
Hotfix d'une régression introduite par #798 : **La Grille du jour ne s'affichait plus du tout** (feed, sticky header « Mot du jour », carte CTA) pour les comptes personnalisés.

## Cause
#798 a rendu la Grille non-réordonnable dans la modal « Mes favoris » → sa clé `grille` n'entre plus dans `tournee_order_v1`. Or `applyOrder` **relègue en fin de liste** toute clé absente de l'ordre sauvegardé (pas « à sa position par défaut »). Pour un compte personnalisé, la Grille passait derrière les favoris → **coupée par le cap de 5 → disparition totale**.

## Correctif
Dans `_orderedTourneeKeys` (`flux_continu_provider.dart`), un seul point de vérité :
- la Grille est **exclue d'`applyOrder`** ;
- elle est ensuite **épinglée juste après les Actus** (`actusIndex + 1`, ou en tête si Actus masqué), avant le `.take(cap)`.

Le feed (slot), le sticky header (onglet « Mot du jour ») et la carte `GrilleCtaCard` dérivent tous de `grilleSlotIndex` → les 3 surfaces sont restaurées d'un coup.

## Tests
- Nouveau test de régression : compte personnalisé, ordre sans clé `grille` + assez de favoris pour remplir le cap → `grilleSlotIndex == 1` (Grille juste après Actus).
- Test legacy « ordre utilisateur prime en mode serène » mis à jour : la Grille n'est plus réordonnable, donc toujours collée aux Actus.
- Suite `flux_continu/providers` + modal : verts, `flutter analyze` clean.

## Impact
Aucun changement backend / migration. Front-only.

author: kompfner
body:
Since `WebsocketLLMService` was introduced (#4211), core `llm_service.py` imported the optional `websockets` package unconditionally. So a missing `websockets` broke importing every LLM service with a raw `ImportError` — short-circuiting the `try/except` guard each service wraps its optional imports in to point users at the right `pipecat-ai[...]` extra (e.g. `[openai]`).

`WebsocketLLMService` is only used by `OpenAIResponsesLLMService`, whose install path already pulls in `websockets`. This PR:

- Moves `WebsocketLLMService` and `WebsocketReconnectedError` to a new `pipecat.services.websocket_llm_service` module that owns the dependency.
- Imports them in the OpenAI Responses service inside its existing `try/except`, so the missing-dependency message is the one users see.
- Re-exports both symbols from `llm_service.py` lazily via module `__getattr__`, keeping the released `from pipecat.services.llm_service import WebsocketLLMService` import path working without re-introducing the top-level `websockets` dependency.

## Testing

- With `websockets` blocked, `import pipecat.services.llm_service` now succeeds; importing the OpenAI Responses service logs the `pip install pipecat-ai[openai]` message and raises `ImportError`.
- With `websockets` present, lazy access of the moved symbols and the OpenAI service work unchanged.
- `tests/test_llm_service.py`, `tests/test_openai_responses_websocket.py`, `tests/test_openai_llm_timeout.py` — 53 passed.

## Summary
🤖 Generated with [Nori](https://noriagentic.com/)

Closes ENG-123. Adds drift schema snapshots + a step-through migration test for the SQLite/drift layer (the highest-risk untested surface), and fixes a real upgrade bug those tests exposed.

- **Bug fixed:** the `from < 6` step `createTable(localStorytellers)` emits the table's *current* (v10) shape — already carrying `serverId/syncStatus/retryCount/lastRetryAt` — and the `from < 10` step then re-added those four columns. So upgrading a **schema v1–v5 database straight to v10** threw `duplicate column name` and the DB failed to open. (drift wraps `onUpgrade` in a transaction, so it rolls back — no data is lost, but the DB is unusable until a fixed build ships.) Guarded the v10 storyteller adds with `from >= 6 && from < 10`.
- **Snapshots + tests:** `drift_schemas/drift_schema_v1..v10.json` (v10 dumped from the real DB; v1–v9 reconstructed — none existed historically), generated `SchemaVerifier` fixtures under `test/core/database/generated/` (committed like `.g.dart`, analysis-excluded), and `test/core/database/migration_test.dart`: migrates every historical version → v10 and validates the resulting schema, plus data-preservation cases for an un-uploaded recording (v1→v10) and a storyteller (v6→v10, the exact branch the fix touches).
- **Docs:** new `lib/core/database/docs.md` covering the migration/snapshot workflow, the 5-step "add a new schema version" process, and the `createTable`-emits-current-shape footgun.

## Test Plan
- [x] `flutter test test/core/database/migration_test.dart` → 11 green (was RED on v1–v5→v10 before the fix, proving the guard works)
- [x] Full suite green locally; `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` clean (no new issues); `dart format` clean
- [x] CI `Test` + `Lint` jobs green on this PR

## Notes for reviewers
- Merged latest `dev` (incl. ENG-89 strict lint + the `Test`/`Lint` workflows). The migration test runs under the existing `test.yml` (full `flutter test`) — no new workflow added.
- Committed snapshots carry a slightly newer drift schema-format `_meta.version` than the post-merge `drift_dev` emits (the `entities` are byte-identical) — cosmetic; a future re-dump would show a no-op metadata diff.
- The Linear description says a botched upgrade "drops un-uploaded recordings"; investigation shows it actually **bricks** (data stranded, not deleted). The genuine data-loss risk would be a naive DB-wipe recovery — deliberately not added.

author: ginsupig
body:
## Why

Both bracket builders hardcoded `type="market"` on the **entry leg**, so the bot paid whatever the book offered on every entry. On a high-churn strategy (114 fills today) that slippage adds up — and it's invisible on paper but real when you go live.

## What

The executor now prices the **entry leg as a marketable limit** when enabled:
- **Buy:** limit placed `LIMIT_ENTRY_OFFSET_BPS` **above** the planned entry → crosses the spread up and fills.
- **Short sell:** limit placed the same **below** entry → crosses down and fills.

This caps worst-case entry slippage to ~the offset while still filling in normal conditions. Exit legs (take-profit limit / stop) are unchanged.

Wired via `ExecutionConfig` (`use_limit_entry` / `limit_entry_offset_bps` / `tif`), read from `USE_LIMIT_ENTRY` (**default true**), `LIMIT_ENTRY_OFFSET_BPS` (8), `TRADE_TIF` (day). Set `USE_LIMIT_ENTRY=false` to revert to market entries.

> **Tradeoff:** if price runs past the offset before filling, the entry may not fill (the bracket sits working until the EOD cancel). That's the deliberate slippage-vs-fill-certainty choice — 8 bps fills in normal tape but protects against chasing a fast move.

## Tests
Long buy limit prices **above** entry (100.00 → 100.08), short sell **below** (→ 99.92), and the market-order default still holds. Full suite: **139 passed.**

author: mir-quadri
body:
## Summary

Wires the engine's `Judge` interface to the now-live `/api/judge` proxy (B3 Unit 1, #17). Headline and About lift above the structural B+ ceiling toward A when the judge confirms the structural cues; harsh judgments can never drop a section below its structural floor; the audit gracefully degrades to today's structural-only output on any proxy failure.

The proxy is deployed and smoke-verified at ~$0.0097/audit (#17). This PR turns "pending AI review" into real Headline + About judgments + Headline/About before-after rewrites, gated behind the email submit (#16 contract preserved).

## What's new

**`lib/judge/httpJudge.ts`** — `HttpJudge implements Judge`:
- POSTs to the proxy with `X-Judge-Auth: <JUDGE_PROXY_SECRET>`.
- Stamps `auditId` on every request so proxy logs correlate.
- 15s caller-side timeout (margin over the proxy's 12s upstream cap).
- **NEVER throws** — every failure (HTTP non-2xx, proxy `judge_unavailable`, network error, `AbortError`) resolves to `{}` so the engine keeps `needsReview: true`.
- Observability hook (`onResult`) fires once per evaluate with status/usage/elapsed/reason; the route logs cost-per-audit through this.

**`lib/judge/createServerJudge.ts`** — factory the audit route uses:
- `HttpJudge` when `JUDGE_PROXY_SECRET` is set; `NullJudge` otherwise (local dev / unconfigured deploys keep working — same fallback contract the proxy already guarantees).
- Defaults `JUDGE_PROXY_URL` to `<request-origin>/api/judge` so the same Vercel function reaches itself. `JUDGE_PROXY_URL` env overrides for split deployments.

## Engine changes

**Lift-only floor invariant** (`scoring/sections/headline.ts`, `scoring/sections/about.ts`):
- Snapshot the structural-only score BEFORE applying judge adjustments, then take `max(structuralFloor, judgeAdjusted)` at the end.
- A harsh judgment can no longer turn a structurally-decent B into a D — exactly the invariant the B3 brief calls out (`structural grades are FLOORS`).
- Without judgment: behaviour unchanged (`structural == floor` by definition).

**Mode-aware `expectedJudgeKeys`** (`scoring/index.ts`):
- The 4-section PDF MVP proxy only judges Headline + About + cross-cutting buzzwords (`lib/judge/buildPrompt.ts`). PDF mode now expects only that set — otherwise a clean proxy response would always report `judgeStatus: 'partial'` because currentExperience/keywords/photo/banner/featured were never asked for.
- Full mode (extension audit) keeps the broader expectation set.

## Wiring

**`app/api/audit/route.ts`**:
- Generate `auditId` up front (needed to stamp the judge request).
- `buildJudgeRequest(parsed)` → set `rewriteTargets: ['headline','about']` (4-section MVP scope).
- `judge.evaluate()` runs BEFORE `runPdfAudit()` so judgments flow into the scorers, the engine applies the lift, and the **stored** audit reflects the lifted composite + cleared `needsReview` flags.
- **One proxy call per audit**: the judge response is baked into the stored audit; email/result routes read from the store and never re-call the judge. Cost invariant.
- Logs cost-per-audit on success: `usd=…`, `inputTokens=…`, `outputTokens=…`, `elapsedMs=…`.

## Gate preserved (#16 contract intact)

- Preview (`lib/audit/buildPreview.ts`) is unchanged — it never carried `rewrites`, `wins`, or `fixes`. The gate test in `buildPreview.gate.test.ts` now pins that AI rewrites (Headline/About before/after) don't leak into the pre-gate payload either.
- Email + result routes unchanged — they read the stored audit, which carries the lifted scores and rewrites.
- Pre-gate composite + 4 letter grades stay byte-identical pre/post-gate (the same stored audit underwrites both).

## Tests added (23 new)

`lib/judge/__tests__/httpJudge.test.ts` (9):
- happy-path: returns judgeResponse, sends `X-Judge-Auth`, stamps `auditId` in the body
- graceful degradation: 200 `judge_unavailable` → `{}`; 403 → `{}`; 5xx → `{}`; network error → `{}`; AbortError timeout → `{}` with `reason='timeout'`; throwing `onResult` doesn't break evaluate
- cost invariant: exactly one fetch per evaluate

`lib/engine/__tests__/judgeLift.test.ts` (11):
- LIFT: strong headline + confirming judgment → above B+ cap; strong About + confirming judgment → above structural
- FLOOR: harsh judgment on decent headline/About → score ≥ structural floor; harsh judgment on weak D headline → still ≥ floor (Mir's D never becomes F)
- needsReview clears ONLY on the sections the judge returned for
- composite differentiation: strong + judged > strong + structural; weak + harsh ≥ weak + structural
- judgeStatus: `ok` when proxy returns the PDF MVP set, `unavailable` when nothing came back, `partial` when buzzwords drop

`lib/audit/__tests__/buildPreview.gate.test.ts` (+1):
- rewrites (literal `rewrite` key + before/after text) absent from the pre-gate JSON

## Manual smoke

- Proxy-down path: with `JUDGE_PROXY_SECRET` unset, the route prints a one-shot warn and falls back to `NullJudge`; the resulting audit is byte-identical to today's structural-only output (the `needsReview` flags stay set, composite stays under B+).

## Verification

- 218/218 tests pass
- `pnpm typecheck` clean
- `pnpm build` clean
- `grep -rE "ANTHROPIC|sk-ant|x-api-key|anthropic-version" .next/static` → no matches
- `grep -rE "JUDGE_PROXY_SECRET|X-Judge-Auth" .next/static` → no matches

## Out of scope (per the Unit 2 brief)

- Extension-side judge wiring (separate repo; engines intentionally differ now)
- Career Arc / Current Experience AI judging (4-section MVP is Headline + About)
- Erum parser bug
- Homepage/footer copy revision

## Test plan

- [ ] Re-audit John's profile on preview: composite moves UP from 68.8; Headline lifts above B+ toward A; "pending AI review" gone on Headline + About
- [ ] Re-audit Mir's profile on preview: composite moves UP from 58.3; Headline D holds the floor (does not drop further); Mir↔John spread preserved or widens
- [ ] Verify rewrites appear ONLY in the post-gate report, not in the pre-gate response (DevTools Network tab)
- [ ] Sanity-check Vercel logs: `[api/audit] judge auditId=… status=ok usd=…` lines visible
- [ ] Proxy-down smoke: temporarily clear `JUDGE_PROXY_SECRET` in a preview deploy, confirm audit completes with structural-only output

## Summary

An audit of phases 0–13 against `docs/chronos_total_parity_matrix.md` (see new `docs/chronos_phase_audit_2026-06-05.md`) surfaced two hard launch blockers plus proof-quality gaps. This PR lands all five recommended fixes. Backend suite: **469 passed, 1 skipped** against a clean-migrated DB.

author: croakingtoad
body:
## Problem

Projects could silently end up pointing at a **parent** directory — e.g. a project saved with path `/home/marty/repos/` instead of `/home/marty/repos/local-event-monitor`. Two root causes:

1. **No normalization / validation on save.** `POST /projects` stored `req.body.path` verbatim. A trailing slash, a bare parent dir, or a non-existent path was all accepted silently. (The folder picker never produces a trailing slash — `resolve()`/`join()` strip it — so these entries come from free-text typing.)
2. **No way to fix it afterward.** Edit mode rendered the path **read-only**, and `PATCH /projects/:id` didn't accept a `path` field at all.

## Changes

**Server (`routes/projects.ts`)**
- `normalizeProjectPath()` — trims whitespace and strips trailing slashes. Applied on **create** and on the new PATCH path branch.
- `PATCH /projects/:id` now accepts `path` (**repoint only — files are not moved**). Empty path → `400`. Because `projects.path` is `UNIQUE`, an exact collision is translated into a clean **`409`** instead of surfacing the constraint as a `500`.

**Dashboard (`ProjectDashboard.tsx`, `lib/api.ts`)**
- **Working Directory is editable in edit mode** (text input + folder browser), no longer read-only. Repointing shows a "files are not moved" hint.
- **Warn-only validation** (add + edit): flags non-existent folders, non-absolute paths, and **"this is a parent of another project's folder"** — advisory, never blocks save.
- Update mutation sends the normalized path and writes edited CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/settings to the new location; folder-pick no longer auto-renames in edit mode.

## Verification

Built and deployed against the running v1.0.84 instance; tested live:
- PATCH path with trailing slash → stored normalized (no slash) ✓
- PATCH to an exact-duplicate path → `409` with a clear message ✓
- PATCH empty path → `400` ✓
- `tsc --noEmit` + production builds pass for server and dashboard.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #38.

Adds CLI controls for selecting network interfaces before rendering/export:

- `-net-include` accepts comma-separated interface names or simple glob patterns.
- `-net-exclude` applies after include selection.
- `-net-aggregate` replaces selected per-interface rows with one synthetic `aggregate` row.
- Defaults preserve the existing sampler/display behavior when no network selection flags are provided.

## Behavior

- Include patterns are evaluated first; when present, only matching interfaces are eligible.
- Exclude patterns are evaluated after include patterns.
- Empty pattern values/segments and malformed glob patterns fail during config parsing.
- Valid patterns that match no sampled interfaces produce an empty network set.
- TUI state/history, non-interactive text output, and JSONL output all use the same selected interface set.
- Aggregate rows sum RX/TX rates, packet rates, issue counters, and known positive link speeds while keeping unknown sentinel behavior when no known values are present.

## Tests

## Summary

author: akhayam99
body:
## What

Switching workspaces silently killed any agent still running in the workspace you were leaving. `setCurrentWorkspace` cancels every running turn (it kills the provider child processes so they stop emitting events into stale sessions) before wiping the in-memory cache, so in-flight agents died with no warning.

This adds an explicit confirmation step.

## How

- New store state `pendingWorkspaceSwitch` + actions `requestWorkspaceSwitch` / `confirmWorkspaceSwitch` / `cancelWorkspaceSwitch` in the workspaces slice.
- `requestWorkspaceSwitch` is the gate: no running agents -> switches straight through (zero friction); one or more running -> records the target and opens a confirm dialog.
- `WorkspaceSwitchDialog` lists each running session (spinner, goal, auto-mode badge) and explains the turns stop now and won't resume on their own, with `Stay here` / `Switch to <name>`.
- The three user entry points route through the gate: sidebar workspace cards, command palette, and the index keyboard shortcut.
- Programmatic switches (boot restore, add-workspace, delete) keep calling `setCurrentWorkspace` directly and bypass the prompt by design.

## Notes

- Confirm button uses the `warning` variant, not `danger`: interrupting a turn is not permanent data loss (transcript is kept, the agent can be re-run), so red is reserved for End/Delete.

## Tests

- Slice contract: switch-through when idle, defer + record target when running, confirm clears pending and moves, cancel stays put.
- Component: renders nothing when no pending switch, warns and lists running agents, confirm/cancel wiring.
- Updated the existing WorkspaceSelect and CommandPalette test mocks for the renamed action.

body:
## Changelog

### Added
- Shared backend setting constraints for operational tuning values, including type, minimum, and maximum ranges.
- API tests covering valid boundaries, below/above range rejects, integer-only validation, float NaN/Inf rejects, and zero-allowed retry settings.
- Runtime policy tests proving unsafe persisted values are clamped or fall back before they can drive excessive work.
- Frontend range metadata for exposed polling worker and isolation controls.

### Changed
- Settings API numeric, float, boolean, and backup interval inputs now trim whitespace before parsing and persist normalized numeric values.
- Runtime consumers now use the shared constraints when reading polling intervals, SNMP worker pools, timeout/retry values, polling budgets, WebSocket coalescing, persistence batching, capacity safety margin, and backup retention counts.
- Device and instance backup retention validation now matches the backend range of `1..365`.
- Settings panel worker controls now use range-aware validation and input `min`/`max` attributes instead of positive-integer-only checks.

### Fixed
- Direct settings writes can no longer persist out-of-range operational values that could create unbounded worker counts, excessive SNMP fanout, retry storms, near-zero timers, excessive WebSocket churn, or excessive persistence batching behavior.
- Existing invalid persisted values are contained at read time through clamping or fallback behavior instead of being trusted blindly.
- Frontend worker fields no longer autosave obvious out-of-range values before the backend rejects them.
- Custom polling interval and bridge port handling no longer accepts decimal-like input through `parseInt` coercion.

author: sellakumaran
body:
A connect-time transport failure (DNS/socket HttpRequestException, or an HttpClient-timeout TaskCanceledException) thrown by the HTTP send escaped the per-attempt auth loop in TeamsGraphBackendConfigurator, which only retried on 401 / "Invalid roles" status codes. A momentary DNS blip against the Front Door / Traffic Manager-fronted agent365.svc.cloud.microsoft endpoint therefore failed registration outright with no retry.

Wrap the send in both SetBackendConfigurationAsync (POST) and ClearBackendConfigurationAsync (DELETE) with the existing RetryHelper, which retries transient transport exceptions with exponential backoff and returns the response so the auth-refresh and status-code handling stay intact. Request content is rebuilt per attempt because HttpContent / HttpRequestMessage are single-use.

author: accauble
body:
## Motivation

The LD_PRELOAD interposer redirects /sys/class/{drm,kfd} but not /sys/bus/pci/devices/.... When RCCL builds its NCCL topology it falls back to real host PCIe data at the BDFs our simulated GPUs claim (location_id  0x300/0x400 -> 0000:03:00.0/0000:04:00.0, which on the test host are real AMD devices with mismatched PCI classes and bridge parents). The asymmetric class codes produced an asymmetric XGMI graph, NCCL's path BFS rejected it ("Failed to find reverse path"), and the five RcclDaemonTest.{AllReduce,Broadcast,AllGather,ReduceScatter, SendRecv} tests failed. NCCL also probed the host's real RoCE NIC and timed out on ibv_create_cq.

## Fix 

Mirror the existing fake-sysfs pattern: the daemon now writes a symmetric NCCL topology XML (all <pci> direct children of <cpu>, class=0x130000, mutual <xgmi tclass=0x130000>) into the existing topology_dir_, and the interposer points clients at it via NCCL_TOPO_FILE. NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 is set with overwrite=0 so users can opt back in for IB testing. The handshake protocol bumps to v3 to carry the new path; mismatched daemon/client fail fast at the existing version check. Local mode (in-process simulation) gets the same env wiring after VM creation.

## Test Plan

RcclDaemonTests need to all pass

## Test Result

All tests pass now

author: kevintiktokai
body:
## Why

Screens currently disagree about a field: the Field Detail page shows "EXCELLENT HEALTH" over a "Critical" NDVI, the Agronomist Insight panel says "Field not found" for fields that exist, confidence renders as "0.6%", and the Crop Health Trends chart has an unlabelled axis. Each screen fetches and interprets data independently, so they drift.

This PR builds the **canonical source of truth** — a Field State Aggregator that every screen reads from. After this, contradictions are impossible by construction: if two screens disagree, that's a bug, because they read the same document.

## What

**Audit (Step A)** — `crop_profiles/_architecture/field_state_audit.md` documents every consumer screen's endpoints, the data each consumes, where interpretation happens locally, the cross-screen contradictions, and the **data gaps** (no `tenant_id` column, missing index columns, free-text variety, localStorage-only scouting) the aggregator handles gracefully rather than fabricating.

**Aggregator (Steps B–C)** — `services/field_state/`:
- `models.py` — the `FieldState` Pydantic contract. Confidence is **always** a band + integer pct (the type makes "0.6%" unrepresentable); units are explicit; KurimaScore is 0–100; the trend uses KurimaScore, not raw NDVI.
- `classifiers.py` — **all** interpretation moved server-side: NDVI label by crop+stage, water balance, soil moisture, confidence banding, completeness.
- `generic_crop_math.py` — crop-agnostic KurimaScore mirroring the tobacco interface for non-tobacco crops (tobacco still uses its own Phase-2 model).
- `aggregator.py` — pure `assemble_field_state(...)` + async `build_field_state(...)`. Composes yield_model, tobacco_math/generic math, climate_service, agronomic_engine, proactive_intelligence, and direct DB reads. **Contradictions are resolved algorithmically**: the score is derived from how NDVI sits inside the stage-expected band, so a low NDVI at a high-expectation stage forces a low score *and* raises an alert.
- `GET /field/{field_id}/state` added to `app.py` (consumer session or `X-API-Key` institutional with tenant scoping; **403 for out-of-scope, 404 for absent**; 120s cache).

**Bug fixes (Step E)**:
1. **Confidence** — banded at source (frontend PR renders band + pct).
2. **"Field not found" insight** — root cause is the `WHERE f.id = … AND f.user_id = …` query in `GET /fields/{id}/insight` returning no row on a scope mismatch. That endpoint is now marked **deprecated**; the panel reads `kurima_score.{primary_driver,likely_cause,recommended_action}` from the aggregator, which runs in the field's own scope.
3. **Identical test data** — root cause: `analyze_field` sampled satellite data at the **first polygon vertex** (`coords[0]`), so fields whose first corners fell in the same ~200 m Sentinel bbox/cache tile collapsed to identical NDVI. Fixed to sample at the polygon **centroid** (the satellite worker itself is untouched per the constraints). The seed script only seeds `crop_varieties`, not `daily_logs`, so it was the ingestion call site, not a seeder.

**Tests (Step F)** — `tests/test_field_state_aggregator.py` + `tests/test_consumer_screens_integration.py`:
- happy path, sparse data, **contradiction resolution** (low NDVI at high-expectation stage → low score + alert), **multi-tenant 403-vs-404**, performance, unit consistency (no fractional %), and an integration test proving no screen can display contradictory state.

## Test coverage & performance

```
tests/test_field_state_aggregator.py ............ (12 passed)
tests/test_consumer_screens_integration.py ...... (6 passed)
tests/test_tobacco_math.py .......... (50 passed, unchanged)
```
Pure assembly compute is ~15–35 ms for a 90-day index history (network/DB excluded); the endpoint targets <300 ms and is cached for 120 s.

## Constraints honoured
- `yield_model.py`, `tobacco_math.py`, and the satellite ingestion worker are **not modified** — the aggregator composes their outputs.
- No new dependencies (FastAPI + Pydantic + httpx only).

## Deprecations
- `GET /fields/{id}/insight` — kept running during the frontend transition, marked `deprecated=True`, superseded by `GET /field/{id}/state`.

## Notes
- Screenshots: behaviour changes are covered by the integration test (`test_field_detail_has_no_excellent_over_critical`, `test_agronomist_insight_never_field_not_found`, `test_crop_health_trend_uses_kurima_score_0_100`) since this environment can't render the UI.

body:
## Summary
- add an ExchangeV3-only order signing method for exact base-unit maker/taker amounts
- bypass the legacy CLOB price/tick floating-point rounding path
- preserve builder codes and deposit-wallet signature semantics

## Scope
This is intentionally isolated to ExchangeV3. It does not change V1/V2 order methods, options, types, rounding, or exchange routing.

## Context
Combo RFQ acceptance signs the maker limit price while preserving the bundle share quantity. The existing `createOrder(price, size)` path rounds through the market tick configuration; for a 0.125 combo price with a 0.01 tick it signs 0.13, causing the RFQ engine to reject the acceptance. `createExchangeV3OrderFromAmounts` lets the RFQ caller sign exact E6 amounts without changing any existing order behavior.

## Verification
- `pnpm test` (281 tests)
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`
- Biome checks

Stacked on #79 because it uses ExchangeV3 signing support.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces a new on-chain order signing entry point; scope is limited to ExchangeV3 and additive, but incorrect amounts or semantics could produce invalid or rejected signatures.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **ExchangeV3-only** signing path for callers that already have exact `makerAmount` / `takerAmount` base-unit strings, so orders are not derived through the existing `createOrder` price and tick rounding.
> 
> **`ExchangeV3OrderAmounts`** is exported from a new `ordersV3` type module. **`createExchangeV3OrderFromAmounts`** validates positive integer amounts, targets `exchangeV3` via `buildOrder` (version 3), and keeps existing maker/signer rules (funder, `POLY_1271` deposit wallet). **`ClobClient.createExchangeV3OrderFromAmounts`** requires L1 auth and applies configured builder codes like other create methods.
> 
> V1/V2 `createOrder` / `createMarketOrder` behavior is unchanged. Unit tests cover exact amount preservation, signature types, and invalid amounts.

body:
## Summary

Migrated the net worth tracker from a static HTML file with inline JavaScript to a modern Next.js application with React components, server-side API routes, and modular styling.

## Key Changes

- **Converted to Next.js App Router:** Replaced `index.html` with a Next.js 14 project structure (`app/page.js`, `app/layout.js`, `app/globals.css`)
- **Server-side quote fetching:** Created `/api/quotes` route that proxies Yahoo Finance v8 chart API requests, eliminating CORS issues and keeping API calls server-side only
- **React component architecture:** Rewrote the entire UI as a single React component with hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, `useMemo`, `useCallback`) for state management and derived calculations
- **Extracted portfolio data:** Moved hardcoded portfolio holdings into `app/portfolio.js` with structured exports (`INDIAN`, `US`, `FDS`, `STATIC`, `RETIREMENT`, `CAT_COLORS`)
- **Modular styling:** Moved inline CSS from HTML into `app/globals.css` with CSS custom properties for theming
- **Enhanced functionality:**
  - Live USD/INR rate fetching and display
  - Market status indicators (NSE/NYSE open/closed) from Yahoo's `marketState`
  - Sortable US stocks table with multi-column sort
  - SessionStorage caching with 10-minute TTL to reduce API calls
  - Auto-refresh every 15 minutes with manual refresh button
  - Skeleton loaders for async data
  - Improved error handling and status messaging

## Implementation Details

- The API route uses a fallback host strategy (query1 → query2) with 8-second timeouts and browser User-Agent spoofing to avoid Yahoo rate-limiting
- Responses are CDN-cached for 60 seconds with `stale-while-revalidate` to reduce load
- All calculations (P&L, percentages, asset allocation) are memoized to prevent unnecessary recalculations
- The UI gracefully handles missing prices with skeleton placeholders and error states
- Portfolio data is static but easily extensible; live prices are layered on top at runtime

## Summary

Move city Telegram broadcast groups out of the GPP Google Sheet into a new
`city_telegram_groups` DB table (DB is the source of truth). Each group can be
FK-linked to its GPP `Party`. Adds two **per-recipient** broadcast template
tokens, both resolved server-side:

- `{link}` → `https://rsv.pizza/${customUrl || inviteCode}` (public event page)
- `{appLink}` → `https://rsv.pizza/host/${inviteCode}/${appTab}` (chosen host app; the URL segment is the app's `tab`, not its `id`)

Unlinked groups (or a missing slug / no app chosen) leave the tokens **empty** —

No Prisma auto-migration in this repo — apply manually via Supabase MCP / `pg`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE "city_telegram_groups" (
  "id"         text         NOT NULL,
  "party_id"   uuid,
  "chat_id"    bigint       NOT NULL,
  "chat_url"   text,
  "city"       text         NOT NULL,
  "country"    text         NOT NULL,

);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "city_telegram_groups_chat_id_key"
  ON "city_telegram_groups" ("chat_id");

CREATE INDEX "city_telegram_groups_party_id_idx"
  ON "city_telegram_groups" ("party_id");

ALTER TABLE "city_telegram_groups"
  ADD CONSTRAINT "city_telegram_groups_party_id_fkey"
  FOREIGN KEY ("party_id") REFERENCES "parties" ("id")
  ON DELETE SET NULL ON UPDATE CASCADE;
```

2. Merge this PR → backend auto-deploys from master.

author: a-horde-o-bees
body:
Two consistency fixes to the submodule-routing feature.

**One mechanical pre-flight.** `pr.py routes` routes the parent *and* every declared submodule in a single in-process pass — each repo's integration verdict plus a combined gap list with fix strings. Checkpoint calls it once and spends no per-repo reasoning gathering routing; the only context left is the unavoidable PR landings.

**Any gap halts, parent or submodule.** Replaces the prior incoherent split (submodule `branch=` gaps were advisory via git-doctor, while permission gaps halted in the router). Now any gap — undeterminable permission, undeclared push branch, edits to a read-only repo — halts up front with the full fix list and a git-doctor pointer.

**No silent fallback.** git-push no longer infers an undeclared `submodule.<name>.branch` from the checked-out branch (which could push wherever HEAD points) — it exits and points to git-doctor. One rule everywhere; the pre-flight catches it before any work starts.

`pr.py`: `routes` subcommand over a pure `branch_gap` helper; `_origin_slug` gains a cwd. Bumps git to 0.0.21.

author: fsawadogo
body:
## Summary

Universal Links for password reset are blocked because the AASA file at `portal.aurionclinical.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` returns HTTP 301 from S3 origin. Apple's `swcd` daemon NEVER follows redirects, so iOS rejects the domain claim. Three prior PRs shipped the file to the deploy bundle and added an Amplify `custom_rule` rewrite — yet the URL still 301s. This PR moves the AASA payload to a NON-hidden path and rewrites the canonical Apple URL to it.

## What changed

- `web/public/aurion-aasa-payload` (NEW) — byte-identical copy of the AASA payload at a non-hidden path. Next.js' static export copies it to `out/aurion-aasa-payload` automatically (no postbuild hook needed for this file — it's not under a hidden directory).
- `infrastructure/amplify.tf` — `custom_rule` target changed from `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` (self-loop) to `/aurion-aasa-payload`. Existing `custom_headers` block stays untouched; Amplify header rules match on the SOURCE URL, so `Content-Type: application/json` continues to apply on the canonical URL.
- `web/tests/AasaFile.spec.ts` — adds a regression test asserting the non-hidden copy is byte-identical to the canonical hidden file. If they drift, iOS will see the WRONG App ID on the live URL while the canonical file looks correct in review — exactly the kind of silent breakage this test catches in CI.
- Original `web/public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` is RETAINED as a belt-and-suspenders fallback (some Apple tooling looks at both). Removal deferred until pilot users confirm Universal Links resolve end-to-end.

## Why

Three hidden-dir traps in a row:
1. **PR #240** — added the Amplify `custom_rule` rewrite, but the file was missing from the deploy bundle (next two PRs fixed that).
2. **PR #241** — added postbuild `cp -r public/.well-known out/.well-known` because Next.js' static export silently drops hidden dirs.
3. **PR #242** — added `include-hidden-files: true` to `actions/upload-artifact@v4` because the upload step otherwise tars without hidden dirs.

After all three: I verified on 2026-06-05 that the file IS in the deployed bundle (474 bytes, correct content) AND the rewrite IS deployed at position 7 of 8 in the live Amplify config. Yet curl still showed `HTTP/2 301 ... server: AmazonS3 ... location: /.well-known/apple-app-site-association/` with a fresh CloudFront miss.

**The undocumented trap:** when an Amplify `custom_rule` rewrites a hidden-source URL to a hidden-target URL with `trailingSlash: true`, S3 still applies its own trailing-slash redirect to the rewritten path BEFORE the file can be served. The rewrite IS firing — but it lands on a path that S3 then 301s. Confirmed by changing the target to a non-existent `/aurion-aasa-payload` mid-investigation: the response then showed `location: /aurion-aasa-payload/` (the new target's trailing-slash variant), proving the rewrite fires correctly but S3 wins.

Workaround: ship the payload at a non-hidden path. Amplify rewrites cleanly to it AND S3 doesn't 301 because a literal file exists there at the no-trailing-slash URL.

## Test plan

- [x] `web` vitest suite passes locally (`npm test -- --run tests/AasaFile.spec.ts` — 6/6 green, including the new byte-equality test).
- [x] `terraform validate` passes on `infrastructure/amplify.tf`.
- [x] `terraform plan -var-file=environments/dev.tfvars -target=aws_amplify_app.web_portal` produces a single in-place change (`custom_rule.target` only). Cosmetic header-block re-render is YAML normalization, no functional drift.
- [x] `terraform apply` succeeded on dev — live state confirms `target = "/aurion-aasa-payload"` (per autonomous-authority memory: dev apply is authorized).
- [ ] After this PR merges and the web workflow deploys: `curl -sI https://portal.aurionclinical.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association | head -5` returns `HTTP/2 200` with `content-type: application/json` (currently 301).
- [ ] After the deploy: `curl -s https://portal.aurionclinical.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association | jq .applinks.details[0].appIDs` returns `["2W2Z75Q5ZA.com.aurionclinical.physician"]`.
- [ ] iOS Universal Link from the password-reset email opens directly in the app (no Safari fallback).

## Security checklist

- [x] No PHI touched.
- [x] No production resources modified — `terraform apply` ran against `environments/dev.tfvars` only.
- [x] AASA payload content matches the existing file byte-for-byte (verified via `diff` and locked into CI via new test).
- [x] No secrets, no AppConfig changes, no schema migrations.
- [x] Hidden-path copy retained as fallback until pilot validates the new path.

## Out of scope

- Removing the `.well-known/` hidden-path copy. Deferred until pilot users confirm Universal Links resolve end-to-end on real devices.
- Removing the `postbuild: cp -r public/.well-known out/.well-known` hook from `web/package.json`. Stays in place to keep the fallback file in the bundle.
- Removing `include-hidden-files: true` from `.github/workflows/web.yml`. Same fallback rationale.
- Prod apply. Promoted via the standard deploy pipeline after dev verification.

author: zvibaratz
body:
## Why

Claude Code gates project-scoped skills/hooks/MCP servers behind a workspace-trust dialog keyed on `projects[<path>].hasTrustDialogAccepted` in `~/.claude.json`. The check walks **up** parent directories, and fresh worktree paths are never trusted — so every Atrium session boots into the dialog and loses project tooling until it's dismissed. There is **no sanctioned mechanism** to pre-accept trust (no CLI flag, env var, settings key, or `claude config` path — verified against current docs), which is why this was previously patched with a per-user launch-wrapper that hand-edited the JSON. This PR ports that shim into Atrium, done properly.

## What

- Opt-in `trust_worktrees_root` config toggle (**default off**), editable in the settings panel ("applies on restart").
- When enabled and any configured program/profile resolves to the claude adapter, `newHome` trusts the worktrees root **once at startup**, on the main thread, before any session starts. The trust target is the root — the parent-dir walk covers every worktree beneath it, so per-session writes (and one `~/.claude.json` entry per throwaway worktree) are avoided.
- `config.WorktreesDir()` becomes the single source of truth for `<config dir>/worktrees` (`session/git` now delegates), so the trusted root stays correct for both `~/.atrium` and legacy `~/.claude-squad` installs — and survives a future data-dir migration, which the old wrapper's hardcoded path would not.

## Safety properties

`~/.claude.json` is Claude's file, holds OAuth tokens, and is rewritten freely by live claude processes (which survive Atrium restarts), so the writer is deliberately conservative:

- missing / malformed / unexpectedly-shaped files are left untouched — and never created
- `map[string]any` + `json.Number` decoding preserves unknown fields and integers beyond float64 precision
- dotfile-manager symlinks are followed, never replaced by a regular file
- temp file born `0600`, matched to the original mode, atomic rename
- a stat re-check aborts the swap if a concurrent writer touched the file mid-rewrite (skipping self-heals at next startup; clobbering claude's state would not)
- already-trusted fast path performs no write; the whole feature is best-effort (warnings only — the fallback is just Claude's own dialog)

**Security framing**: workspace trust is an intentional Claude Code boundary. Enabling this means every repo you open with Atrium gets project-level trust — repo-supplied hooks/skills/MCP run without the per-project confirmation. That's the convenience being bought; default-off encodes the stance. `hasTrustDialogAccepted` is a Claude-internal key: if its schema ever changes, the dialog simply reappears and the existing gate detection holds queued prompts as before.

## Tests

Hermetic (sandboxed `HOME` everywhere — the suite must never touch a real `~/.claude.json`): trust set + unknown fields + sibling project + big-int fidelity + mode preservation; existing-entry sibling keys; already-trusted no-write (content+mtime pinned); missing file never created; malformed and four unexpected-shape variants left byte-identical; missing `projects` key created; symlink preserved with target updated; idempotent second call; app-level gate matrix (flag off / claude default / claude profile under non-claude default / no claude at all); settings-panel toggle; `WorktreesDir` new+legacy layouts. Race detector clean on `session/tmux` and `app`.

author: srest2021
body:
Adds `DatadogDCRView`, `DatadogOAuth2LoginView`, and `DatadogOAuth2CallbackView` in `src/sentry/identity/datadog/provider.py`.

Sentry's existing OAuth2 views don't support PKCE or DCR, which Datadog requires for MCP OAuth clients. These views extend the base OAuth2 pipeline with three Datadog-specific behaviors:

- **DCR (Dynamic Client Registration)**: Registers a new OAuth client with Datadog's MCP server before the login redirect, storing the resulting `client_id` / `client_secret` in pipeline state for subsequent views. Skips registration if credentials already exist (retry idempotency). Errors are handled with `record_event` lifecycle metrics, like the existing OAuth2 views.
- **PKCE**: The login view generates a code verifier, stores it in pipeline state, and sends the SHA-256 challenge in the authorize redirect. The callback view gets the code verifier from the pipeline and includes it in the token exchange.
- **`client_secret_basic` auth**: Datadog's MCP token endpoint rejects `client_secret_post` (credentials in POST body) and requires `client_secret_basic` (DCR credentials in `Authorization: Basic` header). The callback view overrides `get_token_params` to exclude credentials from the body and sends them via Basic auth instead.

This is the first PR in a series to add per-user OAuth for [Datadog's MCP server](https://app.notion.com/p/sentry/Infra-Telemetry-Integration-for-Seer-3738b10e4b5d80419163d6e37a9c87b5). Followup: https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull/117035

Reference: https://docs.datadoghq.com/extend/authorization/oauth2_in_datadog/

## What

The console error `Div for inline form "Inline Form Created 2022/07/09, 12:42:54 PM" is missing. Was inline code installed?` was firing on every page **except** `/news`.

Root cause: the Constant Contact widget script was loaded **globally** from `index.html`, but its target form div (`data-form-id="99081bd2…"`) only exists on the News page. On every other page the widget activates, can't find a div for the configured form, and logs the "missing" error. It first reached production with this morning's deploy (the static div + global script came from the May 23 `bd94ad0` "console log fixes" commit).

Fix: load the widget script from `SignUpForEmails` (the News component) so it only runs where its div lives. The real form still renders on `/news`, and the contact-the-office (Sandi Roop) fallback still covers browsers that block the script (Firefox ETP). Also removed the stray static `.ctct-inline-form` div from `index.html`.

## Verified (headless-browser console capture)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|

author: richardbowman
body:
## Root cause

`waitForAudioSilence()` was calling `createMediaStreamSource(audioEl.srcObject)` — tapping the **raw WebRTC remote stream** rather than the `<audio>` element's playback pipeline. The browser buffers incoming WebRTC audio before rendering it, so the stream could go silent (from the network's perspective) while the browser's audio renderer still had seconds of queued speech to play. This caused `onAudioDone` to fire too early, setting the UI to "silence" while the AI was still audibly speaking.

## Fix

Switch to `ctx.createMediaElementSource(this.audioEl)` so the `AnalyserNode` measures what the audio element's **decoder and renderer** is actually outputting to the speakers — not what's arriving on the wire. The element source node is cached on the instance (the Web Audio API only allows one `createMediaElementSource()` call per element per context) and connected through `ctx.destination` so audio continues to play while being analysed.

On loop completion or cancellation, only the per-response `AnalyserNode` is disconnected; the reused element source stays connected across responses.

## Also fixed

- Pre-existing test-only bug: `flushToolBatch` was called with `this.callbacks` (which is `null` when `connect()` is skipped in unit tests) instead of the `callbacks` argument already in scope from `handleEvent`. This caused 2 tool-batching unit tests to fail.

## Debug logging added (acceptance criterion 3)

Three `console.log` statements now bracket every playback cycle (always on, not gated by `debugLogging`):
- **Buffer receipt**: "audio buffer received from network — waiting for playback to finish"
- **Playback start**: "playback start detected (rms=X.XXXX)" — first tick where RMS exceeds the silence threshold
- **Playback end**: "playback end detected — audio silent for 600ms, transitioning to silence"

## Test plan
- [ ] All 34 unit tests pass (`npm test`)
- [ ] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [ ] In Obsidian DevTools console, verify the three log lines appear in correct order (buffer receipt → playback start → playback end) and that the UI transitions to "silence" only after the last log line
- [ ] Confirm user VAD (silence timer cancellation when speaking) is unaffected

author: udus122
body:
## 背景（真因）

カタログ作り直し後の再ビルドが、dlt の DuckLake ロード中に再現性高く失敗:

```
DatabaseTransientException: Failed to commit DuckLake transaction.
Exceeded the maximum retry count of 10 set by the ducklake_max_retry_count setting.
...
ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "ducklake_snapshot_pkey"
DETAIL: Key (snapshot_id)=(123) already exists.
```

これは DuckLake の**既知の並行/高レイテンシ起因のコミット競合**で、特に「**Postgres エンドポイントへのレイテンシが高いほど発生（localhost では出ない）**」と報告されている（[ducklake#233](https://github.com/duckdb/ducklake/issues/233), [#243](https://github.com/duckdb/ducklake/issues/243), [#459](https://github.com/duckdb/ducklake/issues/459)）。本リポは Neon (ap-southeast-1) へのリモート接続のため該当。**過去の "multiple snapshots" カタログ破損の真因もこれ**（旧テーブルは pkey 制約が無く重複が蓄積、作り直し後は pkey が重複を拒否して表面化）。

## 変更（dlt 設定での緩和）

`pipelines/__init__.py`:
- **`ducklake_max_retry_count = 100`**（既定10→100）を `DuckLakeCredentials.global_config` 経由で設定。`LOAD ducklake` 後に `SET GLOBAL` される。コミュニティ/公式が推奨する本エラーの直接的緩和策。
- **`LOAD__WORKERS=1`** で DuckLake への書き込みを単一ワーカーに直列化し、競合機会を削減。

## 検証

- ローカルで `create_pipeline()` 構築を確認: `ducklake_max_retry_count=100`, `LOAD__WORKERS=1`, `ducklake_name=e_stat` が適用される（実コミットは Neon 接続が要るため CI で検証）。

## マージ後の手順（こちらで実施）

1. Reset DuckLake（クリーンな baseline）
2. Sync 実行（フルロード）→ コミット競合が解消し dbt build まで通るか確認
3. 診断ワークフローで重複 snapshot が出ないことを確認

author: antoinetoussaint
body:
Closes #22.

## Summary

- Right-click-to-open only ever consulted a text scan for literal `http(s)://` tokens. Agents like Claude Code emit clickable links as **OSC 8 hyperlinks**, where the visible glyphs are a title rather than the URL — so detection found nothing, and because the agent is usually idle (mouse tracking off) the swallowed event never reached the PTY either. Net effect: the link was unopenable.
- `libghostty-vt` already parses OSC 8 and exposes `hyperlink_uri()`, but nothing in the TUI called it. We now resolve the clicked cell's hyperlink URI through the grid-ref API and pass it into `detect_target()` as a first-class, authoritative target ahead of the text-scan fallback. Detection runs before the mouse-tracking gate, so it now works regardless of tracking state.

## Test plan

- [x] `detect_target` unit tests: an OSC 8 URI wins over non-URL visible text and over a different visible URL.
- [x] Integration regression: feed a real OSC 8 hyperlink into a shell terminal, assert mouse tracking is off, and assert `target_at()` returns the hyperlink URL — covering the idle right-click path end to end through the real `libghostty-vt` parser.
- [x] `cargo test -p lazybox-tui` (477 passed), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

author: risingtides-dev
body:
Two Longhouse tickets, one branch. Builds on the `ocean-longhouse` crate and `POST /v1/longhouse/convene` already on main (OCEAN-9/36/46).

## OCEAN-58 — topics read endpoints
The council ran entirely in a background task and persisted nothing: `convene()` owned the only `QuorumEngine`, so a deck refresh wiped all topic state. Fixed with a daemon-owned read-side projection.

- New `ocean_longhouse::registry::LonghouseRegistry` — a pure, event-sourced `topic_id -> TopicSnapshot` store that folds each emitted `LonghouseEvent` into a durable snapshot (members, marks, tallies, leader, distance-to-quorum, deadline, firekeeper, decision, abort_reason, lifecycle `state`).
- The snapshot **survives `TopicClosed`** on purpose, so a refresh after the council ends still shows the final field.
- Daemon holds one registry in `AppState` (behind a `std::sync::Mutex`), tees every event the council emits into it from the `convene` emit closure (alongside the existing bus publish), and serves:
  - `GET /v1/longhouse/topics` — all topics, newest-deadline first.
  - `GET /v1/longhouse/topics/{id}` — one topic; 400 on a non-UUID id, 404 on unknown id (mirrors the `/v1/rooms/{id}` typed-error shape).
- Convergence is still decided **only** by the per-council `QuorumEngine`; the registry is a read-only mirror of what it already published.

## OCEAN-59 — claim_outcome quorum gate
The firekeeper could emit `Converged` with nothing checking the daemon's quorum state. Added the accountability brake.

- New `ocean_longhouse::convene::claim_outcome(engine, firekeeper, claimed, now_ms) -> Result<(), ClaimError>`: returns `Ok` only when the engine's own `evaluate()` reports `Converged` on the **same** proposal being ratified.
  - `ClaimError::NotConverged` — the premature-claim attack: engine is still `Pending`.
  - `ClaimError::WrongDecision { engine_decision, claimed }` — firekeeper tried to substitute a different proposal than the one the engine chose.
- The deadline/timeout path is covered for free: `force_resolve` latches `converged` before the firekeeper is bound, so a timeout-forced resolution reads back as `Converged` and the claim is accepted.
- Wired into `convene()`'s resolve path: if `claim_outcome` refuses, the topic **aborts** (`Split`) instead of emitting an unaccountable `Converged`.

author: basecradle-router-ai[bot]
body:
**Roadmap 5 of 11** — v0 `github` route. Closes #6.

## What
Implements `GithubRoute.normalize` — turns a verified GitHub `issues` webhook into the core `Event`, and ignores everything that isn't a handoff.

- **Gates**, in order: `X-GitHub-Event: issues` → action in `{opened, labeled}` → the `handoff` label. For `opened`, the issue must *carry* the label; for `labeled`, the **just-added** label must be `handoff` — so an unrelated label added to an already-handoff issue does **not** re-trigger a wake (a property the #8 per-repo lock shouldn't have to absorb).
- **Extracts** into `Event`: `target_repo` = `repository.full_name` (the repo the handoff issue is filed on — its captain is woken), `origin` = `IssueRef(number, html_url, title)`, `delivery_id` = `X-GitHub-Delivery`, and the documented `Cross-repo handoff: work <url>` trigger line.
- **Ignore vs error:** non-handoff webhooks (wrong event type, non-actionable action, no handoff label) normalize to `None`; only a structurally malformed `issues` payload raises `PayloadError`, with a field-naming message.

## Tests (offline, no network)
Fabricated `issues` payloads (cast: John Doe files a handoff for Nova Digital's repo agent): `opened`/`labeled` handoffs round-trip; non-handoff `opened`, unrelated `labeled`, non-`issues`, `ping`, and `closed` all ignore; malformed JSON, non-object body, missing `issue`/`repository`, non-int issue number, and missing delivery header all reject. 57 tests green; ruff clean.

## Scope
Per #6: normalize only. Agent resolution (#7) is out of scope.

author: copilot
body:
The "Fetch meal plan" job was failing because `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` was being JSON-encoded as a string (env vars are always strings), causing Telegram's API to return `400 Bad Request: chat not found`. Telegram expects numeric chat IDs as JSON integers.

## Change

Attempt to coerce `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` to `int` before JSON serialization, falling back to the raw string for username-style IDs (e.g. `@channelusername`):

```python
# Before
data = json.dumps({"chat_id": os.environ["TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID"], "text": text}).encode()

# After
chat_id_raw = os.environ["TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID"]
try:
    chat_id = int(chat_id_raw)
except ValueError:
    chat_id = chat_id_raw
data = json.dumps({"chat_id": chat_id, "text": text}).encode()
```

author: aibeshkov
body:
## What

Implements **ADR-028 Part E** — the one-time-password out-of-band artifact, the last open item from the credential-delivery ship. It's the third credential mode for admin-direct user creation, alongside an admin-set password and the setup link.

When an admin opts to set an initial credential themselves (rather than have the end user choose one via a setup link), the server **generates** a strong password, **shows it once** for the admin to relay out-of-band, and forces the account into `password_reset_required` (ADR-025) so the user must replace it on first login.

## Changes

- **core** — `CreateUserWithOneTimePassword`: creates the account directly in `password_reset_required` with the generated password in a single write (no second `UpdateUser` that, on failure, could strand an active account whose credential the admin already saw — same invariant as the setup-link path). Fires `credential.displayed_out_of_band` with `artifact=one_time_password` (Part F audit).
- **core** — `generateOneTimePassword`: `crypto/rand`, 20 chars, seeds one char of each required class then Fisher–Yates shuffles, so it always satisfies the default ADR-025 policy. Visually ambiguous chars (`0/O`, `1/l/I`) excluded so it survives hand-relay.
- **http** — `POST /api/v1/users` gains `generate_one_time_password`, mutually exclusive with `deliver_setup_link`/`password`; returns `{user, one_time_password}`.
- **cli** — `keyorix user create --one-time-password` + `common.PrintOneTimePasswordResult`.
- **tests** — producer (account state, audit event, OTP authenticates against the persisted bcrypt hash) and generator (policy-compliant + unique across 50 draws).

## Security notes

- The password is **never emailed** and **never persisted in clear** — only its bcrypt hash. It's returned to the admin exactly once, in the API/CLI response.
- The out-of-band display is audited (`credential.displayed_out_of_band`), the one path ADR-028 singles out for compliance because a human briefly sees a credential.
- `password_reset_required` means the ADR-025 restricted-session gate 403s every endpoint until the user changes it — the OTP is good for first login only.

## Scope

Backend only (keyorix repo), mirroring how setup-link backend (#23) and frontend (#11) were split. A frontend toggle for the OTP mode is a separate keyorix-web follow-up. Resend stays link-only (OTP is a create-time artifact).

`go build/vet/gofmt/test ./...` green.

author: aibeshkov
body:
## What & why

A targeted test-coverage push over the parsing core and the diagnostic brain — the parts whose correctness *is* the product — plus two real bug fixes surfaced by the new tests. Motivated by the recent parser-hardening wave (BUG-024..035): the fragile surfaces had almost no regression net.

All tests are characterization tests (string/struct in → value/`[]Insight` out): no external commands, network, or real `/proc` access. The few filesystem touches use `t.TempDir()`.

## Coverage gains (measured)

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/analysis` (heuristics brain) | 37.3% | **43.9%** |
| `internal/render` | 5.6% | **12.9%** |
| `internal/collectors` | partial | **+5 collectors** with parser tests |

## Bug fixes (2)

1. **Kernel OOM-kills were classified WARN, not CRIT.** `parseDmesgLine`'s CRIT keyword list matched the literal token `oom`, but the kernel OOM killer header is `Out of memory: Killed process …` — no such token. Added `out of memory` to the keywords. A host getting OOM-killed should never read as a yellow WARN in the incident timeline.
2. **`extractKernelSubsystem` kept a trailing colon** for lowercase subsystems (`audit:` instead of `audit`). Stripped in the fallback.

Both were found by the new timeline tests; the pinned cases now assert the corrected behavior as regression guards.

## Refactor (1)

- `lastPart` (SELinux context type extraction): collapsed two redundant identical branches and fixed a doc comment that didn't match the code. Behavior-preserving, guarded by `TestLastPart`.

## Tests added

**Collectors (parsers):**
- `security_linux.go` — SELinux AVC (`avcField`/`avcPerms`/`lastPart`), AppArmor (`extractAAField`), CIS-extended sshd fields, port helpers, firewall decision, `parseLogTimestamp`. Scoped to the surface not already covered by `ssh_config_linux_test.go` / `firewall_ssh_test.go`.
- `timeline_linux.go` — journal/dmesg/sar parsers, dedup, noise filter.
- `nfs_linux.go` — `nfsParseSource` (incl. IPv6), `nfsAuditOptions`.
- `bind_linux.go` — `bindParseZoneFile` (temp `named.conf`: zones, comments, includes, hint/forward skip), error extraction, uptime.
- `k8s.go` — `updatePodCounts`, `k8sTruncate`.

**Heuristics (WARN/CRIT thresholds):**
- Security + storage: SSH hardening (root login CRIT, PVE/offensive downgrade, with a guard that a plain host stays CRIT), empty/stale passwords, world-writable, weak ciphers; ZFS pool state/capacity/frag/errors/scrub; mdadm RAID states.
- Container + drives: `checkK8s` (nodes/pods/pressure), `checkDockerContainers`, `checkDockerSecurity` (docker.sock CRIT), `checkNVMe` (NVMe + SATA SMART).
- Memory/swap/PSI: RAM warn/crit, overcommit, slab WARN **incl. the in-container suppression** (a deliberate false-positive fix); swap usage + paging; PSI memory/io/cpu stalls.

**Render:**
- Guards the `inline*(interface{})` renderers against silent type-assertion failures (nil → `""`, wrong-type → `""`, valid value *and* pointer form → non-empty) for a representative set.

## Verification

`gofmt` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -race -count=1 ./...` green across the whole repo (run on `golang:1.26` Linux, matching CI's ubuntu runners; platform-neutral packages also verified natively on macOS).

author: migmartri
body:
Resolving the CAS mapping for a digest could exhaust the request deadline and surface as a context deadline error on artifact download. Two problems compounded, both fixed here.

1. `FindByDigest` resolved each mapping's public visibility with two queries per mapping, producing `1 + 2N` sequential round-trips. Visibility for all referenced workflow runs is now resolved in a single edge-loaded query.

2. The download path fetched every mapping for a digest globally and filtered by org in memory. Because the same artifact can be pushed across thousands of workflow runs, a single digest accumulates thousands of mappings, yet only one is needed to locate the CAS backend. The org-scoped path now selects a single mapping directly in the database (organization + project RBAC predicates, preferring the default backend, `LIMIT 1`), so its cost no longer grows with the number of mappings. The public mapping lookup remains a fallback, used only when the requester has no org-level access to the digest.

Closes #3167

author: justsomehack
body:
## Summary

The pure-Go JPEG 2000 codec now covers what we need — it decodes classic (EBCOT)
and High-Throughput (HTJ2K) streams (lossless and lossy) and encodes lossless
5/3 — so the optional `openjpeg` cgo backend is retired.

io-dicom's **default build was already pure-Go** (`openjpeg` was opt-in via
`-tags openjpeg`), so default/production behavior is unchanged. This removes the
opt-in path and its build dependency.

## Changes

- Delete `native_backends_openjpeg_cgo.go` (+ test) and the openjpeg build-tag
  stubs. `native_backends.go` is now the sole, unconditional registration (no-op);
  `CGOEnabled` is always `false`.
- Convert the openjpeg cross-validation decode goldens to **frozen `.raw`
  references** (generated from the now-validated pure-Go decoder), so the decode
  regression suite needs no native reference. Drop the encode-vs-openjpeg golden
  (self round-trip already covers it).
- Repoint the sample/cget/matrix tests at the pure-Go backend; drop the
  `openjpeg` build tag from the media/transcoder native-roundtrip tests.
- Drop `openjpeg` from the Makefile/script tag lists, `test_codec_tags.sh`, and
  the codec-deps source build. Update README/cmd docs.

## Validation & scope

The pure-Go decoder was validated byte-exact against OpenJPEG in prior PRs (see
git history); ongoing validation is via self round-trip + frozen goldens.
Out-of-scope codestreams (multi-tile, custom precincts, MCT, non-LRCP) and lossy
encode are not covered and return `errJ2KUnsupported`.

## Coordinated change

This is part of a coordinated removal. io-scp and io-dicom-tools build io-dicom
with `-tags openjpeg`; that tag is now a harmless no-op (no compile break), but
those repos get separate changes to drop it from their tag lists and codec-deps
builds.

author: bramvanoost
body:
## Summary

- New Xcode iOS app target at `ios/CHING/` consuming the local `CHINGEngine` Swift Package.
- `GameStore` (`@Observable`) wraps engine `State` + `Mulberry32` RNG, dispatches actions, auto-drives AI turns. 5 XCTest unit tests, all green.
- Single-screen `GameView` renders all six game zones (title, phase, turn, scores, center tiles, vaults, dice, pick buttons, roll/bank, game-over alert) in default SwiftUI styling.
- Hardcoded 1v1 vs Jones (discipline 0.30) on every new game. End-of-game alert presents winner + scores with a New Game button.
- App builds clean and launches on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator. Proof-of-life screenshot at `docs/superpowers/2026-06-05-phase-2-screenshot.png`.

## Verification done

- Engine `swift test`: 32/32 pass (unchanged).
- `xcodebuild test ... -only-testing:CHINGTests`: 5/5 `GameStoreTests` pass.
- Clean DerivedData rebuild succeeds.
- App launches on simulator; initial state renders correctly (verified via screenshot).

## Verification still TODO before merge

- [ ] Manual end-to-end playthrough on the simulator: tap Roll → Pick → Bank repeatedly, confirm AI takes its turns automatically after each human action, confirm both vaults accumulate tiles, confirm center tiles deplete, confirm the Game Over alert appears, confirm New Game resets the board.

## Notable deviations from the plan

- Bundle id is `com.fastronaut.CHING` (not `com.bramvanoost.CHING`).
- Simulator target is `iPhone 17 Pro` (the plan's `iPhone 16 Pro` doesn't exist in Xcode 26.5).
- `@SwiftUI.State` qualifier needed on the GameView store property because `CHINGEngine.State` and `SwiftUI.State` collide. Plan didn't anticipate this, one-line fix.
- Added `ios/CHING/.gitignore` for Xcode `xcuserdata/` noise (small unplanned addition, prevents per-session diff churn).
- The proof-of-life screenshot is the initial state, not mid-game. `simctl` has no CLI tap, so driving the app to a mid-game state from the command line wasn't worth doing for the screenshot.

## Out of scope (deferred to Phase 3+)

- 1-bit dither visual system
- Display serif typography
- All non-Game screens (Splash, Home, Receipt, Settings, Onboarding)
- Multiple AI characters / character selection
- Settings persistence
- App icon, splash, App Store screenshots
- Sound or haptics

body:
## Summary

Two new charts on both `/games/:id` and `/admin/games/:id`, appearing after the existing three charts.

**Luck Ratio Over Time** — cumulative `(defender_losses − attacker_losses)` per attacker per attack event. Positive = the player is getting lucky (killing more than they lose); negative = unlucky. Can and does go below zero. Tooltip shows who was attacked on each dot.

**Attacks Received Over Time** — cumulative attacker dice directed at each *defender* per attack event. Used as a proxy for attacking pressure received — more dice = larger attacking force. Tooltip shows who attacked on each dot.

Both use `Stats.luck_ratio_series/1` and `Stats.attacks_received_series/1` respectively, returning the same enriched point shape as all other series.

## Note on "attacks received" proxy
The log records `attacker_dice` (e.g. `"6,3,2"`) but not the raw attacking force size. Dice count is the best available proxy — it captures relative pressure even if it's capped at 3 per exchange.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a finished game with log events — all five charts render
- [ ] Luck ratio chart crosses zero for unlucky attackers
- [ ] Hovering a dot on either chart shows "player attacked defender"
- [ ] Drag to zoom / double-click to reset works independently on each chart

author: automatedempires
body:
## Summary
Rewires `/listing/[id]` from fixtures to live Supabase data and adds the seeker **Apply** flow (server action + DB queries + UI states).

Refs: #105 (Claude Code session briefing — Agent A).

@claude — please review.

### What changed
- **`apps/web/app/listing/[id]/page.tsx`** — removed `generateStaticParams` and the fixture import; added `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`; calls `getPublicListingById(id)` and `notFound()` when null. Reads per-seeker applied state via `getSeekerApplicationIds` when a Clerk session is present.
- **`packages/db/src/queries/applications.ts`** (new) — `applyToListing(clerkToken, listingId, coverMessage?)` and `getSeekerApplicationIds(clerkToken)`. Looks up `seeker_profiles.id` by `clerk_user_id = <jwt sub>`, inserts into `applications`, maps unique-violation → `already_applied`, missing profile → `profile_not_found`.
- **`packages/db/src/index.ts`** — re-exports the new queries module.
- **`apps/web/app/actions/applications.ts`** (new, `"use server"`) — `applyToListingAction` (Clerk `auth()` → `getToken({ template: "supabase" })` → `applyToListing` → `revalidatePath('/listing/[id]')`) and `getSeekerApplicationIdsAction`.
- **`apps/web/components/listing/ApplyForm.tsx`** (new, client) — textarea + submit; renders **Sign in to apply** (unauth), **Applied** (already applied / success), or an error message (`profile_not_found` → "Complete your profile first").
- **`apps/web/components/listing/ListingDetail.tsx`** — accepts `isAuthenticated`/`alreadyApplied`, renders `<ApplyForm>` in place of the static CTA.
- **`apps/web/components/listing/toDetailData.ts`** (new) — `ListingRow → ListingDetailData` mapper.

## Reconciliations vs the task briefing (the repo differs from the spec)
I followed what the code actually does (per AGENTS.md §9), not the briefing's description:

1. **`getPublicListingById` returns `ListingRow | null`, not `DiscoveryListing | null`.** `<ListingDetail>` consumes the richer `ListingDetailData`. I added `listingRowToDetailData()` (reusing the shared `rowToDiscoveryFields()` for title/category/location/window/benefits/host-name/verified) rather than passing a raw row.
2. **`seeker_profiles.clerk_user_id` is NOT in the committed `packages/db/src/types.gen.ts`** (the generated types predate migration 009). A fully-typed `.eq("clerk_user_id", …)` will not compile, so that single lookup reads the column through an untyped view of the same authed client, with a `TODO` to regenerate types (needs DB access). The `applications` insert/select still use the fully-typed client.
3. **`applyToListing` is a leaf-package function and cannot call Clerk `auth()`.** It decodes the `sub` claim from the JWT (no signature verification — authenticity is enforced by Clerk when minting the token and by PostgREST on send) to apply the `WHERE clerk_user_id = $sub` guard. Clerk auth itself is enforced in the server action.

## Known gaps (intentionally out of scope — follow-ups)
The public listing projection in `packages/db/src/queries/listings.ts` (`LISTING_COLUMNS`) does not select these, so the mapper leaves them empty rather than expanding a shared query owned elsewhere:
- `description` → `[]` (no body paragraphs render)
- `gallery` → `[]` (ImageGallery renders nothing)
- `host.id` → `""` (host permalink not yet wired; left blank rather than linking a wrong id)

Extending `LISTING_COLUMNS` to project description/media/host id is the recommended follow-up.

## No new dependencies
No packages added. Uses already-installed `@clerk/nextjs`, `@supabase/supabase-js`, `next`, `react`. No `pnpm install` was run.

## ⚠️ Verification not run locally
The sandbox has **no network/DNS**, so `pnpm install`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm build` were **NOT** run. I have not regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`. The code is written to compile against the current `main` types, but **CI must be the source of truth** for lint/typecheck/build. I have not claimed any green checks.

## Acceptance criteria mapping
- `/listing/[id]` loads a real listing (not fixture) — ✅ `getPublicListingById` + `notFound()` + `force-dynamic`.
- Authed seeker can apply (row inserted) — ✅ `applyToListingAction` → `applyToListing` insert.
- Unauthenticated user sees graceful fallback — ✅ "Sign in to apply".
- Already-applied seeker sees "Applied" — ✅ `getSeekerApplicationIds` → `alreadyApplied`.
- Build passes with no new TS errors — ⏳ must be confirmed by CI (see warning above).

author: jakechampion
body:
Companion to the method-arity slice — type-checks method arguments.

## What

When a method call's arity matches, each argument is type-checked against
the resolved user-defined method's `param_types`; a mismatch is E038,
reported at the argument (Go's `arg.Pos()`) with the message
`argument N to "m": expected X, got Y`.

```
struct P { x: i32 }
function (p: P) add(a: i32): i32 { return p.x + a; }
function main(): i32 { var p: P = P { x: 1 }; var s: string = "n"; return p.add(s); }
```
→ `3:81: error[E038]` from both checkers (code + position).

## Restricted to primitives — and why

An unrestricted version false-positived all over the bundle: the
self-host's `type_assignable` can't faithfully compare struct / union /
qualified types the way Go's `assignable` does. Restricting to primitive
param-vs-arg pairs (i32 / bool / string / f64) — the same guard as the
E034 array-element check — keeps it sound while still catching the
unambiguous mismatch. Verified **zero** method-E038 across all thirteen
self-host modules.

A limitation is recorded in the port doc: full non-primitive method-arg
parity needs a stronger `type_assignable` (struct/union/qualified
comparison), the same type-model gap that blocks exhaustiveness (E030)
and several other Go codes.

## Fixpoint-safe

Checker-only — no AST change.

## Tests

- New corpus cases (`method-arg-type-mismatch`, `method-arg-type-ok`).
- New `check-position-method-argtype` CLI subtest.
- x86 fixpoint, checker-codes, CLI, and wasm-run suites all pass locally.

El rol hereda **todos** los permisos de `MEDICO` y suma: `patient:create`, `patient:change-status`, `route:assign-clinical-team` (+ `route:read`).

## Frontend

author: ml404
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the `/cube` ktor migration (#627). The same blocking-IO anti-pattern lived in `/meme`: it created a synchronous Apache `HttpClients.createDefault()` (**no timeout**) and called `httpClient.execute()` directly in `handle()`, which runs inside the listener's `launch { … }` on the CPU-bound `Dispatchers.Default`. A slow/unresponsive Reddit could tie up a Default-pool thread indefinitely. `MemeButton` (the re-roll) had the same issue.

## What changed

- **New `RedditMemeFetcher`** — a `suspend` fetch on `Dispatchers.IO` via the shared ktor `HttpClient`, with a 10s per-request timeout, mirroring `ScryfallCubeFetcher`. Returns parsed post data (`Success`) or a friendly `Error` (non-200, empty listing, NSFW, video, transport failure).
- **`MemeCommand`** parses the options on the calling thread, then launches the fetch on an injected `CoroutineDispatcher` (`fetchAsync`), mirroring the `/dnd` query handler. An unexpected throw resolves the message with an error embed.
- **`MemeButton`** re-rolls via `memeCommand.fetchAsync(...)` instead of constructing its own blocking Apache client (drops the `org.apache.http` dependency from the button).

## Tests

- New `RedditMemeFetcherTest` on a ktor `MockEngine` (success, non-200, empty listing, NSFW/video skips, transport failure, URL shape).
- `MemeCommandTest` now mocks the fetcher and drives the launched coroutine via `Dispatchers.Unconfined` (success → result embed + re-roll row; error → error embed, no row; no-permission → no fetch).
- `MemeButtonTest` verifies `fetchAsync` is/ isn't invoked.
- `:discord-bot:test` and `:discord-bot:koverVerify` pass. The `HttpClient` test-context bean added in #627 covers the new `RedditMemeFetcher` wiring.

Part of a series closing out the remaining blocking-IO gaps (intro attachment download and the lavaplayer gateway are separate PRs).

author: rohandasguptauw
body:
Noise analyzer: shot-noise Poisson correlation is reliably destroyed by JPEG compression and any image processing, causing 57-86% false-positive AI scores on real phone photos. Shot-noise now only contributes to the score (25%) when over-smoothness independently agrees (> 0.6). Otherwise the score is driven entirely by over-smoothness. The "no camera sensor signature" indicator is similarly gated. Confidence is now derived only from over-smoothness, capped at 0.80, to avoid spurious high-confidence false positives from the correlation signal alone.

Ensemble: swap noise (0.150→0.075) and spectral (0.075→0.150) weights. Without ML the effective split becomes noise=15%, spectral=30% — spectral FFT checkerboard detection is more reliable than shot-noise analysis on processed images.

author: licmtuchmann
body:
## Por qué este PR

PR #3 perdió el campo `history` de los 26 artículos del CNPP que llevaban el diff de "redacción anterior vs vigente". El script semanal `cnpp.mjs` solo descargaba la versión vigente actual de diputados.gob.mx y re-parseaba contra esa sola, borrando las 4 versiones históricas (DOF 2016-06-17, 2021-02-19, 2024-01-26, 2024-12-16) que originalmente integramos desde los `.doc` oficiales.

## Solución estructural

**Set histórico permanente en el repo:**
- `scripts/build/sources/cnpp/primary/` — 5 versiones convertidas con `catdoc`
- `scripts/build/sources/cnpp/fallback/` — mismas 5 convertidas con `antiword` (se usan para parchar artículos donde `catdoc` pierde texto; caso conocido: art. 265 en la versión 2025-11-28)

**`scripts/ingest/cnpp.mjs` reescrito** para:

1. Descargar el `.doc` vigente desde diputados.gob.mx
2. Convertirlo con `catdoc` + `antiword`
3. Detectar la fecha "Última reforma DOF" del documento descargado
4. Si esa fecha ya existe en el set histórico → no toca el repo, solo regenera el JSON desde el set conocido
5. Si es **nueva** → la **AGREGA al set histórico permanente** (`primary/` y `fallback/`) con nombre `cnpp_<DOF>.txt`
6. Re-corre el parser contra **todas** las versiones disponibles para preservar el campo `history` por artículo

## Verificación

```
CNPP: 490 artículos, 0 derogados, DOF 2025-11-28
versions_processed: ['2016-06-17','2021-02-19','2024-01-26','2024-12-16','2025-11-28']
articles with history: 26
Art 113 (Derechos del Imputado) — redacción anterior recuperada al DOF 2021-02-19
OK — dataset íntegro.
```

## Costo

~4.8 MB de `.txt` en el repo (texto plano, comprime muy bien en git). A cambio se garantiza que el feature "ver redacción anterior" sobreviva todas las corridas semanales futuras y que cada nueva reforma que el viernes la SCJN/DOF integre quede acumulada en el set histórico permanente.

## Lo que NO toca este PR (pendiente separado)

- Trigger `push` temporal de `weekly-update.yml` (lo dejé puesto para forzar el registro inicial; lo quito en otro PR pequeño cuando termines de mergear este).
- Optimización del bundle: `compendios.json` pesa 11 MB después de la ingesta. Para reducir el precache, conviene servirlo lazy. Otro PR.
